author: Monthly Review Press
title: In Chicago NOW? See August Nimtz speak on “‘Black Marxism’: A Marxist Critique”
content:
APPEARANCES


In Chicago on November 18th? Join August for a talk at the University of Chicago

Center for Contemporary Theory


In conjunction with

3CT’s Marx + Theory reading group

, led by Anton Ford and Gabriel Winant, August Nimtz will speak for himself as a contemporary of Cedric Robinson’s, as he grounds

Black Marxism: A Marxist Critique

 in an account of his own upbringing in New Orleans and his development throughout the struggles of the 1960s–explaining how and why he came to radically different conclusions.


REGISTER HERE.

This event is free and open to the public, and registration is recommended. Please email 

ccct@uchicago.edu

 if you require any accommodations to enable your full participation.


INTERVIEWS


Coming from Left Field

: “Black Marxism, Class Politics, and the Questions We Cannot Avoid” (Episode 153)


This conversation ranges from the Grenadian Revolution and anti-colonial struggles in Africa to Malcolm X, Black nationalism, identity politics, and the enduring question of whether the left can build an independent political alternative to the Democratic Party. Nimtz also reflects on Lenin’s approach to elections, the meaning of revolutionary parliamentarianism, and why he sees troubling parallels between today’s global conflicts and the period leading up to World War I. This is a wide-ranging, challenging conversation about race, class, imperialism, and the political choices facing the left today….


Opera Mundi and Autonomia Literária

 (Brazil)


Nimtz took a three-week book tour in Brazil, from July 20 to August 8, 2026.  These visits were mainly to promote a Brazilian collection of some of 

his essays

, two of which are from 

Black Marxism

, now being translated for a Brazilian edition. The tour began with three presentations to the Historical Materialism Conference, Rio de Janeiro 2026.  That was followed by seven other presentations in Paraty, Guararema, and São Paulo – to about 600 in person audiences, including the leading Left/Progressive bookfair, 

FLIPEI

.  Two in-depth interviews; 

TUTAMÉIA TV

and 

Opera Mund

i.  (See below for a video from one of these events.)


iMWiL!

, with Jared Ball


“What Cedric Robinson’s

Black Marxism

 Gets Wrong”

, an interview with August Nimtz, by Constantin Berlin (originally published on

Jacobin-Germany

)


“Cedric Robinson’s

Black Marxism: The Making of the Black Radical Tradition

did not receive widespread attention after its original publication in 1983. Since 2000, when it was republished with a new preface and an introduction by historian Robin D. G. Kelley, however, the book has enjoyed widespread appeal and influence in the anglophone humanities and social sciences as well as among activists. Robinson’s proposed theory of “racial capitalism” and his framework of a “black radical tradition” have shaped debates about racial inequalities in capitalist societies and Marxism’s potential for anti-racist politics in recent decades. August Nimtz has engaged with the book’s arguments and trajectory, directly or indirectly, since its original publication. The recently published

collection

,

Black Marxism: A Marxist Critique

, makes accessible, for the first time, a critique that spans four decades….”


REVIEWS


Cosmonaut

: ““Black Marxism” Under Debate, 40 Years On” by Gary Levi


“Cedric Robinson’s 1983

Black Marxism

 is a work that has had a second, and even third life. First revived in academic circles by the proselytizing of his acolyte, acclaimed historian Robin D.G. Kelly, the book was again revived in popular circles by the waves of Black Lives Matters protests that sought in it (along with works of prison abolitionists) a theoretical and historical narrative to broaden the immediate convulsive moment of protest towards a vision of how society might change, and under the impact of what form of mobilization. In this sense, it played a role in BLM protests similar to Graeber’s

Debt

 during Occupy. One couldn’t find a prescription of how to protest in it, nor could one find among most protesters a familiarity with its core ideas, but nonetheless those set into motion found themselves drawn to it, and searching for guidance in its pages….For August Nimtz, at the time a former nationalist and pan-Africanist who had moved towards the interracialism and Trotskyism of the Socialist Workers Party, the answer was straightforward. His 1985 review in

Journal of African Marxists

author: Joe Mullin
title: The Justice Department Wants To Give Patent Trolls More Power
content:
Software patents are mostly vague, hard to define, and widely abused. Most tech patent lawsuits aren’t filed by companies that make real products. They’re filed by patent trolls, companies that acquire patents to extract payments through litigation and legal threats.

A patent on one feature of a smartphone shouldn’t give the patent owner the power to threaten the existence of the entire product line. But that is exactly the leverage patent trolls want—and the current administration is helping them to get it.

In two recent patent cases, Radian Memory Systems v. Samsung and Collision Communications v. Samsung, the Justice Department and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office have asked courts to make it easier for patent owners to get injunctions. These are judicial orders that can force companies to stop selling products or remove features from them, rather than simply pay monetary damages.

The threat of an injunction can pressure a company to pay far more than what a patent is actually worth. In 2006, NTP Inc., a patent holding company with no products of its own, was able to pressure BlackBerry manufacturer Research in Motion Ltd. to pay a $612 million settlement when it was on the verge of an injunction.

In May 2006, the Supreme Court rejected the practice of granting permanent injunctions almost automatically after a finding of patent infringement. In eBay v. MercExchange, the high court held that patent owners must satisfy the same tough requirements that plaintiffs in non-patent cases must meet to get a permanent injunction. After eBay, patent owners had to show “irreparable harm,” that they can’t be adequately compensated by money, that the “balance of hardships” favors the plaintiff, and, critically, that an injunction would not harm the “public interest.”

At EFF, we celebrated eBay v. MercExchange as a major win for internet users. More than twenty years ago, we saw that software patents were going to be a disaster—not just for small companies (which they are), but for freedom of expression online. As EFF explained in its brief:

The United States Patent and Trademark Office has issued patents on methods fordownloading video programs, publishing web pages, sending email messages, making internet telephone calls, and even online fundraising methods. Injunctions against uses of these technologies—and many similar technologies—will inevitably affect, and may even chill, free expression on the internet.

The eBay rules make sense because the monopolies provided by patents are only justified when they serve a public purpose: promoting scientific and technological progress. Enforcing patents is not supposed to come at the cost of later innovators, free expression, or people’s access to technology.

Now, two decades after eBay, the government is urging courts to interpret those protections in ways that could give patent owners greater leverage. It’s unusual for the government to intervene in private patent disputes, but the current administration has done so repeatedly—and not on the side of the public.

In June 2025, the Justice Department and Patent Office filed a “statement of interest” in Radian Memory Systems v. Samsung, a dispute over patents involving solid-state drives (SSDs), the storage devices commonly used in modern computers. Radian, a patent assertion company tied to Fortress Investment Group, sought a preliminary injunction that would block sales of Samsung’s products even before a judge or jury had decided whether there was patent infringement.

In its statement, the government argued that even a patent owner whose business depends entirely on patent licensing could suffer irreparable harm, because calculating how much money it should get might be difficult. “In cases of unique assets, courts have commonly found irreparable harm when damages are difficult to calculate,” the DOJ writes in its brief.

But courts regularly resolve disagreements about patent royalty rates, a patent’s contribution, and comparable licenses. The fact that those disagreements exist does not, by itself, establish that monetary damages wouldn’t be enough to compensate the patent owner. If courts adopted the DOJ’s views here, a difficult but ordinary part of patent litigation could become a reason for finding irreparable harm, making it easier for patent owners to seek injunctions that threaten entire product lines. Pure patent-licensing businesses would love that—they would routinely start to ask for injunctions, since …

author: labor4pal
title: AFT-MI Stand In Solidarity With Your Members (Graduate Employees’ Organization, AFT 3550)
content:
At the University of Michigan Faculty Senate’s November 9, 2026 meeting, AFT-MI Secretary-Treasurer Kirsten Herold publicly opposed a faculty-sponsored motion calling on the University of Michigan to bargain in good faith with the Graduate Employees’ Organization AFT Local 3550, which represents 4,000 graduate workers at the University. Herold questioned GEO’s good faith in negotiations, made inaccurate statements about the union’s bargaining process—including incorrectly claiming that GEO had begun negotiations without written proposals and has no bargaining team—and publicly criticized the union’s bargaining priorities while faculty attempted to express solidarity. Herold explicitly leveraged her position within AFT-MI to give credence to her criticisms.

It is inappropriate and deeply damaging for a high-ranking member of our parent union to use their power to disparage a member union.

Send an email to AFT-MI President Terrence Martin and the AFT-MI Administrative Board (elected officers from AFT-MI locals) calling for AFT-MI leadership to formally censure Secretary-Treasurer Kirsten Herold for her damaging actions, inform AFT-MI members of that censure, and publicly reaffirm their solidarity with GEO 3550 in this challenging contract cycle.

author: Unknown
title: World of Hurt: Abolitionist Reflections on the Root Causes of Harm
content:
What causes people to harm others? Reactionaries label certain individuals—or, worse, entire demographics—inherently harmful to justify their own efforts to inflict harm via vigilante attacks, policing, and the court system. Others suggest that experiencing harm can lead some to harm others, as suggested by the common catchphrase “Hurt people hurt people.” Here, we examine this popular notion and propose a more useful framework for understanding the root causes of harm.


Today, a ruling class headed by billionaires and aspiring autocrats is making

the celebration of violence

 central to their narratives and policies, openly campaigning against empathy itself. In this context, the question of what causes harm—and how to interrupt it without reinforcing cycles of hurt and oppression—has become increasingly urgent.


World of Hurt


Abolitionists

 who envision a world without

police

 or

prisons

 often face questions about how to address serious forms of interpersonal harm.

Mutual aid

 and resource redistribution may reduce behaviors that arise as a consequence of lack of access to basic needs. But how can we understand those who seem to hurt others out of cruelty or disregard? If we don’t accept the idea that some people are monsters who must be locked up to keep the rest of us safe, how can we make sense of their actions?


Defenders of the criminal legal system frequently cite rape and abuse to justify prisons and imprisonment. In response, abolitionists have devoted considerable energy to developing

alternative approaches

 to addressing sexual violence. Groups such as Generation Five have proposed

principles for responding to child sexual abuse

 through transformative justice frameworks. By focusing on one of the most stigmatized forms of harm, they aim to cut to the root of

carceral thinking

 in order to reimagine safety and justice.


But creative responses beyond the state are not enough. To end sexual violence, we also need to understand its root causes.


Feminist activists coined the term “

rape culture

” to describe how social norms and institutions enable sexual harm. In addition to these structural effects of gender and power, others argue that past experiences of harm shape the behavior of individuals who go on to harm others. One of the most common ways to articulate this principle appears in the phrase “

Hurt people hurt people

.”


Let’s take a closer look to see where this popular saying came from, how it is used, and its implications for an abolitionist understanding of harm.


The Trajectory of a Slogan


From

self-help books

 and

therapist blogs

 to the

writings of abolitionist activists

, “hurt people hurt people” has become an influential account of the psychology of violence. It suggests that some people harm others not because they are pathological monsters, but because they too are victims whose unresolved trauma shapes their hurtful actions.


The precise origins of the phrase are opaque, but it has been in circulation

at least since the 1950s

. It seems to have begun trending in the 1990s in therapeutic and pop psychology circles. A popular 1993 Christian self-help book titled

Hurt People Hurt People

 promised to support readers in healing from painful past relationships “with empathy and biblical insight.” In recent years, this phrase has been repeated by everyone from megachurch pastor Rick Warren to Hollywood actor Andrew Garfield to the stripper con artist character Destiny in the movie

Hustlers

 to

the metal band Mudvayne

. It appears most widely in discourse about therapy, self-help, trauma, and religion.


On the surface, “hurt people hurt people” might seem an odd slogan for radical critics of the

prison industrial complex

. As a maxim of folk wisdom that spans mainstream, religious, feminist, and radical circles, we should consider carefully whether it aligns with our values.


In some ways, it makes sense that abolitionists would find this formulation promising. It humanizes people who cause harm, whereas dehumanizing them paves the way for carceral responses. It attributes the roots of harmful behavior not to inherent depravity, but to contingent circumstances that can be changed. It resonates with the lived experiences of some people who are struggling to heal and to be accountable for hurting others. It seems to offer a hopeful pathway towards a world without sexual violence by intervening in support of those who have been harmed in order to …

author: Labor Notes Staff
title: Stewards Corner: Laying the Foundation for Change in Your Union
content:
Revitalizing a local union may require electing new officers with a different vision. But running for office should not be your first step.


Successful campaigns for union office usually start by organizing against management first, often years in advance of any eventual run.


A group of workers wants to accomplish something—better pay, more control over their conditions on the job, an end to tiered wages or benefits—but their officials, or something about the way their union operates, is in the way. So they begin to change the culture of the union, getting more members involved in building power on the shop floor.


Your ultimate goal, after all, is not just electing new leaders, but building a stronger union. And doing that means involving as many members as possible.


WHERE TO START


The good news is you can begin organizing for change in your union any time.


“Your campaign should start with workplace fights that involve your co-workers,” says John Pearson, a nurse at Highland Hospital in Oakland, California, and former president of the SEIU Local 1021 chapter there. “You need that type of credibility and trust from people to be able to lead successfully.”


Before running for office, Pearson helped lead a campaign to defend breaks, involving nurses throughout the Alameda County hospital system, which resulted in a big back pay settlement. He also led an effort to save a substance abuse clinic from defunding.


“The word spreads if you’re effective at fighting in the workplace—people know to ask you for help,” says Pearson.


This type of organizing shows members that you have a track record, and that collectively members can make a difference.


The Caucus of Rank-and-File Educators (CORE), which won leadership in the Chicago Teachers Union in 2010, built up strength in campaigns like a fight to stop the school district from closing dozens of neighborhood schools and replacing them with privately run charters.


“So much of our caucus was really forged in the fight against school closings,” says Norine Gutekanst, who was a third-grade teacher at the time. Caucus members attended school closing hearings and teamed up with community activists to camp out all night in front of threatened schools. The leadership of the union, meanwhile, was absent from the fight.


CORE was already “doing what the union should have been doing,” said Chicago social studies teacher Bill Lamme. “So when the election came, [CORE activists] didn’t say ‘Elect me and I’ll do this.’ They said, ‘This is what we’ve been doing and we’ll keep doing it.’”


ATTEND MEETINGS


If you’re serious about getting involved in and transforming your union, you should be regularly attending union meetings, even if the meetings don’t allow for much debate. Bring other members who share your views. By participating, your group can shake things up.


“The first time you attend a meeting, just listen,” says Ken Paff, longtime national organizer with Teamsters for a Democratic Union.


“Later on,” Paff says, “you can make a proposal, and organize your group to present it. Talk to members before the meeting; draw them in. Get things out to the members, not only to make your group transparent, but also to make union meetings that way.


“Tell people there will be a motion on the pension plan, or another burning topic. Ask them to come support the motion. Put it out in writing. Get them to sign a petition in support of it.”


In Letter Carriers (NALC) Branch 9 in Minneapolis, a group of members started meeting to talk about how to change the culture of their branch, including its meeting agendas. “We had a president of over 30 years who would just use Robert’s Rules to keep people down,” says letter carrier Chris Pennock.


But the group of reformers kept bringing more members to meetings. Eventually their motions started winning. Pennock got 10 minutes on the agenda to talk about fighting post office closures. It was a small step, but a co-worker told him: “I don’t know if you know how historic that is—I’ve never seen a motion pass that the executive board not only didn’t support but were actively opposed to.”


Their organizing helped lay the basis to run a reform slate; Pennock is now vice president of Branch 9. “Have faith that you can change the culture,” he says.


At the same time, “it’s a mistake to think that meetings are the important thing,” says SEIU Local 1021’s Pearson—especially since most members won’t attend meetings. You want to find other …

author: Dee Ayroso
title: Romulos Robiños
content:
Romulos “Mulong” Robiños, a 24-year-old tricycle driver was abducted from his home in Angeles city, Pampanga on November 17, 2006 by suspected state forces. The armed suspects barged into their house at 12:30 midnight looking for his sister Leny Robiños, an activist. When they did not find her, they instead forcibly took Mulong. They threatened his mother Lolita that she will not see Mulong again unless she makes Leni “surrender”.

In 2007, the Supreme Court issued a writ of amparo and ordered military camps to allow the search for Mulong. However, the search failed to find Mulong or any other victim of enforced disappearance. He remains missing 20 years later.

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: Two Palestine Solidarity Activists Refuse to Testify Before a Grand Jury
content:
Merrimack County, NH — In November 2023, Sophie Ross and Bridget Shergalis approached a large industrial building in Merrimack, New Hampshire. The structure houses Elbit Systems of America, the domestic branch of an Israeli weapons manufacturer that’s a key supplier of drones and ground equipment used in the country’s ongoing

genocide in Palestine

.


The two were participating in an action organized by Palestine Action U.S. Some blockaded the road leading to the facility while Shergalis and Ross, along with others, continued to the building.


A few protesters stayed on the ground and sprayed the facade with red paint, sealed doors shut with a bike lock, and broke windows. Shergalis and Ross made their ways to the building’s roof and lit flares to announce their presence while attempting to damage the building’s HVAC system.


Both women were arrested that day, along with Calla Walsh. Paige Belanger, another participant, was arrested days later. All four were

charged with multiple felonies

 that could have brought decades in prison if convicted. After a legal battle, and a series of victories, Shergalis, Ross, Belanger and Walsh were

sentenced to 60 days jail time

 for misdemeanor convictions.


See all of our Palestine coverage


Nearly three years after that action, Shergalis and Ross have been subpoenaed to testify in front of a federal grand jury. The reason for the subpoena isn’t clear, but one thing is: both women are refusing to cooperate.


On October 5, Bridget woke up to strangers knocking on her window. When her partner answered, he found people dressed in unassuming clothes. Only after he asked what they wanted did the couple realize what was happening. The strangers were FBI agents there to serve her a subpoena to testify before a grand jury.


She told the agents to leave their contact info and expect to hear from her attorney, Kira Kelly. Ross was spared the door knock after agents delivered a subpoena to Kelly, the attorney representing both of the women.


The document simply ordered both women, individually, to appear in the U.S. District Court in Concord, New Hampshire on October 21, only 16 days out from the delivery of the subpoena.


No other details that clarify the target or goals of the investigation appear in the subpoena, and both Shergalis and Ross, along with their lawyer, are unclear about the reason behind the order. While Kelly told Unicorn Riot an assistant U.S. attorney told them it’s in relation to the 2023 action, no more information was made available to them, leaving everyone but prosecutors to speculate about the motivation behind the investigation.


While details are sparse, reporting from the time of the action and recent developments suggest the grand jury may be related to the Cox Media heir and controversial left-wing benefactor James Cox “Fergie” Chambers Jr.


Chambers participated in the November 2023 Elbit protest where Shergalis and Ross were arrested. In a 2024

profile in Rolling Stone

, Chambers told a reporter he had fled the country after the action for fear that he may be implicated in a racketeering case for his involvement. Chambers insisted in that interview that he wasn’t doing anything wrong by moving to Tunisia, but that he was scared of facing RICO charges.


In July, Chambers was arrested in Ibiza, Spain and he’s been held in the country since while awaiting the

outcome of an extradition order under consideration

 by the Spanish government. The U.S. has asked authorities in Spain to send Chambers back to this country to face charges on a still-sealed indictment.


Related:

Anarchist Hacker Jeremy Hammond Summoned to Testify in Front of Grand Jury


More important to Shergalis and Ross than the who or why of the grand jury’s convening, though, is the principle behind the practice and the pair’s moral objection to the process. The thought of betraying a political movement both say they’re committed to is unacceptable to them.


“I would like to be able to, like, look other people in the eye and sleep at night and all of that good stuff,” Shergalis told Unicorn Riot. “And that’s, that isn’t possible with testifying. It just isn’t, it wouldn’t be.”


By openly opposing the subpoena from the start, both hope to establish that they cannot be coerced into testifying. That’s a key distinction in how things may play out.


Under the

law

, people who refuse to testify after being subpoenaed to a

grand jury

 might be sentenced to jail time for being …

title: La vie d'une fleur.Vostfr
content:
La vie d'une fleur


De Gonzalo Mateos


Titre original : “La vida de una flor”


Catalogne - 2024 – 58'


Version originale sous-titrée en français


Ce documentaire vise à mettre en lumière un épisode peu connu de l’histoire de la Catalogne et de l’État espagnol.


Il s’agit de l’insurrection du Haut Llobregat et du Cardoner, au cours de laquelle le communisme libertaire fut proclamé dans certains villages.


Federica Montseny a évoqué cet événement en ces termes : « Cinq jours d’anarchie… qui n’ont pas duré plus longtemps que la vie d’une fleur. »


L’insurrection libertaire du Haut Llobregat fut la première des trois insurrections générales soutenues par la CNT pendant la période de la République espagnole, avant la Révolution sociale de 1936. Elle s’est déroulée pendant plusieurs jours au cours de la seconde quinzaine de janvier 1932 dans les villages de la région du Berguedà, entre le Llobregat et son affluent, le Cardoner. L’ancrage des sociétés ouvrières catalanes affiliées à l’Association internationale des travailleurs s’appuyait déjà sur plusieurs décennies d’activité de nombreuses associations prônant l’anti-étatisme et une société sans classes. Le capitalisme s’était implanté dans cette région sous la forme d’une exploitation menant principalement à la création de colonies ouvrières textiles et dans l’industrie minière. Dans ces colonies ouvrières, les patrons tentaient de contrôler les relations sociales de leurs travailleurs et d’empêcher leur syndicalisation en les menaçant de perdre leur emploi, et donc les logements où ils vivaient avec leurs familles à proximité des usines.


Le dimanche 17 janvier 1932, une grève est déclenchée dans la commune de Berga, qui s’étendra le lendemain à d’autres localités de la région, parmi lesquelles le village de Fígols, où les ouvrières du textile et les mineurs de Sant Corneli se mettent en grève pour que les accords salariaux conclus soient respectés. La grève fut un succès et entraîna un arrêt total du travail. Mais dans cette commune, la grève avait son propre programme : elle se transforma en une grève révolutionnaire impulsée par des collectifs anarchistes. D’une assemblée réunissant hommes et femmes de la commune naquit l’accord de proclamer le communisme libertaire afin de chasser les patrons industriels de la région. La CNT décide de soutenir l’initiative des travailleurs insurgés ; la Garde civile et le Somatén (milice rurale catalane) sont désarmés, le drapeau rouge et noir est hissé sur la mairie de la localité, la propriété privée est abolie et l’approvisionnement en denrées alimentaires est assuré. Le mercredi 20 janvier 1932, des élections populaires au suffrage universel furent même organisées pour constituer la commune libre de Fígols, au cours desquelles furent élus un délégué général ainsi que huit autres délégués représentatifs. La tendance révolutionnaire de la grève ne triompha toutefois pas complètement à Berga ni à Manresa, mais elle fut un succès dans des villages tels que Sallent, Cardona, Balserany ou Súria. C’est dans ces villages que le communisme libertaire fut proclamé pour la première fois.


À travers des entretiens avec des historiens, des experts, des proches des participants et des habitants de la région, ce documentaire cherche à reconstituer les faits, ainsi qu’à analyser leur contexte et leur importance dans l’imaginaire collectif de la région. Par ailleurs, nous utiliserons comme ressource la voix off des chroniques d’Eduardo de Guzman, un journaliste proche des idées anarchistes, qui fut envoyé spécial par le journal « La Tierra » pendant les jours de l’insurrection. Le documentaire dure environ une heure et utilise des images d’archives ainsi que différents supports graphiques pour reconstituer l’Histoire.

Bangladesh’s first riverkeeper, Sharif Jamil, shares how poor countries in the Global South are struggling to effectively adapt to climate change as rising sea levels, extreme weather patterns, pollution and more are creating an escalating “humanitarian catastrophe,” while the wealthy impede efforts to reallocate financial resources for adaptation and mitigation. “If you want to protect the planet, if you want to save the planet from global warming, you need climate finance to make all this transition,” says Jamil.

Sharif Jamilenvironmental activist, coordinator of Waterkeepers Bangladesh and board member of the Waterkeeper Alliance.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman. We’re broadcasting from COP31, the U.N. climate summit, in Antalya, Turkey.

We turn now to how Global South countries at the frontlines of climate change-fueled disasters are demanding more funding and accountability from rich countries during the negotiations here at COP31.

In August, catastrophic floods in mountainous Nepal washed away entire villages, left nearly 7,000 people dead or missing, triggered by the collapse of a Himalayan glacier. Meanwhile, in low-lying Bangladesh, rising sea levels pose an existential threat to tens of millions of Bangladeshis living along the coast. Bangladesh and Nepal are among the most vulnerable to climate change-related disasters, yet together they contribute less than half a percent of global carbon emissions. They’re also among the poorest countries in the world.

The U.N. Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage was created in 2022 to provide financial support to developing nations on the frontlines of climate-fueled disasters, but the fund has fallen far short of what’s needed. In total, the fund already has over 175 requests from developing countries for nearly $3 billion, but rich countries, the most responsible for climate change, have only pledged $820 million to the fund.

For more, we’re joined by Sharif Jamil, environmental activist, coordinator of Waterkeepers Bangladesh, board member of the Waterkeeper Alliance.

title: Milli Savunma Bakanlığı bütçesinde silahlanmada yüzde 229 artış: Askeri sanayi şirketlerinde kârları patlatmaya devam
content:
Dicle Sezen Öz [email protected]

Milli Savunma Bakanlığının (MSB) 2027 bütçesine ilişkin görüşmeler bugün TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonunda başlıyor. MSB’nin yeni bütçesi, Ankara’da yapılan NATO zirvesinde alınan kararlar, Suudi Arabistan ve Pakistan ile 10 yıl süreyle bağlayıcı olacak şekilde imzalanan Mekke Anlaşması ve Türkiye’nin başta cihatçı HTŞ yönetimindeki Suriye olmak üzere Ortadoğu ve Afrika’da askeri varlığını büyüttüğü bir dönemde görüşülecek.

AKP iktidarı ve askeri sanayi şirketleri yeni siparişler için kapı kapı gezerken, bütçe teklifinde öne çıkan başlık ‘savunma’ ve güvenlik harcamalarındaki rekor artış oldu. Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz’ın da bütçe sunumunda belirttiği üzere silah ve mühimmat alımına ayrılan ödenek yüzde 229 oranında artırılıyor.

2026 yılında 822.9 milyar TL olan MSB bütçesi, 2027 teklifinde yüzde 86.2’lik artışla 1 trilyon 532.6 milyar liraya çıkarılıyor. Bu artışın 573.9 milyar lirası mal ve hizmet alımlarından kaynaklanıyor. Bu kalem yüzde 158.2 artışla 936.6 milyar liraya çıkıyor. Yani 2027 bütçesindeki her 100 liranın 61 lirası bu mal ve hizmetlere yani ‘silah ve mühimmata’ gidecek.

Savaş harcamalarındaki artış Savunma Sanayii Destekleme Fonu (SSDF) ve iç güvenlik birimlerini de kapsayan güvenlik bütçesinde de görülüyor. Söz konusu iki kalemin 2.15 trilyon liradan 3.45 trilyon liraya yükselerek merkezi yönetim bütçesinin yüzde 12.7’sine denk gelmesi bekleniyor. Bu toplam içinde doğrudan ‘savunmaya’ ayrılan pay ise yüzde 83.5 artışla 2.2 trilyon liraya çıkacak.

Aselsan, Roketsan, Tusaş, MKE ve Baykar gibi askeri sanayi şirketlerine akan para, genel bütçe dışında tutulan ve Merkez Bankası nezdinde yönetilen SSDF üzerinden sağlanıyor. Teklifin 10. maddesi, silah alımları ve NATO altyapı yatırımlarında bütçe ödenekleriyle birlikte SSDF kaynaklarının da kullanılmasına imkan tanıyor.

Halktan toplanan vergilerin nasıl şirket kasalarına aktığı Sayıştayın son denetim raporlarıyla da belgeleniyor. Sayıştay verilerine göre SSDF’nin geliri 2025’te yüzde 73.8 artışla 374.5 milyar liraya; bu paranın yüzde 99’unun harcandığı ve çoğunluğu silahlara giden mal ve hizmet alım gideri ise 275.2 milyar liraya çıktı.

Bütçenin diğer yüzünde ise iktidarla kol kola olan askeri sanayi şirketlerinin hızla büyüyen kârları var.

Aselsan’ın 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayındaki net kârı, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 75.1 artarak 15.1 milyar liradan 26.5 milyar liraya kadar yükseldi. Şirketin aynı dönemdeki 151.5 milyar liralık toplam gelirinin yüzde 42’sine denk gelen 63.9 milyar liralık kısmı doğrudan Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığına yapılan satışlardan elde edildi ve elindeki bekleyen sipariş tutarı 30.7 milyar dolara ulaştı.

Baykar 2025 için 2,5 milyar dolar gelir açıklarken, Tusaş’ın üretimden satışları 140.9 milyar lirayı buldu.

Bunlar yalnızca öne çıkan şirketlerin birkaçı. Savunma Sanayii Başkanı Haluk Görgün, geçtiğimiz ay Bursa’da katıldığı bir çalıştayda yıl başından bu yana askeri sanayide 15 milyar dolarlık yeni sözleşme imzalandığını söyledi. Görgün, Aselsan, Roketsan, Tusaş, Havelsan ve STM’nin yurt içindeki alt yüklenicilerine verdiği ve henüz tamamlanmamış siparişlerin tutarının da 13.4 milyar doları aştığını açıkladı.

MSB’ye bütçeden ayrılan bu payın bu denli büyümesinin bir sebebi hiç şüphesiz iktidarın yıl boyu altına imzasını attığı uluslararası anlaşmalar. Son bir yılda askeri sanayi hem yeni iç siparişlerle hem de yeni anlaşmalar ve dış satışlarla yeni pazarlara açıldı. Geçen yılki komisyon görüşmesiyle aynı gün imzalanan 6.5 milyar dolarlık hava savunma paketini, bu yıl ekim ayında Aselsan ile imzalanan 2,46 milyar avroluk hava savunma sözleşmeleri ve mayıs ayında Tusaş ile bağlanan yurt içi Kaan savaş uçağı tedarik anlaşması izledi.

Türkiye, ekim 2025’te Birleşik Krallık’tan 20 Eurofighter savaş uçağı almak için 8 milyar sterline varan bir anlaşmaya imza attı. Mart 2026’da imzalanan eğitim ve destek sözleşmesiyle de BAE Systems ve Rolls-Royce dahil Britanyalı şirketlere iş alanı açıldı. Öte yandan Katar’dan ikinci el Eurofighter alımı için görüşmelerini sürdüren MSB, ekimde Doha’dan satış sözleşmesi taslağını beklediğini bildirdi.

Türkiye’deki askeri sanayi patronlarının bir gözü de dışarıya satışlarda. Bu kapsamda Tusaş, İspanya’nın Airbus liderliğindeki eğitim programı için 30 adet Hürjet, Azerbaycan için ise 14 adet Hürkuş-II üretecek. Türkiye ayrıca Romanya’ya bir adet Hisar sınıfı korvet ve destek paketi satışı için 223 milyon avroluk sözleşme imzaladı.

author: Stelinsky
title: Ανταπόκριση από το εφετείο των 30 συλληφθέντων για την εξέγερση στη δομή Σιντικής τον Νοέμβρη του ’25
content:
Κατηγορίες: Στάση κρατουμένων, διακεκριμένη φθορά πράγματος κοινού οφέλους.

Πρωτόδικες ποινές: 3 χρόνια ο καθένας.

Βρισκόμαστε στο Τριμελές Πλημμελειοδικείο Σερρών. Στην αίθουσα εκδίκασης υπάρχει ήδη από νωρίς παρουσία αλληλέγγυου κόσμου. Η χωρητικότητα είναι περιορισμένη καθώς η αίθουσα είναι πολύ μικρή.

Οι κρατούμενοι εισέρχονται στην αίθουσα, δεμένοι με χειροπέδες, καθένας συνοδευόμενος από έναν αστυνομικό της Υπηρεσίας Εξωτερικής Φρούρησης Καταστημάτων Κράτησης. Κάθονται στην αριστερή μεριά της αίθουσας, όλοι μαζί, περικυκλωμένοι από αστυνομικές δυνάμεις. Τριγύρω τους βρίσκονται οι τέσσερις μάρτυρες κατηγορίας. Στη δεξιά πλευρά της αίθουσας κάθονται οι μάρτυρες υπεράσπισης και ο αλληλέγγυος κόσμος.

Υπάρχει παρουσία ενός διερμηνέα, αλληλέγγυου, που προσφέρθηκε να μεταφράσει για τους αραβόφωνους. Για τον έναν κρατούμενο από το Μπαγκλαντές υπάρχει διερμηνεία στα Αγγλικά, γλώσσα που δεν τη μιλάει με άνεση.

Παρίστανται οι 24 από τους 30. Οι 6 που απουσιάζουν, είναι αυτοί που δεν άσκησαν έφεση, πιθανότατα γιατί δεν ενημερώθηκαν ποτέ ότι είχαν τη δυνατότητα.

10 από τις 24 εφέσεις έγιναν εκπρόθεσμα, κατά δύο μέρες, είτε λόγω έλλειψης διερμηνείας, είτε λόγω καθυστερημένης ενημέρωσης των κρατουμένων. Οι υπόλοιποι, που άσκησαν έφεση εντός προθεσμίας, στην πραγματικότητα ενημερώθηκαν από τον μοναδικό συγκρατούμενό τους που μιλούσε Αγγλικά.

Η εισαγγελέας προτείνει την απόρριψη των εκπρόθεσμων εφέσεων.

— Συνήγορος Υπεράσπισης (στο εξής ΣΥ): Δεν διαπιστώνεται κάπως εάν οι κρατούμενοι πράγματι ενημερώθηκαν την ημέρα που αναγράφεται. Πρόκειται για θεμελιώδη καταπάτηση δικαιωμάτων των κατηγορουμένων, λόγω έλλειψης διερμηνείας. Οι εφέσεις πρέπει να γίνουν δεκτές, εφόσον έγιναν εντός 10ημέρου από την ημέρα που ξέρουμε ότι όντως ενημερώθηκαν. Στο πρωτόδικο δεν δόθηκε ποτέ η ευκαιρία στους κατηγορούμενους κατά την απολογία τους να αναφερθούν στις συνθήκες κράτησής τους, πράγμα που σας ζητάμε να γίνει σήμερα. Επιπλέον, υπάρχει βιντεοληπτικό υλικό που δεν συμπεριλαμβάνεται στη δικογραφία, που θα θέλαμε να προβληθεί, που αφορά τις συνθήκες κράτησης και την επικινδυνότητα εντός του καμπ της Σιντικής.

Οι εφέσεις απορρίπτονται και ακούγονται τα ονόματα των απορριφθέντων. Οι αστυνομικοί τους βγάζουν έναν-έναν από την αίθουσα και τους επιστρέφουν στη φυλακή.

Η έδρα δεν δέχεται την προβολή του βιντεοληπτικού υλικού, με τον ισχυρισμό ότι, εφόσον δεν είναι μέρος της δικογραφίας και δεν έχει εξεταστεί, μπορεί να εκτεθούν προσωπικά δεδομένα.

Ξεκινούν οι καταθέσεις των τεσσάρων μαρτύρων κατηγορίας (στο εξής ΜΚ), όλοι τους αστυνομικοί/συνοριοφύλακες.

Λένε πως υπήρχε αναταραχή στην πτέρυγα 4, όπου οι αστυνομικοί συναντήθηκαν με μία ομάδα τεσσάρων κρατούμενων «για να συζητήσουν για τα αιτήματα τους».

— ΜΚ1: Mέσα στα παράπονά τους ήταν ότι «κάποιοι άλλοι που έρχονται στη δομή από τις ίδιες χώρες [με τους κατηγορούμενους], αφήνονται ελεύθεροι, οπότε εμείς γιατί είμαστε ακόμα εδώ;» Φάνηκε ότι καλύφθηκε το θέμα προσωρινά. Όταν γυρίσαμε στην πτέρυγά τους, όπου ο διοικητής τούς εξήγησε την κατάσταση, ότι δηλαδή οι αστυνομικές δυνάμεις δεν έχουν καμία άλλη αρμοδιότητα πέρα από το να τους περιφρουρούν, τότε αγρίεψαν. Ύστερα μάθαμε από διερμηνέα ότι ο ένας ο μεγαλύτερος τούς έλεγε να ηρεμήσουν, ενώ τρεις άλλοι τούς έλεγαν να εξεγερθούν. Τους βάλαμε και τους τέσσερις στο κελί τους κι άρχισαν να μας πετάνε πέτρες μόλις μπήκαν μέσα απ’ τα κάγκελα.

Όπως αναφέρουν και οι άλλοι τρεις μάρτυρες κατηγορίας «κατά τις 3 η ώρα, κάποιοι ξεκίνησαν να σπρώχνουν το συρματόπλεγμα που περιβάλλει τη δομή και να πετάνε πέτρες στους αστυνομικούς». Ο ΜΚ1 αδυνατεί να αναγνωρίσει κάποιον κατηγορούμενο με εξαίρεση «τους τέσσερις διαπραγματευτές» τους οποίους «θυμάται αμυδρά».

Σε ερώτηση της έδρας σχετικά με το αν εξεγερμένοι κρατούμενοι ήταν κουκουλωμένοι ο ΜΚ1 απαντά: «Όχι, δεν ήταν κουκουλωμένοι απλώς ο ένας ανέβασε το φούτερ του μέχρι το ύψος των ματιών και δεν μου φάνηκε καλό σημάδι.»

Ο ΜΚ2 περιγράφει τρία άτομα να πηδούν έξω από τον φράχτη και να επιστρέφουν μόλις συνειδητοποιήσουν ότι έγιναν αντιληπτοί. Ενώ συμμετείχε στην αρχική αναγνώριση των δραστών, στην αίθουσα αδυνατεί να ταυτοποιήσει κάποιον. Στην πρώτη του κατάθεση λέει πως αναγνώρισε ένα μόνο άτομο, ενώ τώρα αντιφάσκει λέγοντας πως συμμετείχε στην αναγνώριση κάποιων «που του υπέδειξαν οι συνάδελφοί του» και ότι τελικά κατάφεραν να τους ξεχωρίσουν «από εκδορές που είχαν πάνω στα σώματα τους».

Ο συνήγορος υπεράσπισης αναδεικνύει το πώς οι καταθέσεις των μαρτύρων κατηγορίας είναι αντιφατικές μεταξύ τους …

author: Unknown
title: ASAL kasım anketinde de birinci parti "hiçbiri"
content:
ASAL Araştırma'nın 17 Kasım'da açıklanan milletvekili genel seçimi anketi, seçmenlerin mevcut siyasi partilere yönelik tercihlerinde dikkat çekici bir eğilimin sürdüğünü ortaya koydu: Araştırmaya katılanların yüzde 36,7'si kararsız olduğunu, oy kullanmayacağını ya da bir parti tercihi bildirmediğini belirtti.


ASAL'ın ekim araştırmasında bu üç kategoridekilerin toplamı yüzde 37,8'di. Kasım araştırmasında parti tercihi belirtmeyenlerin oranı bir ayda 1,1 puan azalmış olsa da bu toplam, hem ekimde hem kasımda en yüksek oy oranına sahip partininin yaklaşık iki katına ulaştı.


Kasımda AKP'nin ham oy oranı yüzde 18,8, YENİ Parti'nin yüzde 16,1 olarak ölçüldü. Parti tercihi belirtmeyen veya oy kullanmayacağını söyleyenlerin toplamı ise yüzde 36,7 oldu.


SONAR'ın ekim anketinde de, kararsızlar, sandığa gitmeyeceğini söyleyenler ve görüş belirtmeyenler yüzde 33,1 ile en büyük seçmen kümesini oluşturmuştu. AKP'nin ham oy oranı yüzde 19,8, Yeni Parti'ninki yüzde 18,8'di. SONAR Başkanı 38 yılda ilk kez bu sonuçla karşılaştığını söyledi.


SONAR anketinde birinci "parti" yüzde 33 ile "hiçbir parti"


6 Kasım 2026


Üç ayrı yanıt, seçmenin üçte birinden fazlası


İki araştırmanın ham sonuçları karşılaştırıldığında, parti tercihi belirtmeyenlerin toplamındaki gerilemenin esas olarak oy kullanmayacağını söyleyenlerden kaynaklandığı görülüyor.


Kararsız olduğunu söyleyenlerin oranı hemen hemen değişmezken oy kullanmayacağını belirtenler 1,8 puan azaldı. Buna karşılık fikri olmadığını söyleyen veya soruyu yanıtsız bırakanların oranı 0,9 puan arttı.


Bu üç yanıt aynı siyasal tutumu ifade etmiyor. Kararsız seçmen henüz bir parti seçmemiş olabilir; oy kullanmayacağını söyleyen seçmen ise sandığa katılmama eğilimini dile getiriyor. Fikir belirtmeyenlerin gerekçeleri de araştırmanın yayımlanan sonuçlarından anlaşılamıyor.


Dolayısıyla yüzde 36,7'lik toplamı tek bir siyasal eğilimin veya ortak bir protesto hareketinin göstergesi olarak değerlendirmek mümkün değil. Ancak bu büyüklükte bir kitlenin mevcut partilerden herhangi birini tercih etmemesi, siyasal temsil ve seçmen bağlılığı bakımından araştırmanın en dikkat çekici bulgusunu oluşturuyor.


Partilerin oy oranları nasıl değişti?


ASAL'ın kararsızları, oy kullanmayacağını söyleyenleri ve yanıt vermeyenleri orantısal olarak dağıttığı iki araştırma, partilerin oy oranlarında da değişim gösteriyor.


AKP'nin oy oranı bir ayda 1,9 puan gerilerken YENİ Parti'nin oranı hemen hemen değişmedi. İki parti arasındaki fark 6,4 puandan 4,3 puana indi.


DEM Parti'nin oy oranı 0,7 puan yükselirken diğer partilerin oranlarında daha sınırlı değişiklikler kaydedildi.


Bu sonuçlar, kararsızlar ve diğer yanıt vermeyenler dağıtıldıktan sonra hesaplanan oranlar. Başka bir deyişle, seçmenlerin tamamının doğrudan açıkladığı parti tercihlerini değil, araştırma şirketinin uyguladığı dağıtım işlemi sonrasında ortaya çıkan tabloyu gösteriyor.


Ham sonuçlarda AKP yüzde 18,8


Kasım araştırmasının dağıtım öncesi sonuçlarında AKP yüzde 18,8, YENİ Parti yüzde 16,1, DEM Parti yüzde 6,0, MHP yüzde 4,9, İYİ Parti yüzde 4,4 ve CHP yüzde 3,5 oranında destek buldu.


Ekimde aynı oranlar AKP için yüzde 19,6, YENİ Parti için yüzde 15,7 ve DEM Parti için yüzde 5,5'ti.


Böylece ham sonuçlarda AKP 0,8 puan gerilerken YENİ Parti 0,4, DEM Parti 0,5 puan yükseldi.


Ancak iki ayın en belirgin ortak özelliği, partilerin sıralamasından çok, hiçbir parti tercihi açıklamayan veya oy kullanmayacağını söyleyen seçmenlerin toplam büyüklüğü oldu.


Araştırmalar nasıl yapıldı?


ASAL Araştırma, ekim anketini 4-10 Ekim 2026 tarihlerinde, 28 ilde 2 bin 20 kişiyle gerçekleştirdi. Bilgisayar destekli telefon görüşmeleriyle yapılan araştırmanın açıklanan hata payı yüzde 95 güven düzeyinde ±2,41 puandı.


Kasım araştırması ise 8-15 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde 28 ilde 2 bin 5 kişiyle yapıldı. Araştırma için açıklanan hata payı yüzde 95 güven düzeyinde ±2,43 puan.


İki anket, aynı seçmenlerin zaman içindeki davranışlarını izleyen bir panel araştırması değil. Bu nedenle aylık oran değişimleri, tek tek seçmenlerin hangi partiden ayrıldığını veya nereye yöneldiğini göstermiyor.


(AEK)

author: Unknown
title: Иван Асташин о смерти Татьяны Уваровой — тёти политзаключённого Никиты Уварова
content:
Публикуем текст Ивана Асташина из его телеграм-канала, посвящённый памяти Татьяны Уваровой, скончавшейся 12 октября.

Татьяну я впервые увидел 17 января 2021 года — она подключилась вместе с мамой Никиты Анной к инфовстрече, посвящённой «делу канских подростков», которую мы проводили в Петербурге. Когда она начала выступать, было слышно, что она с трудом сдерживает слёзы. Она говорила, и Анна это подтверждала, что растила и воспитывала Никиту вместе со своей сестрой как родного ребёнка.

С тех пор у меня было ощущение, что они всё время вместе — Татьяна, Анна и двоюродный брат Никиты Максим. Вместе ездили на свидания к Никите в колонию, были рядом, когда я звонил Анне... Это подтверждает и журналист «Новой газеты» Алексей Тарасов, написавший после смерти Татьяны большой репортаж о жизни большой семьи Никиты: «Штаб по спасению детей располагался в доме Тани, для невеселых разговоров там и собирались. Татьяна была крестной матерью Никиты, вместе с Анной растила его с пеленок. И если Анна теперь каменела в горе, несла его как двужильная (ей и дальше нести — больше некому), то Таню эта беда расщемляла, топтала, размазывала. Она не могла себя собрать обратно».

Я третий раз погружаюсь в эту тему — и третий раз слёзы наворачиваются на глаза. 6 лет назад я узнал про «дело канских подростков». В этом году Никита должен был освободиться — уже не 14-летний подросток, каким его задержали, а 20-летний юноша. Но чекистам оказалось мало кражи 5 лет свободы у юного анархиста — за месяц до освобождения против него сфабриковали новое, совершенно абсурдное дело.

Ни Татьяне, ни Анне после возбуждения нового дела не давали свиданий с Никитой. Звонки тоже не разрешали. Суд раз за разом продлевал содержание в СИЗО. Татьяна вместе с Анной ходила на все заседания, снова и снова подавала следователю заявления на свидания. Её последней репликой в суде стало восклицание: — Когда уже это кончится, господи?! Сколько можно издеваться над нами, кровь пить?! Господи, есть ли ты?!

Теперь Татьяны нет. И я не представляю, что чувствует Никита в одиночной камере красноярского СИЗО. Что чувствует Анна. Что чувствует Максим.

Близким политзаключённых нередко приходится тяжелее, чем самим узникам. Следователи, чекисты, менты понимают это. Но для них они родственники «врага народа». Да и в целом у силовиков, которые занимаются политическими делами, как правило, отсутствуют какие-то человеческие чувства по отношению к тем, чьими судьбами они распоряжаются. Смерть Татьяны на руках ФСБ и СК.

Таню не вернуть, но вы можете поддержать Никиту, а можете — близких политзаключённых, если знакомы с ними. Не только сами политпреследуемые не должны оставаться один на один с репрессивной машиной, но и их близкие, те, кто их поддерживают.

Адрес для писем Никите: 660075, г. Красноярск, ул. Республики, 72, СИЗО-1 Уваров Никита Андреевич 2005 г. р.

Отправить письмо можно через сервисы «Ф-письмо», «Зонателеком» и PrisonMail.Online (для зарубежных карт).

На фото Никита, Татьяна и Максим. Фото из семейного архива, опубликовано «Новой газетой»

author: Unknown
title: Ji bo girtiyên nexweş ben berdan çalakiya nobetê hat destpêkirin
content:
Malbatên Girtiyên Nexweş, Komeleya Piştgirî û Piştevaniyê ya Malbatên Girtî û Hikumxwaran re (TUAY-DER), DEM Partî, Komeleya Hiqûqnasên Ji bo Azadiyê (OHD), Komeleya Mafê Mirovan (ÎHD) gelek kes bi daxwaza girtiyên nexweş bên berdan û gihîştina mafê tenduristiyê li ber Wezareta Dadê çalakiya nobetê ya bêdem dan destpêkirin.


Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat parlamenterên DEM Partiyê û gelek kes jî ji bo piştgiriyê tevlî daxuyaniyê bûn.


Di daxuyaniyê de pankarta navê girtiyên nexweş li ser bû û li ser, “Em ê deriyên zindanê bi berxwedanê vêbikin” dinivisî hat vekirin. Her wiha girseyê bênavber dirûşmeyên, “Girtiyên siyasî rûmeta me ne”, “Ji girtiyên nexweş re azadî” berz kir.


"Heta girtiyên nexweş bên berdan çalakiya me dê bidome"


Hevberdevkê TUAY-DERa Enqereyê Şîrîn Altay bi lêv kir ew ji bo êdî di girtîgehan de girtî jiyana xwe ji dest nedin dest bi çalakiyê kirinê û wiha axivî:


“Tevî pêvajoya Aştî û Civaka Demokratîk jî hê li girtîgehan girtiyên nexweş jiyana xwe ji dest didin û berdana wan tê asteng kirin. Em ji bo dengê xwe bigihînin berpirsan li vir dest bi çalakiyê dikin. Divê girtiyên nexweş demildest bên berdan. Heta girtiyên nexweş bên berdan çalakiya me dê bidome.”


"Em ji bo kes êdî nemirê têdikoşin"


Parlamenterê DEM Partiyê yê Mersînê Alî Bozan jî destnîşan kir ku bernedana girtiyên nexweş baweriya ji bo pêvajoyê dişkînê û wiha got:


“Em ji bo pêvajoyê têdikoşin. Em ji bo kes êdî nemirê têdikoşin. Lê hê jî li girtî jiyana xwe ji dest didin. Êdî tahamula me nemayê. Hê hefteyê borî girtiyê nexweş Tuncer Sağlam jiyana xwe ji dest da. Baweriya civakê ji bo vê rewşe kêm bû ye. Em ji bo girtiyên nexweş dest bi çalakiya nobeda bê dem dikin. Em li vir bang li Wezareta Dadê û saziyên dewletê dikin ku li gor pêvajoyê tevbigerin û girtiyên nexweş berdin.”


"Divê ev nobet ji berê ve bihata dest pê kirin"


Dayika girtiya nexweş Newroz Bozkurt ku nexweş,ua Losemiya kronîkê lê peyda bûye û li nexweşxaneyê tê derman kirin û rewşa wê xeternek e, Sultan Bozkurt jî diyar kir ku ew ji ber nexweşiya keça xwe ji Stenbolê hatiye û wiha axivî:


“Hê jî min nekariye keça xwe bibînim. Ne nexweşxaneye, ew der jî girtîgeh e. Ez Enqereyê baş nizanim. Heke min baş bizaniba ez ê peya biçûma wir. Divê ev nobet ji berê ve bihata dest pê kirin. Bi vê pêvajoyê re me got êdî dayik nagirîn. Lê dayikên Kurd hê jî digirîn. Tu ferqa hêsirê çavê dayikan tune ye. Divê êdî dayik negirîn û ji bo wê ez li vir careke din bang li saziyên dewletê dikim ku girtiyên nexweş demildest berdin.”


"Mafê tenduristiyê mafekî bingehîn e"


Hevjinê girtiya nexweş Evîn Zapsûyê ku teşhîsa penceşêrê merheleya 4an lê hatibû danîn Mecîd Zapsû jî destnîşan kir ku ew ji bo dengê xwe bigihînin saziyên pêwendîdar dest bi çalakiya nobetê dikin û wiha got: 


“Em ji bo Wezareta Dadê peywîra xwe bi cih bîne li vir in. Mafê tenduristiyê mafekî bingehîn e. Lê ji ber ku ew maf tê binpêkirin îro girtî bi gelek nexweşiyan re rû bi rû dimînin. Hevjina min Evîn jî li girtîgehê nexweş bû û ji ber ku tedawiyeke baş nehat kirin rewşa wê giran bû. Heta girtiyên nexweş werin berdan em ê çalakiya xwe bidomînin.”


Piştî axaftinan girseyê li vir dest bi nobedê kir. Piştî demekê polîsan xwest mudaxileyî çalakiyê bike. Li ser vê yekê girseyê bertek nîşan da û di bin dorpêça polîsan de çalakiya xwe didomîne. Hate gotin ku dê nobet sibê jî li heman cihî berdewam bike.


Li gorî agahiyên fermî yên Parlamentoyê di sala 2025an de li girtîgehan jê 792 hukumxwar, 77 girtî û bi giştî 869 kesan bi awayekî bi guman jiyana xwe ji dest dane. 132 girtî jî di pêvajoyên qeza an destûrê de mirine ku bi hev re 1001 kes mirine. Her wiha di navbera 1ê Kanûna Paşîn û 6ê Gulana 2026an de 26 girtiyan xwe kuştiye û ji van 14 girtî jî dermanên psîkiyatrîk bi kar dianîn.


Li gorî daneyên ÎHDyê hezar û 412

girtiyên nexweş

 hene. 


(AY)

author: Unknown
title: Pisa, depositi di esplosivi: la città sempre più esposta ai rischi della guerra
content:
Due nuovi depositi di munizioni a San Giusto, un hangar da 40 milioni e un aeroporto che ogni anno accoglie quasi sei milioni di passeggeri. Chi garantisce la sicurezza della popolazione?


Un’interessante inchiesta condotta dal

Movimento No Base.


All’interno dell’aeroporto militare di Pisa vogliono realizzare due nuovi depositi destinati allo stoccaggio di esplosivi e munizionamento. Non si tratta di un’ipotesi o di un progetto ancora indefinito. A confermarlo è il capitolato speciale d’appalto dell’Aeronautica Militare, che descrive nel dettaglio le opere previste, le loro finalità e i costi.


Il progetto prevede la costruzione di due riservette di tipo igloo, strutture in cemento armato destinate alla conservazione di materiale esplosivo, accompagnate da bastionature di protezione, una tettoia per lo stoccaggio temporaneo degli esplosivi, una recinzione perimetrale con cancello carrabile elettrificato e un locale uffici. L’importo a base di gara è di oltre 5,5 milioni di euro. Il 28 ottobre 2026 l’appalto è stato aggiudicato per un impegno complessivo indicato in oltre 6,1 milioni di euro. Secondo la documentazione progettuale resa pubblica da Diritti in Comune, ciascuna delle due strutture sarebbe dimensionata per una capacità indicativa di dieci tonnellate di esplosivo netto equivalente, per un totale iniziale di venti tonnellate. La stessa documentazione segnala inoltre la possibilità di predisporre in futuro altre quattro riservette, che porterebbero la capacità complessiva potenziale a sessanta tonnellate.


Ma il dato che più dovrebbe richiamare l’attenzione della cittadinanza non è soltanto la quantità di materiale che potrà essere conservata. È la funzione che queste strutture sono chiamate a svolgere. Il capitolato spiega infatti che la necessità di stoccare munizionamento e materiali esplosivi, indicati con la denominazione 

HOT CARGO

, deriva da esigenze operative direttamente collegate all’attività di volo e alla presenza di un 

Air Terminal Operation Centre

 della JMOU Italia. Non siamo quindi davanti a un intervento edilizio generico all’interno di un’area militare: l’obiettivo dichiarato è dotare lo scalo di una nuova capacità di deposito e gestione di munizionamento ed esplosivi funzionale alle attività militari, anche a quelle connesse ai teatri di guerra.


È questo passaggio che rende il progetto particolarmente rilevante per Pisa. La città ospita la 46ª Brigata Aerea, uno dei principali reparti italiani per il trasporto militare di personale, mezzi e materiali. L’aeroporto militare costituisce una componente essenziale del sistema infrastrutturale della Difesa, ma si trova anche al centro di un contesto urbano densamente abitato e condivide lo spazio aeroportuale con lo scalo civile Galileo Galilei. La realizzazione dei depositi aggiunge dunque una funzione nuova e significativa a un’infrastruttura che già svolge un ruolo militare rilevante.


Un aeroporto, due funzioni, milioni di passeggeri


C’è un elemento che rende la vicenda pisana particolarmente delicata e che non può essere lasciato sullo sfondo: l’aeroporto militare non è un’infrastruttura separata dalla vita civile della città. La gestione dello scalo civile è affidata a Toscana Aeroporti, società il cui presidente è 

Marco Carrai

, che ricopre anche l’incarico di console onorario dello Stato di Israele per Toscana, Emilia-Romagna e Lombardia. Il sedime e le infrastrutture militari fanno invece capo all’Aeronautica Militare. Le due funzioni convivono nello stesso sistema aeroportuale.


Nel 2025 lo scalo ha registrato quasi sei milioni di passeggeri. A questi numeri si aggiungono le centinaia di lavoratrici e lavoratori che ogni giorno operano nei servizi aeroportuali, nella movimentazione delle merci, nella manutenzione, nella sicurezza e nelle attività connesse allo scalo. Intorno all’aeroporto si trovano inoltre quartieri abitati da decine di migliaia di persone, a partire da San Giusto e San Marco. 

Ma non ci sono soltanto le abitazioni e le infrastrutture aeroportuali: nelle vicinanze si sviluppano alcune delle principali arterie di comunicazione della città e dell’intera area pisana, come la via Aurelia e la superstrada Firenze-Pisa-Livorno (Fi-Pi-Li), percorse quotidianamente da un intenso traffico di automobili, mezzi pesanti e lavoratori pendolari. author: Nathaniel Njeru Mugo
title: The names on the ice
content:
Mount Kenya’s glaciers carry names such as Lewis, Gregory, Tyndall, Darwin, Forel and Heim. Within a few years, the ice carrying those names may be gone. Two of the less famous glaciers, Cesar and Josef, tell the story better.

In 1899, Halford Mackinder set out to make the

first recorded ascent of Batian

 with six Europeans, 66 Swahilis, two Maasai guides and 96 Kikuyu. Among the Europeans were César Ollier and Joseph Brocherel, Alpine guides from Courmayeur in Italy. Brocherel was also listed as a porter. Both men left their names on the mountain:

Cesar Glacier and Josef Glacier

.

The 96 Kikuyu did not.

That discrepancy invites an easy story about Europeans overwriting an African map. The mountain is less tidy. Lower down, African names persist:

Kikami

,

from the Kikuyu word for hyrax;


Mbairunyi

,

“Place of Fighting”;


Gacheno

,

“Place of Danger”;


Kethimbui

,

“Place of Rest.”

 They record animals, conflict, fear and respite rather than distant scientists and explorers. The pattern is not absence but altitude. The higher the map goes, the whiter it gets.

Even the summit area complicates that pattern.

Mackinder adopted Batian, Nelion and Lenana, names of Maasai figures, on the suggestion of Sidney Langford Hinde

, a British colonial officer in Maasailand. Africans appear throughout the mountain’s nomenclature — as guides and porters, as informants and sources of names. Europeans were usually the people deciding which names entered the map, and which endured.

At the ice line, the contrast becomes harder to miss. Lewis is named for a geologist; Darwin for Charles Darwin. The ice became an index of European science, honoring men with no particular connection to Mount Kenya. Tyndall is the sharpest case.

His experiments established that gases including carbon dioxide and water vapor absorb radiant heat

. The glacier bearing his name is disappearing in a changing climate.

There is a second imbalance. The industrialized countries from which many of those explorers and scientists came account for a disproportionate share of the emissions changing the planet’s climate. From 1850 to 2019,

the IPCC calculates

, developed countries produced 57% of cumulative fossil fuel and industrial carbon dioxide emissions; Africa, just 3%. The names were assigned here; most of the carbon was emitted elsewhere.

Nor was every European name an act of personal vanity. When J.W. Gregory surveyed Mount Kenya,

he named glaciers after Forel and Heim for a practical reason: glaciers needed names if they were to be described and mapped

.

Useful to whom is a small question, but not an empty one.

The

Mountain Club of Kenya’s guide

 records that in 1924 porters insisted they had seen a lion beside a tarn; Melhuish and Dutton called it Simba Tarn. The porters’ observation survived on the map; their names did not. The same men named another tarn after Gitchini, Melhuish’s personal servant, who accompanied him on mountain journeys.

Another name connects Mount Kenya with Kilimanjaro. The missionary

Johannes Rebmann joined Johann Ludwig Krapf in Mombasa in 1846

. In 1848, Rebmann reported snow on Kilimanjaro. On

December 3, 1849, Krapf sighted Mount Kenya

, whose name he recorded as Kenia or Kegnia after hearing it from Kamba people. The precise etymology is disputed, but an African name entered the European written record and eventually named the country.

Krapf got a glacier too.

There is precedent for reconsidering what mountains record. At

Tanganyika’s independence in 1961, Kilimanjaro’s Kaiser-Wilhelm-Spitze became Uhuru Peak

. The summit proclaimed freedom; the ice retained a different history.

Rebmann Glacier

 was not renamed. Kenya became independent two years later, and Krapf Glacier kept its name too.

In 1963,

twelve of Mount Kenya’s named glaciers still survived

: Northey, Krapf, Gregory, Lewis, Melhuish, Diamond, Darwin, Forel, Heim, Tyndall, Cesar and Josef. Their names did not change. Kenya nonetheless

renamed Lake Rudolf as Lake Turkana in 1975

. The machinery existed. It simply never reached the ice.

Lewis Glacier

lost 90 % of its volume between 1934 and 2010

.

Prinz and colleagues found

 Lewis Glacier’s mass balance most sensitive to atmospheric moisture, through snowfall, cloud cover, and surface reflectivity. Their model showed that increased snow accumulation could produce net gains in ice without significant cooling. Satellite mapping from 2021 and 2022 found just

0.069 square …

author: WoMin
title: Women Unite to Defend the Congo Basin Against Extractivism – A Call for Climate Justice at COP31
content:
As world leaders gather in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), taking place from 9–20 November 2026, women from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the Republic of Congo and Cameroon are raising an urgent message: there can be no climate justice without defending the Congo Basin, protecting community territories and recognising the leadership of women on the frontlines of environmental struggles.


The Congo Basin is one of the world’s most important ecological treasures, acting as the “

second lungs

 of the Earth”, after the Amazon, which is being decimated. Spanning over four million square kilometres across six countries, its forests, rivers and peatlands play a vital role in regulating the global climate, protecting biodiversity and sustaining millions of people. For Indigenous Peoples and local communities, the forest is not simply a natural resource; it is their home, heritage, identity and source of life.


Yet this vital ecosystem faces growing threats from mining, logging, oil and gas extraction, deforestation and expanding infrastructure. Across the Congo Basin, rising demand for minerals is increasing pressure on forests and community territories.


Recent investigations have

documented

 mining concessions overlapping with community forests in the DRC, gold-mining-related

forest destruction and water pollution

 in the Republic of Congo, and

concerns over the impacts

 of the Lobé-Kribi iron-ore project on forests and livelihoods in Cameroon.


This exposes a growing contradiction: while governments promote renewable energy as a solution to the climate crisis, the extraction of minerals needed for the energy transition can create new threats to forests, water resources and the communities that depend on them.


For women in the Congo Basin, this is not an abstract debate. It means polluted rivers, disappearing food sources, loss of agricultural land and declining access to forests.


Women on the frontlines expose the cost of extractivism


To strengthen collective resistance, women and community organisations from the DRC, the Republic of Congo and Cameroon came together for a

cross-border solidarity exchange

 to share stories of resistance, expose the impacts of extractivism and develop strategies to defend the Congo Basin.


Over three days, organisations including

Centre d’Encadrement pour la Promotion de la Femme et la jeune fille

 (CEPF),

Dynamique des femmes pour le développement

 (DYFED),

Green Development Advocates

 (GDA), and the Association pour le Respect des Droit des population autochtones et du développement rural et du Droit de l’homme (ARPA2DH)

shared their experiences and struggles. Testimonies from women in Lessoukou, Mayoko, Mangi, Bongonde and Bandzonko revealed the devastating impacts of mining and forest exploitation.


In Lessoukou, 17 of the community’s 24 villages are reportedly occupied by mining companies, threatening access to ancestral lands and traditional livelihoods. Élisé Matsanga, an Indigenous woman from Lessoukou, shared:


“

Agriculture once enabled us to feed our families and send our children to school. Today, because of corporate activities and the loss of access to our lands, we can no longer farm as we used to. We have lost our livelihoods

.”


In Mangi, Tshopo Province, Nyota described how communities are excluded from decisions affecting their territories while rivers become increasingly polluted.


“

We are forced to walk up to three kilometres to find safe drinking water, and sometimes even our children have no choice but to drink polluted water. Our lands, forests and rivers are our sources of livelihood, yet we watch helplessly as they are destroyed

.”


In Bandzonko, Republic of Congo, Odile, the village chief,

described how mining pollution

 has forced women to walk up to 15 kilometres in search of water, exposing families to serious health risks. In Bongonde, Équateur Province, Annie Mboyo, a community woman,

highlighted the disappearance

 of mushrooms, caterpillars, wild fruits and fish, resources that have traditionally sustained community food systems. Meanwhile, in Mayoko, Oko Jeanine, another community woman, denounced the lack of consultation and the destruction of agricultural fields by mining companies.


“

These lands belong to us. They are our heritage, our livelihoods and our identity. How can companies demand that we obtain permits to cultivate our own land while they extract …

author: Mzi Velapi
title: Western Cape hit with tighter water restrictions
content:
The water and sanitation department has issued a warning to residents and businesses in the Western Cape that it will implement a 7% reduction in domestic and industrial water allocations as well as a 15% reduction in water for irrigation. Addressing the media on Monday, Minister of Water and Sanitation, Pemmy Majodina said that the current water in storage in the province is below the preferred operational threshold of 80%.


“While the major dams remain at acceptable levels overall, some key components of the system have recorded significant declines compared to the previous year. Storage levels remain significantly above those experienced during the severe drought period of 2016-2017; yet, the current water storage is below the preferred operational threshold of 80% and approximately 11.9 % points below the ten-year average of 84.49%,” Majodina said.


According to the minister, the decline in stored water resulted from below-average winter rainfall in the province while the looming El Niño event is increasing temperatures and evaporation.


Municipalities are expected to restrict water supply to residents and can impose further restrictions, but by no more than the 7% that the national government has imposed. The department is expected to write a submission to the director general who will approve the restriction and get it gazetted.


“Modelling undertaken by water resource specialists reveals that if water users continue to utilise their full allocations without intervention, the risk of water shortages and mandatory restrictions will increase substantially from 2027 onwards,” said Majodina.


The City of Cape has announced that it will introduce level 1 water restrictions from 1 December 2026.


Rural taps already dry


The Kannaland Local Municipality that covers Ladismith, Calitzdorp and Zoar are already on level 4 water restrictions. Water in the municipality is available for human consumption only.


Carmelitta Juries lives on a farm near Ladismith. While the farm dam is full, the water isn’t safe to drink without first disinfecting it with bleach. Carmelitta said they have no choice but to rely on the unsafe dam water as the municipality offers no alternative. “The municipality promised that they would put up water tanks. One tank could sustain a couple of homes. For example, 10 homes can use one tank, but to date we haven’t heard anything further,” she said.


Zoar resident, Irene Isaacs said that it is harder for the village to access water in summer. Community members without water storage tanks must wait for municipal trucks to deliver water. Elderly residents are especially vulnerable in these circumstances, she said, and depend on members of the community to carry water in buckets to their homes.


Kannaland Municipality is already on level 4 restrictions. File photo by Mandla Mnyakama


Bergriver, Swartland and Saldanha Bay municipalities have been flagged as key areas where water scarcity and aging infrastructure pose significant constraints to future growth unless supply and bulk infrastructure are urgently upgraded. Hendrix Van Wyk from Vredenburg, which falls under Saldanha Bay Municipality, told

Elitsha

 that in poor neighbourhoods like Hopland, Louwville, Selbou and Yskor, the water pressure in the taps is low. “It takes up to 30 minutes to fill up a 5-litre bucket and a 20-litre bucket takes about 2 hours to fill up,” he said.


According to Majodina, construction of the Clanwilliam Dam, which will increase water availability for the West Coast District Municipality, is 40% complete.


Partnership, not privatisation of water

 insists DWS


A

new amendment to the Water Plan

 states that if a municipality is not delivering a clean, safe supply of water, the national government can hand that function over to the private sector. The government has already implemented this in the City of Tshwane where a public-private partnership is taking effect. According to

BusinessTech

, Coca-Cola has partnered with the government to invest R500-million in municipal water infrastructure to stop service delivery from collapsing.


During Cape Town’s severe drought between 2015 and 2018, marked by the

Day Zero Campaign

, water rights groups protested against water guzzlers, and the soft drink manufacturer was one of their targets. At the time, Coca-Cola drew about 530-million litres of water annually from the City of Cape Town to manufacture its products. A litre of Coke requires about 2 litres of …

author: ROAPE
title: Who gets to make Ethiopia’s peace?
content:
Ethiopia’s newest opposition alliance contains a remarkable contradiction. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the main party in northern Tigray, now shares a coalition with the Amhara Fano National Movement, although their forces fought on opposite sides of the devastating 2020–2022 war.

[1]

 The Oromo Liberation Army and organizations rooted in Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz also appeared in its founding declaration.

[2]


Announced on 20 September 2026 as the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, the coalition seeks Abiy’s removal and an inclusive transitional administration. Its advertised seven-member composition was soon disputed: the Gumuz Peoples’ Democratic Movement denied membership on 26 September.

[3]


Removing a government requires agreement about an adversary. Constructing the political order that follows requires agreement about something much harder: who may exercise power, how that power will be limited, what happens to rival armies, how disputed territory will be governed, which crimes from the previous war will be investigated, and who has the authority to write the rules of a transition.


Opposition to Abiy may be sufficient to create a wartime coalition. It is not, by itself, a postwar settlement. Events have since altered the military balance. Tigrayan forces seized the airports at Mekelle, Axum and Shire in September, actions the African Union described as inconsistent with the Pretoria Agreement.

[4]

 Britain condemned the seizures and rejected the alliance’s objective of overthrowing the government, while calling for an end to hostilities and renewed dialogue.

[5]


By early October, federal and allied forces had retaken Mekelle after the TPLF withdrew. Their allies include the Tigray Peace Force, composed of former TPLF fighters.

[6]

 On 16 October, Abiy announced a six-month caretaker administration for Tigray, tasked with restoring services, facilitating displaced people’s return and preparing elections.

[7]

 Fighting nevertheless continued: ACLED reported clashes in northwestern Tigray on 19 October.

[8]


These reversals change the immediate question. Alongside the alliance’s claim to determine a transition stands the federal government’s ability to reshape Tigray’s administration through military success. Neither battlefield control nor an electoral timetable, by itself, establishes that civilians can freely determine their political future. Military power can determine who cannot be ignored. It does not automatically determine who is entitled to rule.


A coalition united by a common opponent


The alliance presents itself as an answer to a profound political crisis. Its members accuse Abiy’s government of centralizing power, producing insecurity and restricting political space.

[9]

 Some concerns overlap with independent findings. Human Rights Watch has documented arrests of journalists, newsroom raids and regulatory pressure on independent outlets.

[10]

But opposition to the federal government does not erase the histories separating the coalition’s members.


Fano forces fought alongside the federal side against Tigrayan forces during much of the 2020–2022 war, before entering their own confrontation with the federal government in 2023.

[11]


The TPLF, which dominated Ethiopia’s ruling coalition

 before Abiy took office in 2018, signed the Pretoria Agreement and subsequently alleged federal failures to implement it; the Oromo Liberation Army has pursued a separate insurgency in Oromia.

[12]


Their present cooperation rests chiefly on agreement about what they oppose. Reuters reported when the coalition was announced that its members remained divided over territorial and political questions.

[13]

 These disagreements concern how the Ethiopian state itself is organized. Ethiopia’s constitution links regional boundaries to language, identity, settlement patterns and consent, while protecting communities’ right to self-government.

[14]


The clearest example is the territory commonly called Western Tigray by Tigrayans and Welkait-Tegede by many Amhara claimants. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International documented competing claims, earlier abuses under TPLF-led rule against Amhara and Walqayte communities, and wartime ethnic cleansing of Tigrayans under Amhara-controlled authorities.

[15]

 Hundreds of thousands of displaced Tigrayans remained unable to return when Human Rights Watch reported continuing persecution in April.

[16]

author: Abahlali_3
title: Socialism or Barbarism?
content:
Keynote address at the Third National Conference of the Aotearoa New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies held in Ōtepoti Dunedin, on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

Comrade Programme director, thank you for welcoming me to Aotearoa once again. May I express my sincere gratitude to the New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies and Palestine Solidarity Network Aotearoa for inviting me to speak here today, and across the country. I bring greetings from Abahlali baseMjondolo, our movement in South Africa which now has more than 200,000 members.

I want to begin with the words of a song, a song about socialism, that is often sung in the struggles of the left in South Africa.

Yini iSocialism? Umhlaba wonke ezandleni zabantu Akunamuntu, akunamuntu ongaphatha umhlaba ngayedwa Ayayesaba bo, ayesaba amabhujwa, nongxiwa Ngoba bona, ngobabona befuna ukusetshenzelwa ngabantu

The song asks, ‘What is socialism?’ It answers that socialism is the whole world in the hands of the people. It goes on to say that no one person can own the world on their own. It concludes that the bourgeoisie are afraid of socialism, because they want the people to work for them.

Comrades, as you will all know, in 1915, during the mass slaughter of the First World War, Rosa Luxemburg wrote from a prison cell in Germany that humanity stood at a crossroads. Either it would move towards socialism, towards global justice and peace, or it would collapse into further barbarism. She was writing as millions of workers were being sent to kill each other in the trenches for the profits of their rulers. Four years later she was murdered.

In our movement we have our own version of this choice. Lindokuhle Mnguni, the gifted young chairperson of one of our branches, the eKhenana Commune in Durban, introduced the slogan ‘Socialism or Death’ into our movement. For Lindokuhle, socialism was not something that would come one day in the future, after a revolution, or after an election. Socialism had to be lived now, in the way we occupy land, ensure that it is not bought and sold, manage it democratically, grow food together, ensure that nobody goes hungry, care for each other, build and manage social infrastructure like halls, creches and kitchens, and make decisions together.

For us, like urban and rural movements elsewhere in the world, building socialism from below means building communes, connecting them and building wider forms of democratic popular power from these communes. In the same way that the liberated zones were the bases for anti-colonial movements in countries like Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau, communes – from South Africa to Brazil, Venezuela and elsewhere – are the strongest bases for our movements to build socialism. As Ruthie Wilson Gilmore says, ‘Freedom is a place’.

The price for challenging oppression can be very high. Many comrades around the world have given their lives. On 20 August 2022, Lindokuhle was shot dead in his home. He was the third leader of the eKhenana Commune to be assassinated in less than six months.

Frantz Fanon taught that ‘Each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfill it, or betray it.’ Comrades like Rosa Luxemburg and Lindokuhle Mnguni understood the mission of their generation, and gave their lives to it. Our generation also has a mission. We are living in a time of genocide, of wealth beyond imagination for a few and hunger for millions, of the far right and fascist forces rising and of the poor being turned against each other. We have to decide whether we will fulfil our mission or betray it. In our movement we have often used Fanon’s words. When people find themselves pushed to the margins of the city and of life, they have the opportunity to discover their mission and to decide whether they want to fulfil it or betray it.

I want to speak today about the barbarism that we see around us, in South Africa and around the world, and about the work of building socialism from below, as we have tried to do it in our movement.

When Luxemburg wrote about barbarism she was thinking of the slaughter of the First World War. Today we are witnessing another mass slaughter of human beings. We have all watched the genocide in Gaza. We have watched children being starved, hospitals and schools being bombed, and whole families being buried under the rubble of their homes. We have watched the most powerful governments in the world supply the weapons and protect Israel at the United Nations. We …
