author: Liza Stephens
title: Students strike against Hanson
content:
For the third time this year, thousands of high school students across the country walked out of class on 12 November to reject One Nation’s far-right agenda. Buoyed by the youth revolt igniting Europe, the protesters drew direct links between their fight and the one against our own monsters here in Australia. 

Students faced a deluge of condescending articles in the media decrying the long-term developmental dangers of missing an afternoon of classes. Minister for Social Services Tanya Plibersek suggested it was just an excuse for students to wag school, "We'll see how many kids turn up if it's a Saturday”. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson said, “These kids really need to get back to class”.

Students proudly clapped back though creative handmade signs which read: “We are skipping class to teach you a lesson” and “The only minority destroying Australia is the rich”. In Sydney, protesters were cheered on by workers at a construction site as they made their way through the CBD.

“Migrants are welcome, Hanson is not” was a popular chant, an expression of solidarity between the protesters and their migrant classmates who are facing the brunt of One Nation’s extreme racism. Minh, a Vietnamese university student speaking at the Adelaide rally, pointed out Labor’s complicity in the increasingly right-wing climate:

“Labor’s tripling of student visa fees and the barring of international student family members is an attack on the rights of migrants. These cowards are happy to appease Hanson while punching down on the rest of us.”

References to the courageous student movements overseas were met with huge cheers. Australian young people connect with the problems driving students in Europe to protest, including having their futures sold off to the highest bidder, the racist politicians who legitimise genocide and then speak down to young people who call them out, and the schools left under-funded while governments hand tax cuts to the rich and billions to the military.

Luca, a high school speaker in Brisbane, spoke to the sentiment underpinning the protests: 

“I refuse to sit and accept the terror inflicted all across the planet by the minority ruling class. We must rise up and join France, Spain, Germany, Serbia and many more in their fight. We all have the same goal, and we can only win if we move together.”

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Protesters condemn state government attacks on Palestine solidarity, free speech
content:
Rallies were held across the country on November 15 to express solidarity with the people of Palestine and oppose repression of speech and protest by all levels of government.

The national day of action against repressive laws was called by Justice for Palestine Magan-djin (JFP) as part of its campaign to repeal the Queensland Liberal National Party government’s laws which criminalise Palestine solidarity slogans including “From the river to the sea” and “Globalise the intifada [uprising]”.

Chris Minns’ NSW Labor government is supporting the Queensland LNP government in the High Court challenge brought by JFP to overturn the laws. Victorian Liberals leader Jess Wilson has vowed to ban the phrase “Globalise the intifada” if elected on November 28.

JFP spokesperson Remah Naji said repression is “uniting our political class” and “thousands of us are united in defending our right to protest genocide”.

“The crimes remain the crime of genocide, the crime of occupation and the crime of apartheid. There is no amount of repression that will distract us from Israel’s crimes or absolve our government from its complicity in them.”

Michael Bradley, from MARQUE Lawyers, which is representing JFP in the High Court Case, said: “Queensland is currently leading the way with its ridiculous law that criminalises mere words, but other states are watching and keen to follow suit.

“It is more critical than ever that a stand is taken — in the courts and on the street — to demand our basic rights: to assemble, to protest and to speak.”

The crack down comes as Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza and the Occupied West Bank, despite the so-called ceasefire. Its strike on the Nasser Hospital on November 12 — the only functioning hospital in Gaza — which killed six people, including surgeon Dr Rizq Shaira and a teenage patient, was condemned by 18 countries for violating international law.

As winter floods, storms and cold descend, many are still left sheltering in tents because of Israel’s restriction of supplies into Gaza. A nine-month-old baby died from hypothermia in Khan Younis in Southern Gaza on November 12 due to exposure to extreme cold.

Israel has killed at least 1610 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire took effect.

Jonathan Strauss reports that 500 people marched in Magan-djin/Brisbane behind a large banner featuring the banned slogan “From the river to the sea”, a frequent chant of the Palestine solidarity movement.

The other banned slogan, “Globalise the intifada”, was not commonly used at Palestine rallies in Magan-djin, but expresses a desire for international support for the Palestinian people.

Anti-Zionist Jewish activist Stephen Heydt told the crowd that “kifah” means “fight” in Arabic. At the end of his speech he and others revealed t-shirts with the “globalise” slogan.

Police soon forcefully intervened, arresting seven people throughout the rally, including Heydt and two women who had carried the lead banner.

Naji said genocide was the real crime, not protesting the complicty of the Queensland and federal government.

The seven arrests add to the 31 previously made under the anti-free speech laws. Some, like Heydt, have now been arrested twice.

JFP is pursuing a High Court challenge to strike down the anti-free speech laws. It is asking for financial support for this and is organising a fundraising event on December 11.

The rally also featured music from a local punk band and a Riff Raff brass contingent.

Pip Hinman reports from Gadigal Country/Sydney that hundreds took to the streets again for Gaza on November 15. They demanded that NSW and federal Labor take action for Palestine, and stop trying to suppress free speech — particularly those speaking up against genocide.

The protest was called to show solidarity with pro-Palestine supporters in Queensland, who are being criminalised for standing up against genocide, and called for the scrapping of bans on phrases which call for rights, dignity, peace and justice for those living between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

Minns wants to bring in similar laws, but is waiting on the outcome of the High Court challenge.

Speakers at the protest included Dr Shamikh Badra, who is from Gaza. He called on the federal government to act for Palestine, and not allow the weapons trade to continue.

Badra condemned the strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza. He said people were still being denied food, medical assistance and other aid, and …

author: Deaglan Godwin
title: Businessmen, not battlers, lead the charge for One Nation in NSW
content:
Pauline Hanson’s One Nation pretends to be a party of battlers, standing up for the little guy against the major parties. This narrative has been parroted by the mainstream media and even taken up by Hanson’s opponents. The party’s lead candidates for the March 2027 New South Wales state election paint a very different picture of who the party represents.

Take Mike Newman, newly-appointed NSW leader and candidate for Cessnock, the Hunter Valley seat One Nation considers winnable. Newman’s riches-to-riches story involves growing up in well-heeled Mosman on Sydney’s lower North Shore and attending the elite private school Cranbrook, along with billionaire James Packer. His father, Maurice Newman, was the chair of the Australian Securities Exchange and then of the ABC. 

Son followed father into the world of investment banking. After a long career as a banker in Tokyo, Newman landed a gig in the public service as NSW Senior Trade and Investment Commissioner in Japan. The wasteful inefficiency of the bureaucracy supposedly radicalised Newman and convinced him to go into politics. Curiously, during his three-year stint as commissioner, Newman racked up hundreds of thousands of dollars in expenses (funded by the taxpayer) for flights, five-star hotels and restaurant and bar bills, as was recently revealed by the

Sydney Morning Herald

. This spending included more than $20,000 for an extended stay in a Meriton Suite in Sydney.

Next up is Jeff Bacon, who will be second on One Nation’s ticket for the upper house. Bacon is the managing director of Oceana Precision, a weapons manufacturer based in Tamworth, his north-eastern NSW hometown. He ran as the lower house candidate for Tamworth with the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers party in 2019, then joined the Nationals in 2023 before defecting to One Nation in October 2025. 

In an interview with Tamworth’s local newspaper, the 

Northern Daily Leader,

 in January, Bacon alleged that every single one of Oceania Precision’s rifles was banned in NSW following firearms legislation passed by the state Labor government in the wake of the Bondi Massacre. Bacon would, apparently, be broke in six months if the laws weren’t repealed. Hanson has described him as her “go-to man on the firearms industry”.

Sure, you might struggle to pay grocery or electricity bills, or cover your mortgage or rent. But spare a thought for the owner of a medium-sized weapons manufacturer whose human rights have been trampled on by the Labor government. 

Stuart Bonds, the party’s lead upper house candidate, is more regularly held up as emblematic of the party’s battler credentials.

Bonds, a former Hunter Valley coal miner, won 21 percent of the vote for One Nation in the 2019 federal election. Bonds is critical of both renewable energy and the behaviour of multinational mining companies. He left One Nation in 2021 over its support for the Morrison government's industrial relations legislation that undermined casual workers’ rights.

Bonds, however, is more representative of your average bigot than battler. At an anti-immigration rally in early November, he espoused the far-right Great Replacement conspiracy theory. He told the protesters that, “we are being demographically replaced inside our own nation”, and warned them that this was part of a “socialist plan” to “tear down the fabric of your civilisation”. 

Bonds is also a bigot on other social issues. Many have rightly pointed out the irony of his misogynistic comments when he boasted: “I don’t have a woman boss, and I don’t have a gay boss, and there’s a reason for that”. The only problem for Mr Bonds is that he does indeed have both a woman boss in Hanson and a gay boss in James Ashby, the party director. Irony aside, the comments indicate the rank misogyny and homophobia that aren’t simply personal opinions, but party policy. One Nation boasts about being “pro-life” and is currently campaigning to restrict abortion rights in NSW. 

One Nation’s NSW state election candidates give you a glimpse into the actual character of the party. Rather than being the authentic expression of working-class grievances, the party is a Frankenstein-like combination of bankers, bigots and small business owners. What unites them is not their genuine struggles under the system, but their hostility to the gains made by oppressed groups and minorities, hatred of the left and commitment to a pro-business economic agenda.

title: Gıdada yangın sönmüyor: Vatandaş sofrasına koyamadığı Erzurum tulumunu anıyor
content:
Ankara — Gıda fiyatları malum uzun zamandır cep yakıyor. Batıkent’te Andaç Kapalı Pazarı ve Ankara Toptancı Halinde gıdayı kiloyla satın alımları bıraktığını söyleyen yurttaşlardan kimi en sevdiği peynir çeşidi olan tulumu alamadığından dert yanarken, kimi ise ilacı veresiye alabildiğini anlattı. Pazar esnafı ise eskisi gibi satış yapamadıklarını, büyük marketlerle baş etmekte zorluk yaşadıklarını söyledi. Hal esnafı ve emekçileri ise 2012’de çıkarılan, şimdilerde değişikliğe gidilecek olan Hal Kanunu’na dair, “Halde çöpe giden ürünler oluyor. İnsanlar halin kapanma saatlerinde gelip o ürünleri seçerek seyyar tezgahlarda satıyor. Bazıları alıp evine götürüyor. Hangi yasayla düzelteceksin bunu?” dedi.

Andaç Kapalı Pazarında limon 40 TL, istavrit 150 TL, mandalina 75 TL, havuç 50 TL, patates 40 TL, soğan 30 TL, domates 70 TL. Tezgahlar arasında 20-30 lira arasında fiyat oynamaları var.

Evlerine tek bir maaş girdiğini söyleyen bir vatandaş, “Ucuz, bozuk ürün almak istemiyorum ama iyisini de alamıyorum. Ucuz olan çoğu kez çürük çıkıyor. Bütçeme göre davranıyorum” dedi. Uzun zamandır evine muz almadığını söyleyen aynı vatandaş, “Çünkü çok pahalı. Sadece temel sebzeleri ve meyveleri tercih ettiğim bir pazar alışverişi aylık neredeyse 15 bin lira tutuyor. Ayda bir kilo et ya da kıyma alıyorum. Onu da parçalara bölüp ay boyunca azar azar yemeklerde kullanıyorum” dedi.

Geçmişle bugün arasında fiyatları da kıyaslayarak, “eskiden 20-25 liraya aldığım peynirin kilogramı şimdi 250-300 lira. Erzurum tulum peynirini çok severim fakat onun yerine ucuz olduğu için süzme peynir alabiliyorum” dedi.

Sadettin Koçer adlı emekli bir vatandaş yaşadığı geçim zorluğunu anlattı: “Eskiden bir üründen iki kilo alırdım artık alamıyorum. Yarım kiloya param yetmediğinde tane usulü alıyorum. En ucuzunu bulmaya çalışıyorum. Fon mağduru değilim fakat bizim paralarımızdan milyarları çaldılar. 80 yaşındayım 4 ilaç kullanıyorum ve kullandığım ilaçların tamamını devlet ödemiyor. Eczanelerden ilaç alırken de problem yaşıyorum. İlaç parasını ancak ilacı aldıktan 1-2 hafta sonra ödeyebiliyorum.”

Bir başka vatandaş ise, ailesinin çiftçi olduğunu tezgahta yer alan sebze ve meyvelerin nasıl yetiştirildiğini bildiğini söyledi: “Bu hükümet hangi problemi çözmüş de gıda enflasyonunu çözecek? 50 yıl önce babam tarla sürmek için hayvanları kullanırdı, mazot fiyatlarındaki artış yüzünden atla tarla sürmeye çalışan insanların haberleri çıktı” dedi.

Pazarda balık satan Eren Deniz her balığı tezgahına koyamadığını söyledi. Deniz, “Balıkta hangisi ucuzsa o satılıyor fakat yine de satışlar düşük. 250 gram hamsi alan müşteriler var. Günlük satışlarımızdan sıcak para geliyor ancak günümüzü kurtarıyor” dedi.

Pazarcı Burhan Çeyil, kendi cephesinden anlatıyor: “Müşterinin alım gücü olmayınca 30 kasa getirdiğim domatesi artık 10 kasa getiriyorum. İşçi, mazot, nakliye ücretlerini daha az ürün satarak çıkarmaya çalışıyoruz. Domatesin haldeki fiyatı 40-70 lira arasında değişiyor. Ben 60 liradan satıyorum. Rekabet için kâr marjını düşürüyoruz. Zaten artık pazara gelen müşteri profili çoğunlukla yoksul, emekli ve yaşlılardan oluşuyor. Alım gücü yok. Bazı ürünler çöpe gidiyor. Akşamları pazar kalktıktan sonra o çöpten ürünleri alanlar oluyor.”

50 yıldır pazar tezgahı kurduğunu söyleyen Zeynel Güvercin, “Halden patatesi 35, soğanı 20 liradan alıyorum. Patatesi 50 liradan, soğanı ise 30 liraya satıyorum. Bana fazla kâr kalmıyor. Günümü kurtarabiliyorum. Günde ortalama 500-600 kilo patates satıyordum şimdi müşterilerin çoğu sayıyla alıyor. Saat öğlen 3 oldu ben daha 25-30 kilo patatesi ancak satabildim. Ben de et almayı geçtim artık zeytini bile 100-200 liralık alabiliyorum” diye konuştu.

Pazarcı Osman Şahin satışların azalmasında ithal ürünlerin olumsuz etkisi olduğunu düşünüyor: “Büyük marketlerin ithal ürün getirmesi fiyatları etkiliyor. Aynı zamanda insanlar kredi kartıyla alışveriş tercih ediyor çünkü kartın ödemesi 1 ay sonra geliyor. Durum böyle olunca insanlar marketleri daha çok tercih ediyor. Biz de rekabet edebilmek için fiyatları düşürüyoruz. Enflasyondan dolayı insanlar artık ürün kalitesine değil, ürünün ucuzluğuna bakıyor. Şu an temel sebze ve meyveden 1’er kilo alsa bir müşteri cebinden en az 2-3 bin lira çıkacak. Ayda 4 kez pazar alışverişi yapan birinin cebinden çıkan para 8-12 bin lira oluyor. Bu pahalılıkta insanlar nasıl geçinecek? Biz nasıl geçineceğiz?”

author: Clare Hymer
title: The Workers Who Made GTA 6 Are Voting on Whether to Form a Union
content:
UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are voting on whether to recognise a union in their workplace, as the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to break records.


The ballot of around 1,600 workers runs from 12 to 26 November and could lead to the creation of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, which would be the biggest in the UK video games sector.


Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar, told Novara Media that game workers were being dragged into “a future of uncertainty”, and that the ballot was their chance to regain some control.


“As Rockstar workers we build games that set the industry standard. It’s time for us to build a workplace that does the same,” he said

.


The vote comes as the games giant faces an employment tribunal over the dismissal of dozens of workers.


Rockstar sacked 31 UK-based union members without warning in October 2025, in a move the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain (IWGB) called “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry”. 


The firm denied this allegation, claiming the workers were dismissed for leaking confidential information. The IWGB insists workers “only communicated in private and legally-protected trade union channels”. 


In June,

Rockstar lost a legal battle

 to stop fired workers from pursuing claims that the firm blacklisted them. Closing submissions for the employment tribunal are scheduled for 17 and 18 November – although a ruling could take weeks.


Jack Hoxby, a sacked worker and claimant in the tribunal, told Novara Media that he and other colleagues had been organising to try and give Rockstar workers a say over their working conditions. “We never imagined that doing so would cost us our jobs,” he said.  


GTA 6, which will be released on Thursday, is the first new game in the GTA franchise in 13 years and is set to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time. Anticipation is so high that researchers expect another outbreak of

“GTA flu”

, whereby workers take time off to play the game. 


The UK video games sector has historically had few trade unions. If unionisation efforts are successful, Rockstar would become the second UK games studio with a recognised union – following ZA/UM in October 2025 – in a breakthrough workers hope could boost unionisation efforts across the rest of the industry.


Hoxby said that regardless of the outcome of the tribunal, “more and more people across the sector are building unions… Whilst a ruling in our favour would be a form of justice for us, that wave of organisation is a victory for everyone.”

author: CNT Sevilla
title: Victoria sindical: condena a Transportes Nieves por vulneración del derecho de huelga
content:
Nueva victoria sindical en Sevilla

.

CNT doblega a transportes Nieves ante los tribunales por vulnerar el derecho de huelga.


Un Juzgado de los Social de Sevilla ha declarado la nulidad radical de las prácticas de esquirolaje interno llevadas a cabo por la empresa Transportes Nieves S.A. durante la huelga indefinida en el Bloque Logístico de Huévar del Aljarafe. La sentencia condena de forma contundente a la empresa por pisotear los derechos fundamentales de la clase trabajadora.


CNT Sevilla ha sumado un nuevo golpe judicial contra la impunidad patronal en el sector del transporte. El Juzgado de lo Social de Sevilla ha dictado sentencia estimando la demanda interpuesta por nuestro sindicato, ratificando punto por punto lo que veníamos denunciando en la calle y ante la Inspección de Trabajo:

las vulneraciones de los derechos fundamentales se pagan y la acción sindical combativa no se puede neutralizar.


Los derechos fundamentales se pagan y la acción sindical combativa no se puede neutralizar


Los hechos: Esquirolaje interno para romper la huelga.


Los hechos se remontan al verano de 2025, cuando la plantilla del centro de trabajo adscrito a la logística de Mercadona

inició una huelga indefinida

 legalmente convocada por CNT. Ante el éxito de la convocatoria y la paralización total de la actividad, la dirección de Transportes Nieves, de manera fraudulenta y abusiva, optó por desplazar a trabajadores de otros centros y provincia ajenos al conflicto para subirse a los camiones que los huelguistas habían dejado inactivos legalmente, práctica ilegal conocida como

esquirolaje interno

. Una burda maniobra para anular de forma sistemática el impacto legítimo de la huelga.


La justicia nos da la razón: Nulidad de la conducta empresarial.


La resolución judicial no deja lugar a dudas. La magistrada asume los argumentos jurídicos de CNT y las actas previas de la Inspección de Trabajo, sentenciando que

el empresario no está facultado para utilizar la movilidad interna de su plantilla con el fin de sustituir a trabajadores huelguistas.


Cualquier intento de reventarla mediante esquirolaje se encontrará con el muro de nuestra militancia


Un aviso para navegantes: con los derechos de la CNT no se juega.


Desde CNT Sevilla enviamos un mensaje alto y claro a toda la patronal del sector logístico y de transportes de la provincia, así como a todas las empresas frente a las que hagamos huelga.

No vamos a tolerar que se neutralicen las herramientas de lucha de la clase obrera.

 La huelga es un derecho fundamental y cualquier intento de reventarla mediante esquirolaje se encontrará con el muro de nuestra militancia y la contundencia de los tribunales.


Esta victoria demuestra que la lucha de CNT funciona. Conseguimos arrancar un

pacto de fin de huelga

 favorable a la plantilla sobre el terreno y, ahora, rematamos la batalla obligando a la empresa a asumir las responsabilidades legales de sus abusos.


¡Si nos tocan a una, nos tocan a todas!


¡Frente a los abusos patronales, organización y lucha sindical!

Victoria sindical: condena a Transportes Nieves por vulneración del derecho de huelga

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

title: Government invokes ‘bullet costs’ but ignores workers in peace process
content:
The Ministry of Health's proposed budget for 2027 will be discussed by the Parliamentary Planning and Budget Committee today, Monday. Ahead of the discussions, Diren Can Kaya, a member of the Istanbul-Aksaray Branch Executive Board of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES), spoke about the unequal distribution of budget allocations, the resources transferred to private capital through city hospitals and the problems facing healthcare workers.


Kaya highlighted inequalities in budget allocations, saying that a total of 3.3 trillion Turkish lira had been allocated to security and defence spending, while only 1 trillion 196.6 billion lira had been earmarked for healthcare. Kaya said that the budget deficit had reached 4.1 trillion lira and that a large proportion of the budget was being directed towards interest payments and security policies.


 


Even during the peace process, workers have not benefited from the budget


Kaya recalled that the government's response to their demand for “A budget for health and education, not war” in previous years had been to ask, “Do you know how much a bullet costs?” Referring to figures released by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance, Kaya emphasised the importance of the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


Kaya said that the 40-year war had cost workers in Turkey 2.3 trillion dollars: “Figures released by the Ministry of Finance show that 2.3 trillion dollars came out of the pockets of workers in Turkey during the 40-year war. Despite nearly two years of discussions about democratic society and peace, we see that the current budget has brought no benefits to workers. Yet these resources could have been used to establish healthcare and community centres in cities, providing services in people's mother tongues, rather than being spent on security policies. Domestic peace can only be established through policies that benefit the people.”


Kaya also highlighted shortcomings in primary healthcare, saying that deficiencies in services designed to prevent illness and provide care for conditions that do not require hospitalisation must be addressed. Kaya also pointed to the barriers preventing sick prisoners from accessing healthcare and said that the budget should be structured to guarantee their right to treatment.


‘The current system creates artificially stimulated demand for healthcare’


Kaya said that while 1.5 trillion liras had been allocated to curative healthcare services, preventive healthcare had not received an adequate share of the budget. Criticising a budget policy focused on treating illnesses rather than preventing them, Kaya said: “What we have is not really a Ministry of Health budget, but rather a ‘Ministry of Illness’ budget. Looking at the budgets over the past three years, we see only minimal increases, with figures of 6.2, 6.9 and 7.2. However, as the Health and Social Services Workers' Union, we emphasise that the existing problems in healthcare cannot be resolved unless its share of the budget rises above 10 percent.”


Kaya also criticised the city hospital model, saying that resources allocated from the healthcare budget through the Build-Operate-Transfer model were being channelled to private capital and what Kaya described as “illness lobbies”.


Kaya said: “With the resources transferred to city hospitals, 300 new healthcare facilities with 600 beds each could have been established. Similarly, the budget allocated to city hospitals over 25 years could have been used to rebuild approximately 900 hospitals. The current system constantly directs people towards emergency departments and hospitals, creating ‘artificially stimulated demand for healthcare’. Patients are being deprived of their right to healthcare.”


‘There is a huge workforce waiting for healthcare appointments’


Kaya emphasised that doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers were not responsible for the failures of a healthcare system that produces illness rather than health. Kaya also acknowledged that the union had not done enough to explain this reality to the public. Kaya said that healthcare workers were among the lowest-paid public employees and that excessive workloads and duties imposed on them were causing serious burnout.

The Guardian has revealed that “israel” uploaded 3.5 million photos of Palestinians into Amazon’s cloud to be run through AWS Rekognition, the company’s facial recognition technology. The photos include the ID photos “israel” forces every Palestinian to take at 16. After the ground invasion in Gaza, the IOF aimed this system at its own checkpoints, where cameras scanned Palestinians as they fled “israeli” bombing and matched their faces against Rolling Stone, described by an IOF soldier as the system “where all the information relevant to the control of the Palestinian civilian population is centralised”. A military IOF source said Amazon’s cloud was used precisely because of the “very large scale” of images collected at those checkpoints, which became sites of mass detention and enforced disappearance, as documented by UN bodies.

Under Project Nimbus, the company constructed a segregated, fortified “walled garden” inside its Tel Aviv data centers for IOF military and intelligence data, and hosted IOF soldiers at its own offices in “israel” as they explored how to run the Gaza facial recognition programme on AWS. Rolling Stone’s plan, in the words of a military source, was to migrate “pictures, videos, all the confidential intelligence information — everything.”

Since October 2023, “israel” has carried out a sustained bombardment that has caused daily suffering and the murder of countless Palestinians, enforced a deliberate starvation blockade, continued bombing Gaza despite the so-called “ceasefire”, and damaged or destroyed 82% of all structures, including schools and hospitals. Behind this carnage, Amazon serves as the technological backbone of “israel’s” surveillance and bombing apparatus in Gaza.

Through contracts like Projects Nimbus and Sirius, Amazon facilitates A.I. targeting systems that use mass amounts of surveillance data to identify and strike Palestinian civilians. When data volumes, including billions of audio files, exceeded military server capacity, the IOF turned to Amazon Web Services (AWS) and its “endless storage” for information on almost “everyone” in Gaza. IOF personnel testified that data stored in Amazon’s cloud was used to confirm aerial assassination strikes, many firing munitions from “israel”-owned weapons firms that Amazon has sold cloud and A.I. services to throughout the genocide.

In June 2025, a UN report formally categorized Amazon, Google, and Microsoft as part of a “joint criminal enterprise” actively transforming colonial occupation into genocide by providing “israel’s” essential tech and A.I. infrastructure. By September 2025, Microsoft was exposed storing 11,500 terabytes of intercepted Palestinian phone calls for Unit 8200 on Azure, and the IOF swiftly planned to move the trove to AWS. A month later, it was revealed that as part of Project Nimbus, Amazon and “israel” agreed to a secret “winking” mechanism: coded payments that alert “israel” of any incoming legal demands or investigations from foreign governments for “israeli” data. Similar to Microsoft, Amazon has engineered a scheme to buy the IOF time to move evidence of its genocide hosted in AWS.

Amazon Rekognition is just one tool in the digital arsenal powering “israel’s” ongoing genocide of Gaza.

author: Michael_1973
title: South Africa’s ANC Is Collapsing. The Far Right Is Rising.
content:
The African National Congress is losing its working-class base. The beneficiaries: parties of the Right. South Africa’s local elections expose the fallout of three decades of economic failure — and the need to rebuild working-class power.

In this article, Zwelinzima Vavi, the General Secretary of the South Africa Federation of Trade Unions, reflects on the rout of the ANC in the local government elections on 4 November 2026.

While the global left celebrates the recent successes of the Workers’ Party in Brazil and the Democratic Socialists of America in the United States, the African National Congress (ANC) has suffered a historic collapse in South Africa’s November 4 local government elections. After three decades of mass unemployment, deepening inequality, corruption, and economic policies that have failed the working class, the former liberation movement is losing its political authority. The principal beneficiaries of the ANC’s electoral rout are parties of the Right, including an increasingly powerful far right that has built its project around aggressive and often violent xenophobia.

With more than 70 percent of votes counted, the ANC’s national share of the vote fell to around 32 percent. The ANC is not expected to retain an outright majority in any major city, and the center-right Democratic Alliance (DA), historically the principal party of the white liberal establishment, is making substantial gains and is projected to become the largest party in most of South Africa’s big cities. Former President Jacob Zuma’s Zulu nationalist uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) is on track to be the largest party in Durban. The far-right ActionSA has made a strong showing in Johannesburg and Pretoria and is likely to be the second-largest party in Pretoria, with the ANC in third place.

The central question is not only why the ANC has lost so much support. It is why the suffering and anger of the working class have failed to produce a powerful democratic socialist alternative, and why the Right has been so successful in presenting itself as the answer to a crisis created by the existing economic and political order.

The defeat of apartheid was an extraordinary achievement. We won universal suffrage, democratic institutions, constitutional rights, and legal protections for workers. Those victories were won through generations of sacrifice and collective struggle, and they must be defended. But political apartheid was defeated while the economic structures inherited from apartheid remained largely intact.

The liberation movement historically brought together different classes and social groups united against racial oppression. That unity was indispensable to apartheid’s defeat. But national identity does not abolish class contradictions. Instead of using democracy to transform the ownership and control of the economy in the interests of the majority, the ANC increasingly became an instrument through which a new elite could enter and benefit from the existing economic order.

The ownership and control of the commanding heights of the economy were never fundamentally transformed. Land ownership remained extraordinarily unequal. The former Bantustans, created as reservoirs of cheap African labor, were never provided with the productive economic foundations needed to overcome their inherited poverty.

Over time, the ANC came to treat the advancement of an emerging black capitalist class as evidence of economic transformation. A narrow layer of businesspeople accumulated wealth, in some cases extraordinary wealth, through access to political power, state contracts, and opportunities created by the Black Economic Empowerment policy, while the overwhelming majority remained excluded from meaningful economic power.

The ANC’s adoption of neoliberal economic policies in the 1990s deepened this problem. The language of economic liberation gave way to investor confidence, competitiveness, and market reform. Brutal austerity, liberalization, and dependence on private investment displaced the redistributive ambitions of the liberation struggle.

We were repeatedly told that economic growth would eventually deliver employment and redistribution. We were also told that redistribution must wait for economic growth and the development of the productive forces. But if redistribution had to wait while productive capacity developed, why did South Africa simultaneously deindustrialize?

We have become what I have described as a “warehouse economy …

The 24-hour general strike that took place on Wednesday, November 11

th

, involving around 4 million people, had its origins in the big protests in October against the housing policies of the Socialist Party (PSOE) government, led by Pedro Sanchez, in alliance with the left Movimiento Sumar, especially against the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal which eventually led to her death.  Rents have risen by 45% and house prices by 68%. Between 2008 and 2015 there were 500,000 evictions. These protests themselves involved millions turning out in many parts of Spain.


Sanchez responded by dissolving his government and calling for snap elections on November 29

th

. He hoped to blackmail the movement by offering a false alternative of supporting the PSOE government, or opening the way to a government of the Popular Party-PP (with its roots in Francoism) and the fascist Vox party.


A movement towards organising a general strike began with the housing movement, especially around the Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos (Tenants Union) of Madrid, spreading to Catalonia. It coordinated with the syndicalist and anarcho-syndicalist unions CGT and CNT (100,000 members and 15,000 members respectively. These jointly organised neighbourhood strike committees, which ensured massive strike pickets on the day.


The leadership of the union centrals UGT, controlled by the PSOE, and in alliance with Sumar, and the CCOO, controlled by the Stalinists, then were forced to swing in behind the strike call, hoping to gain control of the movement.


This is in the context not just of the housing crisis, but of wages remaining stagnant, and rising inflation. The cost of living has shot up considerably, by at least 45%, with big food, and energy increases. In the meantime, corporate profits have risen 40%.


Sanchez used the vote in Congress (Parliament), where a Housing Decree, reforms announced to head off the housing movement, was blocked by the PP, Vox, and the Catalan right-wing party Junts. The PSOE was re-elected in 2023, on a promise to halt the housing crisis. A huge building boom led to a slump, but instead of socialising the huge number of empty houses, the PSOE government sold them cheaply to investment bankers. Promised rent controls and increases in social housing were not enacted, whilst tax breaks were given to the big landlords.


The Sanchez government and its allies in the UGT and CCOO leadership hoped to use the mobilisation to stay in power. However, the four million who turned out on the day, are acting against the policies of the PSOE-Sumar government, disgusted by both the crises in housing and the cost of living. On the day, the various unions influenced by anarchism and anarcho-syndicalism mobilised their members, as did the many neighbourhood housing action committees, which have a membership of 10,000.


Despite the bad weather in some regions, there were massive demonstrations and large blockades in many towns and cities. The biggest was in Madrid, despite teeming rain, followed by that in Barcelona. The strike began at midnight. Blockades were put up on major highways, and large workplaces were picketed. Strikes heavily impacted industries in Madrid, Catalonia, Valencia, and the Basque country, and less so in other cities and provinces.


The railways were completely closed down, with a strike beginning the day before. Big chain stores were picketed and shut down, including supermarkets like Mercadona, Adidas, Benetton, El Cortes Ingles and Zara.


Of course, the forces of the State intervened, with the cops attacking demonstrations and making at least 115 arrests.


On the day after the mobilisation, Sanchez introduced another two decrees that were almost identical to the rejected ones. They were presented to a smaller parliamentary council on Thursday, giving the government a better chance of passing the laws. The first decree passed narrowly and includes a measure extending protections against evictions for tenants deemed by social services to be in a precarious financial or social position, as long as regional authorities cannot offer them an alternative residence. Another measure attempted to reduce real estate speculation by stopping any company involved in the real estate market from buying properties for less than 70 percent of their value.


However, it was rejected. again narrowly, after the centre-right Basque party voted with the right-wing bloc after having supported the other decree. The PP …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Explosión en Remedios de Escalada: la privatización “profundiza la precarización y fragmenta los controles”
content:
El viernes 13 de noviembre una fuerte explosión tuvo lugar en una zona comercial de Lanús que provocó un muerto y dejó decenas de heridos. “Lo que ocurrió no fue un hecho inesperado del destino. Es la consecuencia de una sistemática estrategia de tercerización de las concesionarias de distribución de gas natural en el AMBA desde la privatización que profundiza la precarización, fragmenta los controles del cumplimiento de la actividad, impide un código común en la aplicación de normas de seguridad y subestima la importancia de la capacitación continua y el traspaso de la experiencia acumulada por sus trabajadores”, señalaron desde la Asociación del Personal Jerárquico de la Industria del Gas Natural, Derivados y Afines (APJGas).


 


Compartimos el comunicado de APJGas:


Ante la tragedia ocurrida en Lanús, los trabajadores del gas natural nos expresamos


El viernes 13 de noviembre, en la localidad de Remedios de Escalada, provincia de Buenos Aires, ocurrió un gravísimo siniestro durante la realización de tareas operativas sobre la red de gas, dentro del área de concesión de METROGAS. Debemos lamentar la muerte de un compañero y al menos siete heridos de gravedad, además de decenas de vecinos evacuados o que sufrieron lesiones menores.


Nuestro apoyo, solidaridad y acompañamiento a las víctimas y sus familias de tan tremendo siniestro.


El respeto hacia ellos no implica silencio. Exigimos un pronto esclarecimiento de lo ocurrido, con información transparente y una trazabilidad vertical que permita determinar las responsabilidades en todos sus niveles y un cambio en las políticas que dominan el servicio público de distribución de gas natural, especialmente, en el AMBA.


La realidad nos vuelve a pegar en la cara y las primeras víctimas son los trabajadores de nuestra industria y los usuarios que vivieron con desesperación una tragedia que conmociona por su letalidad.


Lo que ocurrió no fue un hecho inesperado del destino. Es la consecuencia de una sistemática estrategia de tercerización de las concesionarias de distribución de gas natural en el AMBA desde la privatización que profundiza la precarización, fragmenta los controles del cumplimiento de la actividad, impide un código común en la aplicación de normas de seguridad y subestima la importancia de la capacitación continua y el traspaso de la experiencia acumulada por sus trabajadores.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/explosion-gas-remedios-escalada.mp4


La APJ GAS denunció en varias oportunidades las irregularidades y los métodos de trabajo de las empresas tercerizadas como Exgadet que está contratada por Metrogas y Naturgy Ban. No fuimos escuchados por las empresas concesionarias del servicio ni por el Estado. Las consecuencias son claras: las víctimas somos los trabajadores del gas natural y los usuarios.


Lo dijimos y lo repetimos: el gas no perdona. No es un instante. Es un encadenamiento de decisiones que toman las autoridades de las empresas privadas y repercute en el servicio. Nuestras tareas llevan incluidas un riesgo permanente que debe ser minimizado. Tercerizar la actividad para mantener la precarización de miles de trabajadores es un camino de ida que tiene un alto costo humano e impide unificar criterios, sostener una política única de seguridad y transmitir experiencia.


Metrogas y las distribuidoras de gas natural lo saben. El camino es otro. Hay que recorrerlo con urgencia.


COMISIÓN DIRECTIVA APJ GAS

author: anred
title: MetroGAS: una distribuidora, un negocio y responsabilidades que no se tercerizan
content:
La responsabilidad de la muerte de un obrero y una treiuntena de heridos con gravedad en la explosión tras la fuga de gas en Remedios de Escalada no puede reducirse a la empresa Exgadet que operaba la tuneladora. MetroGAS es la distribuidora que tiene a su cargo la red y el servicio en buena parte del Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires. La contratación de una firma externa no la exime de garantizar que las obras se realicen bajo condiciones adecuadas ni de supervisar los procedimientos de seguridad. Los trabajadores venían advirtiendo de las malas condiciones de trabajo. ¿Como operó el lobby Vila Manzano en la justicia? . Por ANRed


La propia empresa cuenta con un Programa de Prevención de Daños que establece responsabilidades compartidas entre quienes ejecutan excavaciones y la distribuidora. MetroGAS debe garantizar la integridad de la red y brindar asistencia técnica durante las obras. Por eso, la investigación debe establecer qué controles realizó sobre Exgadet, qué instrucciones había impartido y cómo respondió cuando recibió el aviso de la rotura.


La actuación de la distribuidora quedó especialmente comprometida por lo sucedido después de las 9.44. Según la reconstrucción municipal, recibió el aviso de la fuga, envió una cuadrilla y no activó el sistema local de emergencias. La decisión de mantener el episodio bajo control de la propia empresa, sin alertar a los organismos municipales, dejó expuesta a toda la población de la zona.


Mientras tanto, el Gobierno nacional avanza con un esquema de desregulación y reorganización del mercado energético que favorece la concentración empresarial y la rentabilidad privada. En agosto de 2026, YPF acordó vender el 70% de MetroGAS a Edenor por 780 millones de dólares. La operación fue impulsada por el grupo empresario integrado por José Luis Manzano, Daniel Vila y Mauricio Filiberti, y quedó sujeta a las autorizaciones correspondientes.


La operación se inscribe en un proceso más amplio de concentración de empresas de servicios públicos. Edenor, que ya controla la distribución eléctrica en una extensa zona del AMBA, busca incorporar a su estructura una de las principales distribuidoras de gas del país. Al mismo tiempo, el nuevo marco regulatorio energético contempla revisiones tarifarias y una eventual extensión de la concesión de MetroGAS hasta 2047.


En este escenario, la pregunta por los controles adquiere una dimensión política. ¿Qué lugar ocupa la seguridad de los usuarios y trabajadores en un modelo donde los servicios esenciales se organizan alrededor de grandes negocios privados? ¿Quién garantiza que la búsqueda de eficiencia y rentabilidad no termine descargando los costos sobre quienes trabajan y viven en los territorios?


La desregulación no significa solamente modificar normas o reducir la intervención estatal. También implica discutir qué controles se mantienen, quién los ejecuta y qué capacidad tienen los organismos públicos para fiscalizar a empresas que manejan infraestructuras fundamentales para la vida cotidiana.


Dos directivos de MetroGAS y una investigación que debe avanzar


La gravedad de lo ocurrido llevó a la fiscal Yanina Estévez, de la UFI N.º 6 de Lanús, a disponer inicialmente la detención de dos responsables jerárquicos de MetroGAS que se encontraban en el lugar. La medida fue informada por el director de Defensa Civil municipal y estuvo vinculada al presunto incumplimiento de los protocolos de emergencia.


Posteriormente, fuentes judiciales informaron que los dos directivos habían sido trasladados para su identificación y puestos preventivamente a resguardo, y aclararon que no estaban formalmente detenidos ni aprehendidos. La diferencia entre ambas versiones deberá quedar esclarecida en el expediente.


La investigación debe determinar qué hicieron los responsables de la distribuidora durante la hora que transcurrió entre la detección de la fuga y la explosión. También deberá establecer quién decidió que la situación estaba controlada, por qué no se dio intervención inmediata a los servicios municipales y qué responsabilidad tuvieron los directivos en la cadena de decisiones.


No se trata solamente de establecer quién rompió el caño. La responsabilidad empresarial incluye la prevención, la supervisión de las contratistas y la respuesta ante una emergencia. Son obligaciones que no desaparecen cuando una empresa decide tercerizar sus trabajos.

author: Stelinsky
title: Ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους του αγώνα
content:
«Ο φασισμός δεν έρχεται από το μέλλον, καινούργιο τάχα κάτι να μας φέρει». Δεν εμφανίζεται σαν κεραυνός εν αιθρία και η επανάνοδός του δεν αποτελεί έκπληξη. Αποτελεί βασική δικλείδα ασφαλείας για το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο: Είναι το πιο σκληρό τους πολιτικό εργαλείο, το οποίο αντλείται από την ίδια εργαλειοθήκη που περιέχει και τη δημοκρατία. «Αναβιώνει», πάντα, όταν η τελευταία παρουσιάζεται αδύναμη να διαχειριστεί τον κοινωνικό και ταξικό ανταγωνισμό, για να τις παράσχει εξωθεσμικές λύσεις.

Σε μια συγκυρία γενικευμένης πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, η εθνικιστική ιδεολογία εξυπηρετεί τη στροφή του πολιτικού σκηνικού σε ζητήματα «εθνικής κυριαρχίας» και αυστηρότερες συνοριακές πολιτικές. Ταυτόχρονα, η διάχυση του ρατσιστικού μίσους στην κοινωνία έρχεται να πλαισιώσει τις κρατικές αφηγήσεις περί εσωτερικού εχθρού – διεργασία που κυρίως γίνεται μέσα από τη στοχοποίηση των μεταναστ(ρι)ών, και τις επαναλαμβανόμενες αναφορές περί «συνεχούς επίθεσης και εισβολής», με σκοπό τον αποπροσανατολισμό της κοινωνικής βάσης από τα βασικά αίτια εξαθλίωσης της ζωής της, και τη συσπείρωσή της γύρω από την εθνική ιδεολογία.

Παράλληλα, οι φασίστες αποτελούν τον απαραίτητο παρακρατικό μηχανισμό που θα αναμετρηθεί με το ανταγωνιστικό κίνημα απέναντι στις επερχόμενες κοινωνικές διεκδικήσεις και αντιστάσεις: Μηχανισμός που δεν υπόκειται στους περιορισμούς της νομιμότητας, και με όρους δρόμου, δρα συμπληρωματικά στο μονοπώλιο της νόμιμης βίας του κράτους. Είναι ακόμα νωπές οι μνήμες από τη δράση των φασιστών κατά τα ταραχώδη χρόνια που ακολούθησαν την εξέγερση του 2008. Τότε, αφενός η προβολή της Χρυσής Αυγής από τα καθεστωτικά media, και αφετέρου η στήριξή της και η συνεργασία με κυβερνητικά στελέχη (κυρίως της Δεξιάς) συνέδραμαν προς αυτήν ακριβώς την κατεύθυνση. Ταυτόχρονα, η δραστηριότητά της αξιοποιήθηκε ως «αντιπολιτευτική» πίεση εκ δεξιών, ώστε το κράτος να ενσωματώσει υπό τον δημοκρατικό μανδύα τα προτάγματά της (χαρακτηριστικά παραδείγματα οι κρατικές επιχειρήσεις-σκούπα «Ξένιος Δίας» στο κέντρο της Αθήνας, όπως και οι επιθέσεις μπάτσων από κοινού με ναζί απέναντι σε αγωνιστές). Κατά τραγική ειρωνεία, η κυβέρνηση Σαμαρά, βασικός υποστηρικτής της Χ.Α., καρπώθηκε και την αντιφασιστική «αναγνώριση» ως αυτή που έβαλε τους φασίστες στη φυλακή. Εκείνα τα χρόνια, βέβαια, το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα έδωσε μεγάλες μάχες στους δρόμους, αναχαιτίζοντας επιτυχώς το φασιστικό φαινόμενο, διατηρώντας διαρκώς οξυμένα τα αντιφασιστικά κοινωνικά αντανακλαστικά.

Το τελευταίο διάστημα, η ακροδεξιά ρητορική και ο φασιστικός οχετός αναβιώνουν σε επίπεδο κεντρικής πολιτικής σκηνής, σε παγκόσμιο κλίμακα. Από τις ΗΠΑ και τη ρατσιστική αντιμεταναστευτική πολιτική του Τραμπ (ICE, τοίχος στα σύνορα με το Μεξικό, απελάσεις μεταναστ-ρι-ών), την επάνοδο ακροδεξιών φιλοαμερικανικών κυβερνήσεων σε χώρες της Νότιας Αμερικής (Χιλή, Βολιβία, Βενεζουέλα, Αργεντινή), μέχρι την εφαρμογή αντιμεταναστευτικών πολιτικών από χώρες της Ευρώπης (κλειστά σύνορα, pushbacks, κατάργηση ασύλου) και την άνοδο ακροδεξιών κομμάτων σε πολλές από αυτές (Ουγγαρία, Αυστρία, Γερμανία, Ιταλία, Γαλλία, Ουκρανία). Και φυσικά τη συνεχιζόμενη εξολόθρευση του παλαιστινιακού λαού από το γενοκτονικό κράτος του Ισραήλ, με τη στήριξη και συμμετοχή των ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ-ΕΕ.

Όλη αυτή η διεργασία διεξάγεται με τηναδιαμφισβήτητη στήριξη εκπροσώπων του κεφαλαίου: Ένας από τους πλουσιότερους ανθρώπους του πλανήτη, ο Ίλον Μάσκ, επιλέγει να στηρίζει οικονομικά την άνοδο φασιστικών/ακροδεξιών κομμάτων και οργανώσεων σε ολόκληρο τον κόσμο (Ρεπουμπλικάνοι-Τραμπ στις ΗΠΑ, Εθνικό Μέτωπο-Λεπεν στη Γαλλία, Λίγκα του Βορρά-Μελόνι στην Ιταλία, AfD-Βάιντελ στη Γερμανία, Κασιδιάρης στην Ελλάδα). Παράλληλα, η στήριξη κολοσσών της ενέργειας, μεγάλων βιομηχανιών και εταιρειών προς το κράτος του Ισραήλ, ώστε να συνεχίζει, χωρίς οικονομικό κόστος, το αιματοκύλισμα των Παλαιστινίων, αποτελεί την ιστορική συνέχεια της σύνδεσης βιομηχάνων-ναζί από τον Β’ Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο.

Στον μικρόκοσμο της ελλαδικής επικράτειας, οι πολιτικές που εφαρμόζονται ενάντια στις/στους μετανάστ(ρι)ες (επανεξέταση ασύλων και αναστολή υποβολής νέων αιτήσεων, μαζικές δολοφονίες στην Πύλο και στην Χίο, pushbacks, τείχος στον Έβρο, στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης-κράτησης), όσο και η εθνικιστική ρητορική περί «εθνικών απειλών» και διαφύλαξης της «εδαφικής ακεραιότητας»συνθέτουν ένα ολοκληρωτικό τοπίο. Εντός αυτού λαμβάνει χώρα η αποφυλάκιση του Ηλία Κασιδιάρη, όπως και η ευρύτερη εμφάνιση φασιστικής δραστηριότητας, εν όψει και των επερχόμενων εκλογών: Από τη διάρρηξη στο 2ο …

author: AusDemWeg
title: Neue Broschüre: Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs
content:
Auf unserer Website

www.ausdemweg.net/downloads/

 ist ab sofort unsere erste Broschüre „Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs“ zum Download bereit. Die Broschüre umfasst unsere drei bereits veröffentlichten Texte zum Thema, sowie eine Einleitung und einen Prolog, der auf die Rolle der Sozialpolitik im historischen Nationalsozialismus im Zuge der Machtergreifung eingeht. Falls ihr die Texte auf unserer Website verpasst habt oder nochmal alles in hübschem Design nachlesen wollt ist das jetzt die perfekte Gelegenheit.


Es stellt sich die berechtigte Frage, warum so viel Arbeit und Energie in eine Auseinandersetzung mit der Ideologie einer kleinen faschistischen Partei gesteckt werden sollte. Schließlich hat die antifaschistische Bewegung in der Vergangenheit oft sehr erfolgreich Treffpunkte und Kader solcher Gruppen oder Parteien unter Druck gesetzt. Doch einerseits funktionieren diese Vorgehensweisen bei wirklich großen Organisationen wie der AFD nicht mehr und andererseits bilden sich insbesondere in den letzten Jahren an vielen Orten wo faschistische Strukturen zerschlagen wurden wieder neue Zusammenhänge. Es reicht offenbar nicht die feindliche Bewegung zu zerstören, da sich nach einigen Jahren einfach eine neue bildet.


Der III. Weg ist eine Partei, die bundesweit viele erfahrene und gut organisierte Nazis in einer Partei vereinen konnte. Auch wenn die Partei immer wieder Rückschläge erlitten hat, ist ein stetiges Wachstum der Strukturen erkennbar. Ein Teil dieses Wachstums ist eine immer größere Zahl von Broschüren und Büchern im parteieigenen Onlineshop. Aktuell sind dort zehn Bücher und vier Broschüren erhältlich, wobei auch einige Schriften fehlen. Es wäre demnach ein Fehler der Partei wie der lokalen Kameradschaft eine mangelnde theoretische Grundlage zu unterstellen. Auch in den Reden und den Beiträgen in den sozialen Medien zeigt sich, dass diese theoretische Grundlage durchaus Anwendung findet.


Die Auseinandersetzung mit den Schriften der Nazis zeigt wenig überraschend eine Vielzahl an Schwächen, die ausgenutzt werden könnten. Dabei geht es sowohl um die innere Logik in ihrer Ideologie, als auch um Grundannahmen und sich daraus ergebende Theorien. Es wäre daher wünschenswert, wenn die antifaschistische Bewegung in Zukunft neben dem Kampf gegen faschistische Infrastruktur und die Aktivisten auch die inhaltliche Auseinandersetzung vorantreibt. Abgesehen davon hilft eine solche Auseinandersetzung mit den Positionen des Gegners auch bei der Schärfung der eignen politischen Vorstellungen. All das kann der antifaschistischen Bewegung nur gut tun.

author: CNT Galiza
title: 20 de noviembre. Combatir el fascismo desde su raíz
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

Combatir el fascismo desde su raíz. Cuatro paradigmas de opresión.


Desde CEAG consideramos necesario organizar este evento, donde contaremos con cuatro expertos en diferentes áreas para descifrar algunas claves del discurso fascista. Ofreciendo una perspectiva multidisciplinaria, abordaremos los aspectos más importantes para enfrentarlo desde una posición crítica y de clase. Hablaremos sobre los problemas que atraviesa la clase trabajadora desde una perspectiva laboral-legal, feminista y comprometida con la causa palestina.


En las ponencias, cuatro personas de diferentes ámbitos de la militancia explicarán, desde su experiencia y conocimiento en sus respectivas áreas de lucha, un aspecto muy concreto de la expansión de nuevas formas de autoritarismo dentro del capitalismo: cómo las ideas de los opresores han permeado la lógica de pensamiento de los pueblos oprimidos y sus organizaciones.


Este es un primer acercamiento desde ámbitos específicos de la militancia: la lucha contra el genocidio palestino, la lucha de clases, la lucha feminista y la lucha LGTBI+.


No se pretende agotar el análisis de estas manifestaciones de resistencia, ni ofrecer en esta primera conferencia un enfoque global y abstracto: buscamos realizar una primera aproximación, desde la perspectiva de estas luchas concretas, al cambio de mentalidad que se observa en las personas y en las propias organizaciones de izquierda, a la existencia o no de permeabilidad de las ideas del opresor en la mente de los oprimidos.


Queremos que sea una primera línea de un análisis más amplio y global, pero partiendo de las impresiones de la experiencia, con cuatro ejemplos para un diagnóstico.


Hace 90 años, la clase trabajadora inició una lucha contra la reacción fascista que aún continúa. Para combatirla, comprender los cambios que se están produciendo debe ser, y es, una misión prioritaria para todos nosotros.


Situados en un momento histórico, tenemos la oportunidad de cambiar el rumbo de la situación.


Por lo tanto, les invitamos a participar en la charla en la que habrá espacio para el debate el próximo viernes 20 de noviembre en la Casa do taberneiro (Rúa de San Pedro, 15, Santiago de Compostela) a las 19:00 horas. ¡Asiste y difunde!


Galego

Combater o fascismo de raiz. Catro paradigmas da opresión


Desde o CEAG cremos necesario orgnanizar este acto onde contaremos con 4 expertos en diferentes áreas para poder descifrar algunhas claves do discurso fascista. Ofrecendo unha perspectiva multidisplinar cubriremos os aspectos máis importantes para facerlle fronte desde unha postura crítica e de clase. Falaremos sobre as problemáticas que atravesa a clase traballadora desde un punto de vista xurídico-laboral, feminista e comprometido coa causa palestina.


Nas palestras, catro persoas de diferentes ámbitos de militancia explicarán, dende a súa experiencia e coñecemento no respectivo ámbito de loita, un aspecto moi concreto da expansión das novas formas de autoritarismo dentro da capitalismo: como as ideas dos opresores permearon na lóxica de pensamento das persoas oprimidas e das súas organizacións.

Trátase dunha primeira aproximación dende ámbitos concretos de militancia: A loita contra o xenocidio palestino, a loita de clases, a loita feminista e a loita LGTBI+.

Non pretende agotar a análise nestas parcelas de resistencia, nin aportar nesta primeira palestra un enfoque global e abstracto: queremos facer unha primeira aproximación, dende a óptica de esas concretas loitas, do cambio de mentalidade que se observa nas persoas e nas propias organización de esquerdas, da existencia ou non de permeablidade das ideas do opresor na mente das persoas oprimidas.

Queremos que sexa unha primeira liña dunha análise máis ampla e global, pero comenzando coas impresións da experiencia, con catro mostras para unha diagnose.

Ha 90 anos a clase traballadora comezou unha batalla contra a reacción fascista que aínda continúa hoxe en día. Para poder combatela, entender os cambios que se están a producir debe ser e é unha misión prioritaria para todas nós.

Situadas num momento histórico, temos a oportunidade de darlle a volta á situación. 


Por iso, invitámosvos a participar da charla na que haberá espazo para o debate o vindeiro venres 20 de novembro na Casa do taberneiro (Rúa de San Pedro, 15, Santiago de Compostela) ás 19.00. Asiste e difunde!

Dossier


Der

faschistische brasilianische Präsidentschaftskandidat

Indische Safran-Faschisten wollen den muslimischen Teil der eigenen Geschichte nicht gerne hören, bei Orban sollen die Kinder auf Panzern rumklettern statt Sozialkunde  und so weiter – da konnte ein rechtsradikaler Ideologen-Verein wie die AFD nicht fehlen: Neutrale Schule nennen sie ihr Denunziations-Programm, erfindungsreich waren sie halt noch nie.

Die Neutralität

 soll dann vermutlich anfangen bei historischen völkischen Idiotien wie etwa der Frankenkönig (und Sachsenschlächter) sei der erste „deutsche“ Kaiser gewesen und enden mit dem Ende des Lehrplanes in bezug auf Nazi-Diktatur und (natürlich, schon aus Eigeninteresse) Kritik an Rassismus aller Art. Erfindungsreicher allemal als AFD-Hetze ist etwa der Protestmodus der fzs gegen diesen Vorstoß. Siehe dazu das allgemeine Echo auf die AFD-Denunziantenkampagne, gewerkschaftliche Stellungnahme und weitere Informationen:


AfD setzt Lehrkräfte unter Druck – Forscher fordert: „Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung“


„Sozialwissenschaftler Tim Engartner erklärt, warum politische Neutralität im Unterricht weder möglich noch gewünscht ist. Er fordert mehr Courage – auch angesichts der AfD-Meldeportale.


Erstarkende Kräfte von Rechts, namentlich die AfD, fordern Lehrkräfte zunehmend dazu auf, sich politisch neutral zu verhalten und berufen sich dabei unter anderem auf den Beutelsbacher Konsens. Der ist seit 50 Jahren die Grundlage politischer Bildung. Im Interview erklärt der Sozialwissenschaftler der Universität zu Köln, Tim Engartner, warum Lehrkräfte nicht nur Haltung zeigen dürfen, sondern sogar müssen, wo Grenzen von Meinungsfreiheit und politischer Einflussnahme liegen und weshalb der Beutelsbacher Konsens angesichts sozialer Medien und gesellschaftlicher Polarisierung weiterentwickelt werden sollte. (…)


Der Beutelsbacher Konsens kennt kein Neutralitätsgebot. Es geht darum, politische Mündigkeit und Urteilsfähigkeit zu fördern – und gerade nicht darum, politische Positionen aus dem Unterricht herauszuhalten.


[Was soll eine Lehrkraft tun, wenn sie von Schülerinnen und Schülern nach ihrer politischen Einstellung gefragt wird?]


Deutlich machen, dass es sich um eine persönliche Überzeugung handelt. Und die Lehrkraft darf den Schülerinnen und Schüler nicht die eigene Meinung aufdrängen.


[Dürfte eine Lehrkraft also sagen: „Ich wähle auf jeden Fall eine demokratische Partei“?]


Ja, das ist eindeutig erlaubt. Sie dürfte auch sagen, dass sie persönlich die AfD für eine Partei hält, die menschenfeindliche Positionen vertritt. Man darf nicht nur deutlich machen, dass bestimmte Werte und Positionen, die von Parteien vertreten werden, nicht mit dem Grundgesetz oder den Menschenrechten vereinbar sind. Man muss es sogar. (…)


Wo genau die Grenze zwischen zulässiger Kritik und unzulässiger Abwertung liegt, ist umstritten – und muss im Einzelfall entschieden werden. Was aber klar ist: Schulen und Lehrkräfte müssen zwar parteipolitisch neutral sein, nicht aber wertneutral. Das ist zentral. (…)


[Kann man denn politisch neutral unterrichten?]


Ich halte das für geradezu unmöglich – und es ist auch nicht das Ziel. Im Gegenteil: Die Lehrkraft soll ihre politische Position durchaus deutlich machen, um Diskussionen anzuregen. (…)


Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung, denn wer schweigt, stimmt zu. Allerdings hat auch die Schulleitung eine wichtige Aufgabe: Sie muss die Lehrkräfte schützen, ihnen den Rücken stärken und darf nicht zulassen, dass Eltern oder auch Parteien einzelne Lehrkräfte persönlich anzugreifen, obwohl diese unsere demokratischen Werte verteidigen

…“

content:
Am Wochenende um den sogenannten „Volkstrauertag“ (

Wir sagen:


Deutsche Täter sind keine Opfer! Wir schauen hin, wenn Nazis Heldengedenken praktizieren wollen, in Neukölln, Köpenick und anderswo!


Antifaschistische Gedenkpoltik statt Volkstrauertag!


Der Volksbund Kriegsgräberfürsorge (VDK) organisiert oft gemeinsam mit Politiker*innen, Bundeswehr, Soldatenverbänden oder Polizei Gedenkveranstaltungen auf Friedhöfen. 1922 wurde das erste Mal der „Volkstrauertag“ durchgeführt. 1934 wurde er von den Nazis in „Heldengedenktag“ umbenannt. Der Inhalt war von Beginn an nationalistisch und militaristisch. Im Aufruf von 1926 heißt es: „Und das soll der Volkstrauertag: Symbol sein und werden für ihren Geist, in dem sie auszogen in unendlicher Begeisterung, in dem sie kämpften wie Löwen, litten wie Märtyrer, starben wie Helden für das große Ziel: Deutschland, Deutschland über alles, über alles in der Welt!“


Der VDK hatte immer Verbindungen zu Personen und Organisationen aus dem Spektrum der Vertriebenenverbände, soldatischen Traditionsverbänden und bis 1987 auch zum Verband der Soldaten der ehemaligen Waffen-SS, der „Hilfsgemeinschaft auf Gegenseitigkeit der Angehörigen der ehemaligen Waffen-SS“ (HIAG).

Nazis fühlen sich aktuell im Aufwind – sie rufen dieses Jahr wieder auf, an vielen Orten, an Friedhöfen oder Kriegerdenkmalen Kränze, Kerzen oder Blumen abzulegen, die Gräber zu säubern, den „Helden zu gedenken“…

title: Women’s Justice and Memory Vigil in Amed: Stories of seven women shared
content:
At the “Women’s Justice and Memory Vigil” organized by the Network Against Violence outside the courthouse in Amed (tr: Diyarbakır), participants carried photographs of women who had been killed. Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the demonstration, chanting slogans including “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), “Femicide is political” and “Stop protecting and exonerating perpetrators, prosecute them.”


Reading the statement on behalf of the organizers, Nermin Unat, a member of the Rosa Women’s Association, said that the stories of seven women who lost their lives in different cities between November 9 and 15 had been added to the collective memory. Unat emphasized that women who had been killed despite filing complaints and requesting protection, as well as those whose families were still seeking justice, would not be forgotten.


The women whose stories were shared this week included Pelin Pınar and Nuran Tay, who died after falling from balconies in Istanbul, Rukiye Demirel, who lost her life in Niğde, and Sema Gündüz, who died in Uşak. The stories of Aysel Sakaldaş, who was stabbed to death by her former husband in the Bayramiç district of Çanakkale; Ayşen Güneş, who was found dead in her home in the Elbistan district of Maraş; and Hanife K., who was shot dead by her husband in the Suluova district of Amasya, were also read aloud.


Speaking at the vigil, Amed Metropolitan Municipality Co-Mayor Serra Bucak said that activities organized as part of the November 25 International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women aimed to prevent further femicides.


Calling on the government to review its policies and take into account the efforts of local administrations to prevent violence against women, Bucak stated that 16 femicides had been officially recorded in Amed in 2026. She also drew attention to suspicious deaths of women, emphasizing the need to investigate these cases and hold those responsible accountable. “We will never give up demanding accountability,” Bucak said.


The vigil concluded with chants following a silent protest.

Wir erleben eine Militarisierung in allen Bereichen der Gesellschaft. Seit langem ist dies ein schleichender Prozess, seit kurzem ein offen ausgerufenes Ziel. Wofür Aufrüsten? Junge Menschen haben keinen Bock ihr Leben und ihre Karriere aufs Spiel zu setzen, um Deutschland den Arsch zu retten. Sie wollen keinen Staat und kein Wirtschaftssystem, was ihnen eine positive Zukunftsperspektive verwehrt.


Wir grüßen an dieser Stelle die Gen Z- Proteste!


Faschismus ist die Herrschaftsform des Kapitalismus in der Krise.


In dem was „Zeitenwende“ genannt wird, geht es um die Erneuerung des Kapitalismus in einer Phase wirtschaftlichen Niedergangs. Diese Phase soll einmal mehr durch Aufrüstung, Krieg und die militärische Sicherstellung der Zugänge zu Ressourcen, auf die es vermeintlichen Anspruch gibt, überwunden werden.


Um die Militarisierung voranzubringen, wird vor allem Angst und Unsicherheit in den Köpfen verursacht. title: Karaköy'den Eminönü'ne kadın zinciri: “Erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulsun”
content:
İstanbul – Karaköy’de iskele önünde zincir oluşturan kadınlar Eminönü’ne yürüyüş gerçekleştirdi. Eminönü’nde iskeleye gelen kadınlar burada, ölümü aydınlatılmamış kadınların hikayelerinden aktarımlarda bulunduktan sonra basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. Açıklamada, “Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

25 Kasım Kadın Platformu öncülüğünde Karaköy'de zincir oluşturuldu, Eminönü'ne bir yürüyüş düzenlendi. Eylemde, 2026-2035 yıllarının iktidar tarafından ‘Aile ve Nüfus On Yılı’ ilan edilmesinin ardından 2026'nın ilk 10 ayında 245 kadının erkekler tarafından katledildiği ve 274 kadının şüpheli şekilde yaşamanı yitirdiğine dikkat çekildi, iktidarın mevcut politikalarına tepki gösterildi.

Eminönü'nde yapılan açıklamada “Kadın cinayetlerinin karşısında yalnızca yas tutmayacağız. Kadınların yaşam hakkını tehdit eden bütün mekanizmaları teşhir edeceğiz. Koruma kararlarının kağıt üzerinde kalmasına, şiddet başvurularının görmezden gelinmesine, faillerin iyi hal ve haksız tahrik indirimleriyle ödüllendirilmesine, şüpheli kadın ölümlerinin karanlıkta bırakılmasına izin vermeyeceğiz. Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

Eylemde son yıllarda hayatını kaybeden kadınlara yönelik bazı saldırılar hakkında da şu bilgiler verildi:

“Fatmanur Çelik, 30 yaşında genç bir kadındı. Kuran'a Hizmet Vakfı'nda sohbetlere katıldığı sırada vakıf çalışanı Ayhan Şengüler tarafından tecavüze uğradı. Ailesi tarafından Ayhan Şengüler ile evlenmeye zorlandı ve evliliği boyunca cinsel şiddete maruz kaldı. Ayhan Şengüler'in kızı Hifa İkra'yı istismar ettiği için yargılandığı davada savcının beraat istemesinin ardından 13 Ocak'ta Anadolu Adliyesi önünde adalet nöbetine başladı. Fatmanur Çelik ve kızı Hifa İkra'nın cansız bedenleri 3 Mart'ta Zeytinburnu Sahili'nde bulundu.

Arya 19 yaşında, TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi İngiliz Dili Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisiydi. 13 Nisan 2026’da kaldığı üniversite yurdunda intihara sürüklendi. Ailesi Arya’ya trans kadın olduğu için şiddet uyguladı, onu onarım terapisine götürdüler. Arya kaldığı yurtta hem yurt yönetimi hem öğrenciler tarafından baskı, dışlanma ve tehditlere maruz kaldı. Arya’nın ölümüne intihar deniyor ama Arya’yı intihara sürükleyen koşulların üstünün örtüldüğünü biliyoruz.

İlayda Zorlu 19 yaşında, Karadeniz Teknik Üniversitesi’nde Uluslararası İlişkiler bölümü öğrencisiydi. Polis, İlayda Zorlu'nun ailesini arayarak 'Kızınız 8 Mart eylemlerine katılıyor, çocuğunuz örgüte katılmış' dedi. Ailesinin baskısına maruz kalan, evde alıkonulduğunu, okutulmayacağını ve evden kaçmak istediğini arkadaşlarına anlatan İlayda, 17 Nisan 2026'da Hatay'ın Kırıkhan ilçesindeki aile evinde, polis olan babasının silahından çıkan kurşunla hayatını kaybetti.

Ayşe Tokyaz, 22 yaşında bir üniversite öğrencisiydi. 2025 yılının temmuz ayında, ihraç polis Cemil Koç tarafından Küçükçekmece’de öldürüldü. Cansız bedeni bir valize konularak katil Cemil Koç’la suç ortaklığı yapan erkekler tarafından yol kenarına bırakıldı. Ayşe’nin ikizi Esra, kardeşini kurtarmak için tek başına mücadele etti. Ayşe yalnızca Cemil Koç tarafından değil, katilin işlerini yapan, cinayetten sonra evi temizleten, Esra’yı oyalayan, sosyal medyadan taciz eden, ifadesini katile sızdıran ve cinayetten sonra çevirmelere takılmaması için katile eşlik eden polis memurunun da aralarında olduğu erkekler tarafından el birliğiyle katledildi.

creekfiend

as someone who has severe sensory issues re: my own hair but who also KNOWS THINGS ABOUT MISOGYNY, I always want to respond to “I shave/wax for sensory reasons” with “me too, but I was encouraged to do that with the hair on my legs, whereas when I removed the hair on my eyelids, eyebrows, and scalp, it got me institutionalized. can you think of any reasons why that might be, bc I have a hypothesis”

people do not like when you say things such as this. i think its a conversation which needs to be had, though!!! like what hair is it considered appropriate and desirable for women to remove? what hair is it considered inappropriate and pathological for women to remove? WE HAVE SOME VERY OBVIOUSLY ANSWERS HERE we just choose not to look at them

“I do it for sensory reasons” is, CHARITABLY, not the end of a conversation. i say charitably because it often is not even fucking relevant. but assuming that it is, ok. and how did those around you react when you began doing this. were you encouraged or discouraged? what would the reaction be if you stopped? what if you removed hair from other areas? what if a man removed his hair for sensory reasons? what would the reaction be? what social pressures might he need to overcome in order to take that action that don’t exist for those of us for whom this is expected?

LET’S GO ON A THOUGHT JOURNEY TOGETHER.

less generously and more straightforwardly because I think many people are missing my point here

“I do it for sensory reasons” is almost never fucking relevant to an existing conversation about the expected removal of body hair in women and is 100% never a relevant response to an existing conversation about SOCIETAL MISOGYNY.

and I would like for those who deploy it as such to do some serious reflecting on why they think it is a reasonable counterpoint in said discussions, rather than a segue into another related discussion about what behaviors are rewarded and encouraged in what people and whether those same behaviors are discouraged and punished in other people. and what someone’s experiences seeing reflected in the world around them might prime them to see certain things as normal (and therefore no big deal to engage in) and others as abnormal (and therefore something that would require an unusually strong individual motivation to engage in)

author: Alyssa Mae Clarin
title: Women, youth groups slam Sara Duterte over sexual advice to women OFWs
content:
One of the places where OFWs spend their rest day in Hong Kong. (Photo by Carlo Manalansan/Bulatlat)

“Instead of holding men accountable for their cheating and abuse, the advice places the burden on women to keep their partners through sexual performance.”

Women’s group Gabriela condemned Vice President Sara Duterte for telling female Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in Hong Kong to be good at sex to prevent their partners from cheating or leaving them, calling the remarks “misogynistic” and an example of “victim-blaming.”

In a video posted online by Filipino singer Jimmy Bondoc, Duterte told the Filipino women in the audience that they should be good at “esmeringhoy,” a Bisaya term used as a euphemism for sexual intercourse, to keep their partners from going astray.

Although the remark drew cheers and laughter from the audience, national women alliance group Gabriela said it should not be dismissed as merely tasteless banter, particularly because it came from the country’s second-highest official.

“Instead of holding men accountable for their cheating and abuse, the advice places the burden on women to keep their partners through sexual performance,” Gabriela said in a statement.

The national women’s alliance said Duterte’s remark reflects the same victim-blaming logic that women face daily, wherein they are made to question what they did or failed to do to supposedly warrant the violence, abuse, or betrayal committed against them.

Gabriela also stressed that the remark is profoundly detached from the realities faced by Filipino women, whose struggles are rooted in the lack of protection, decent livelihood, and respect for their rights—not in any supposed failure to please men.

Read: Citing women’s conditions, Gabriela Women’s Party questions Marcos’ UN statement

“A woman is never to blame for a man’s infidelity,” the alliance further added.

Bayan Muna Youth also criticized Duterte, saying that even when delivered as a joke, her advice to Filipino women migrants contributes to broader public discourse on women’s rights and gender relations.

“Humor does not remove the responsibility to challenge harmful gender stereotypes, particularly in a country where violence against women, sexual exploitation, economic abuse, and unequal domestic responsibilities remain pressing concerns,” the youth group said.

Gabriela urged women to reject the notion that their worth is measured by how well they serve and satisfy men. The alliance also called on public officials to stop dressing up patriarchal beliefs as concern for women.

Similarly, Bayan Muna Youth also urged public officials to move beyond jokes that reinforce misogynistic attitudes and instead push for concrete policies that uphold and protect the rights and welfare of Filipino women.

“Remarks that reduce women to instruments of men’s satisfaction have no place in a government that claims to protect them,” Gabriela concluded. (AMU, RVO)
