author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Harassment won’t stop a son’s search for his missing father
content:
Marklen Lariosa, son of missing Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) labor organizer William Lariosa, speaks during a rally in Davao City on the first anniversary of his father’s disappearance on April 10, 2025. Photo by Kath Cortez/Davao Today

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through.”

Is it a mistake for a son to demand justice and accountability?

Marklen, son of disappeared labor organizer William Lariosa, raised this question following the recent incident of harassment and surveillance he experienced. Members of his family were alarmed after two unidentified individuals were looking for his residence on the night of October 25.

He told Bulatlat that this was the first time such an event had happened since his father, a labor organizer under Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao, was abducted in Quezon, Bukidnon, on April 10, 2024.

Marklen could not think of other possible reasons, suspecting that the incident may have something to do with his continuing involvement in campaigns and mobilizations that demand the surfacing of Lariosa. “Is it a mistake for a son to search for his missing father?” he further asked.

Read: After 2 years, son laments continuing disappearance of Mindanao labor organizer

Neighbors of the Lariosa family in their hometown in Davao de Oro province were the ones who encountered the two individuals. They reportedly wore helmets and were on board a black motorcycle, introducing themselves as “collectors” when they were asked.

For Marklen, the response and presence of the two raised suspicions. Aside from the fact that they visited the community around 7 p.m., which is outside the regular working hours, Marklen said that he did not apply for any financial loan.

After the incident, he was concerned for the safety of his family, prompting them to lodge a blotter report with the barangay. However, he stood firm that it won’t stop him from continuing his cause.

Desaparecidos, an organization of families and friends of enforced disappearance victims, denounced the incident, urging the government to put an end to this kind of harassment.

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through,” JL Burgos, Desaparecidos chairperson, said in a statement.

Rights groups Karapatan and the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR) also expressed strong condemnations about what happened.

Marklen, a member of the National Board of Desaparecidos, has raised a possibility that the two individuals who recently visited their neighborhood might be connected to those who visited their house several times prior to the disappearance of his father.

He said they were visited by individuals who allegedly introduced themselves as state agents once in 2022 and three times in 2023, accusing Lariosa of being involved in communist insurgency. There were warnings, he added, that they would get dragged into it if they would not cooperate.

The series of visits was reportedly the primary reason why Lariosa was forced to take refuge in Bukidnon. Marklen affirmed that his father, who remains missing, had been a labor organizer.

On July 8, the Supreme Court required certain commanders and elements of Philippine Army units to comment on the petition for review on certiorari filed by the family.

Read: Military ordered to reply to missing Mindanao labor organizer’s case

Since 2024, KMU Southern Mindanao has documented 57 cases of human rights violations against its members and organizers.

The labor group released a statement on October 24, presenting the faces of some individuals, including former high-ranking New People’s Army (NPA) member Roberto Rosete Jr., who allegedly harassed KMU’s leaders and members.

Read: Groups decry surveillance of KMU office in Southern Mindanao

Marklen called for an end to any form of harassment and intimidation against families of the disappeared, pointing out that achieving justice is their only goal. (RVO)

author: Coral Wynter
title: Standing with the women and girls of Afghanistan
content:
About 110 people from Australia and Britain joined Amnesty International (AI) in an on-line forum, on September 23, to hear about the human rights group's strategy to support women in Afghanistan. Kathy Allan from AI introduced the forum by saying that when Kabul fell on August 15, 2021, the United States handed over power to the Taliban, after the US Coalition, including Australian forces, had carried out a military intervention into Afghanistan for two decades.

The Taliban has 164 decrees targeting women and girls. Women have been barred from most jobs, and from working with non-government organisations (NGOs). Girls are banned from secondary school and university, parks, gyms and beauty salons. Women cannot speak publicly. LGBTIQ+ Afghans have been forced into hiding.

The Taliban is also attacking ethnic and religious minorities, as well as journalists and human rights defenders.

This institutionalised pattern of systemic domination and oppression based on gender has been labelled “gender apartheid”. Afghanistan is the only country in the world to impose this extreme form of gender discrimination.

Right now, international law has no statute that fully captures this situation. AI is calling for gender apartheid to be recognised as a crime under international law.

Muslima, an Afghan educator and writer, told the forum, “Almost overnight, the door to our classroom was closed. Just because you were a girl, you lost your classroom.

“I never imagined that my future would just mean I stay home ... simply because I was born a girl. Being at home every day felt like a prison, like being in jail. Where do I go? My human rights were wiped out.

“But now I have a computer, my classroom to the outside world. All that I have is a small screen in my room. If they find out, I can face charges.

“Thousands of girls have no access to a computer and internet, but I am lucky. Afghan women can’t talk about their stories, nor can they speak about these issues. Girls of 12 years of age are denied the simple right to education, to learn, to develop their skills, to make friends.

“The Taliban can’t build a strong future by excluding half of the population. Afghanistan is losing enormous [human] potential.

“I want the world to see something beyond our suffering. Women are still writing, working, advocating, creating, contributing and building. If you want to support Afghan women, you must listen to them.

“When the headlines disappear, Afghan women do not disappear.

“So my message is clear: make a space for us to speak. Share our voices.

“Sometimes solidarity begins with something as simple as a refusal to forget. Listen to the voices of Afghan women, who are denied their human rights,” Muslima concluded.

The next speaker was Shaharzad Akbar, a human rights activist from Afghanistan, currently living in exile. She talked about the Peoples Tribunal on Women of Afghanistan, which was held in Madrid, Spain, in October last year and hosted by four Afghan women’s organisations.

They are worried that the actions of the Taliban, as the de facto regime, are being normalised in the region. The Taliban currently have consulates in Germany, China, India and Turkiye, although only Russia officially recognises the Taliban government. Europe is now holding conversations with the Taliban regarding potentially deporting Afghan men and women.

Akbar said, “Women are not able to train as midwives or doctors ... Women will die from preventable diseases because there are not enough female health-care providers.”

Women are suffering from domestic abuse, but it is not considered a crime inside Afghanistan. Emotional, economic and physical abuses are not criminalised. Husbands are allowed by law to punish their wives for any offence.

Women can only go to a judge to make a complaint if they have obvious bruises or broken bones — and face many hurdles to do so. They are not allowed to leave the house alone and a male family member has to accompany them to the court. So a brother or father has to be convinced to support them.

The woman has to relay her message to the judge through a man. If she is believed and she has broken bones caused by her husband, he will be imprisoned for 15 days. He usually returns home only to repeat the abuse.

“We have had increased killing of women, increased suicides of women and a mental health crisis for women and girls in Afghanistan. They don’t see a future for themselves. They are imprisoned in their homes …

author: Bizzi Lavelle
title: Young Women, Pain, Mobility Aids
content:
Stories Contributors Pitch an Idea

To be sick, or have a health condition of any kind is not a moral failing. I know this and I hope that you do too. However, every time I find myself staying in or leaving something early because I’m in pain or I’m fatigued, I can’t help but feel the people around me are disappointed.

People wish they had a friend who could come to their fortnightly event like they said they would. They wish they could book a performer to MC an event without them withdrawing due to spending that week pain ridden in bed. They wish the friend they extended a birthday party invite made it instead of sending through an apologetic message. They wish their friend would be in the room cheering them on at their weekly drag comp or production show.

A common online talking point echoes in my head as I send my latest “I’m sorry” message; you have to inconvenience yourself a little for the sake of your community. You have to be someone’s villager if you want to have a village.

With the weeks or days I spend hidden away, inside, barely leaving the house I often ask myself, do I deserve to be in anyone’s village? Do I deserve my own villagers?

The words to Rina Sawayama’s ‘Bad Friend’ circle my mind as I spend another Saturday night in my pajamas, watching anime in bed: “So don’t ask me where I’ve been, been avoiding everything.”

As I’m lamenting my woes to my notes app and the friends who get it, an article from The Times UK comes across my feed. “Why are young women using walking sticks?” by Katherine Stock. And then another, this time from The Telegraph, “How having a disability became cool” by Poppy Coburn.

The themes of these pieces are misogyny and ableism, with sprinkles of transphobia and ageism.

In both of these pieces, the authors seem to believe that young women in increasing numbers are faking to be disabled for social clout. In the first piece, Stock declares young women using mobility aids and posting about being ill are victims of “social contagion” deems the pain they’re in as “unclear” and therefore “unclear” if these women “really have” disabilities.

It’s wild to me, that in 2026, anyone would partake in such ableist vitriol. Despite what both authors think, there are a wide range of ways to be disabled. Disability and chronic illness don’t always look like a wheelchair user. Sometimes disabilities and chronic illnesses are invisible. Sometimes they’re dynamic. The only criteria to being disabled is having a condition, injury or alike that impedes you and your ability to do day to day tasks.

Disability is the only minority group a person can become part of at a moment’s notice, and is the only minority group we will all be part of at some point in our lives. As my friend, Protect our NDIS rally organiser and activist Oriela says “You will become disabled. That’s a promise not just a threat”.

That one influencer you follow could one day be surfing and the next using a wheelchair or cane. You aren’t able to discern how much pain someone is in by simply looking at them. If that were the case, women wouldn’t be waiting years for their pain to be believed and diagnosed.

For Aboriginal women, seeking medical care has an extra layer of stress. Racial bias in medicine historically saw beliefs that bla(c)k people, particularly women, have a higher pain tolerance than their white counterparts. This, along with classic medical misogyny has led to Aboriginal women being mistreated, ignored or treated as though they’re only ‘drug seeking’.

In Allanah Hunt’s 2024 piece ‘The Good Patient’, she details her experiences of medical racism as she navigates dealing with endometriosis. Despite Allanah’s attempts to present to hospitals as the best and most polite patient, her pain was still disbelieved and she was still treated as a drug seeker. “Because the truth is, no matter how much I’m ‘the good patient’, I will never escape the racial judgement from healthcare providers” Allanah writes.

Similarly, Colleen Lavelle (my mother) discusses her experience of medical racism in her 2017 piece. “Death by racism: bigotry in the health system is harming Indigenous patients’”.

She notes from her own experiences and other First Nations people whose medical experiences she’s listened to that a common thread is wondering if you’ve been overly sensitive.

One memory I have from my teens is when I was at the shops with my mum and younger sister. I went out to the car to put some bags in the car and a man …

author: S. Baum
title: Justice Department Official Who Led Attacks on Gender-Affirming Care Resigns
content:
Brett Shumate is the fourth DOJ official to resign since the midterms after leading investigations that pressured hospitals to end care for trans minors.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Brett Shumate has become the fourth Department of Justice official to join the post-election exodus from the agency following Republicans’ crushing midterm defeat — marking the end of the tenure of a man who helped grease the wheels of the anti-trans machine.

“The rats are fleeing the sinking ship,” Alejandra Caraballo, a lawyer and trans rights scholar, posted on Bluesky, alongside news that Shumate, the Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Division, was resigning.

Under Shumate’s leadership, the DOJ aggressively targeted providers of gender-affirming care, subpoenaing patient records and waging False Claims Act investigations to intimidate hospitals. This caused some major hospitals to end care for trans minors and pay millions in settlements to the government. He was also instrumental in defending these actions in court against claims they were unlawful government overreach.

No hospital or clinic has been successfully sued because it provides evidence-based medicine, but some of them signed agreements with the DOJ to stave off the worst of federal threats: the demand that providers hand over identifiable patient data about thousands of transgender children and their families. Not all of these investigations or deals have been public.

Still, hospitals shut down their gender-affirming care programs for trans youth, leaving care deserts across the country. Lower courts condemned the government’s ploy, with one Boston judge calling it “a fishing expedition.” In a similar Rhode Island case, another judge said the DOJ — under Shumate’s leadership at the time — “has proven unworthy of this trust at every point in this case.”

In June 2025, Shumate issued a memo directing Civil Division employees to prioritize attacks on gender-affirming care, courtesy of the whims of President Donald Trump and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, who was ousted in April. Shumate’s memo announced the Civil Division will “prioritize investigations of doctors, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, and other appropriate entities” that ostensibly violate Trump’s declarations about transgender youth care. “In addition, the Civil Division will aggressively pursue claims under the False Claims Act against health care providers that bill the federal government for impermissible services.”

This largely included providers of wholly legal gender-affirming care, even in blue states — such as Children’s Hospital Los Angeles in California and Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. There is no federal ban on gender-affirming care.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, in announcing Shumate’s departure on X, praised him for “shutter[ing] dozens of clinics” for gender-affirming care.

The DOJ also saw the departure of Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division, and whose firm previously represented “ex-trans” activist Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against Kaiser Permanente for providing gender-affirming care.

Jason Reding Quiñones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, and John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for the National Security Division, also resigned. The department is also reeling from general attrition of staff throughout. The DOJ is not likely to stop pursuing political targets, including trans people and their caretakers and doctors, but if nothing else, the turmoil at the DOJ is liable to make it less effective. Under Trump, “a drastically diminished Justice Department workforce is struggling to keep up with its civil side caseloads,” The Hill found.

“A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.” This may slow down some of the destructive efforts by the DOJ — going after lawful gender-affirming care providers, defending the government from lawsuits over human rights violations. But others question how this might shape the department politically as new hires grow increasingly conservative and less qualified or willing to defy unlawful orders. Other important targets of the DOJ, such as those guilty of terrorism or white-collar crime, may also benefit from less competence in oversight.

A replacement for Shumate has not yet been announced.

author: TGEU
title: Trans Murder Monitoring 2026 shows that every 32 hours, a trans person was murdered
content:
TGEU’s Trans Murder Monitoring (TMM) has recorded 273 trans and gender diverse people murdered worldwide over the past year, on average, one murder reported every 32 hours. Murders were reported across 35 countries, the second-highest number since the monitoring began, and for the first time in Romania and Cameroon. In total, TMM has now recorded over 5,500 murders globally since data collection began in 2009. 


TGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia publishes the annual update of its global Trans Murder Monitoring project in the lead-up to Trans Awareness Week, ending with the Trans Day of Remembrance (TDoR) on 20 November. 


The TMM project counts only reported murders, and monitoring work is getting harder. The total number of reported murders is under 300 for only the second time in a decade, but the violence has not eased. Shrinking civic space, media and state-backed hostility towards trans people, and cuts to funding make it less likely that a murder is reported and recorded. 


Read in:


Portuguese

 ┃

Spanish

┃

Russian


Key findings


273 trans and gender diverse people were reported murdered

 between 1 October 2025 and 30 September 2026 –

one murder every 32 hours

.


35 different countries

 reported a murder –

the second highest ever

. Only in 2024 was the number of reporting countries higher (38).


One in three victims were sex workers (

32%

), who remain the most targeted group

 of all known occupations. 


Echoing the patterns of previous years,

almost all reported murders (95%) were feminicides

 (victims were trans women or transfeminine people), and

three-quarters (75%) of victims were Black or Brown trans people.


The age profile of murder victims appears to be shifting

slightly older

. More than one third (35%) were aged

31-40

 in 2026, while one in five (21%) victims were aged

19-25

 – consistently the largest age group in the first decade of TMM. One in twenty (5%) victims in the past year were

minors under the age of 18

.


Seven out of ten (

69%)


murders occurred in Latin America and the Caribbean

. Brazil leads the list once again, accounting for one in three (32%) of the global total. Numbers continued to fall in

Mexico

, with the lowest reported murders (29) since 2011. However, 2026 saw the highest-ever total in

Argentina

 (16) and the second-highest total in

Ecuador

 (16) since TMM began.


The number of reported murders in

Asia

 (32) fell after last year’s all-time high (51). This year’s total is

likely an undercount

 – some monitoring partners in Asia reported no capacity to provide data this year, citing lack of resources and even electricity.


13 murders were reported in Europe,

the highest total since 2023

 – as many as 2024 and 2025 combined. The

majority of victims were international migrants

.


One in ten murders were recorded in the

United States

 (29), a similar level to 2025 (31).


Two in five (40%) reported murders were

shootings

, while a quarter (24%) were

stabbings

. Three in ten (30%) of murders occurred on the

street

, and one quarter (25%) occurred in the victim’s own

home

.


Of known perpetrators, one in four (25%) were a current or former partner, lover or spouse. Other commonly reported perpetrators were organised hate groups/gangs (15%), strangers (14%), police/military/army (12%) and sex work clients (8%).


A

perpetrator was


arrested

 in only one in five murders (21%) where local authorities documented a response.


Intersectional violence


Year after year, the same demographic of trans people are murdered. Almost all reported victims (95%) were trans women or transfeminine people. Sex workers, who make up one in three victims, remain the most targeted group of all known occupations, and three in four victims were Black or Brown trans people.


This is what intersecting oppression looks like in practice. Misogyny, transphobia, racism, xenophobia and whorephobia compound one another, and those at their crossroads are the ones most at risk. 


“As a Black trans woman and a refugee, I live with the constant fear of losing my life. While others go about their daily lives with a sense of safety, Black trans women must remain vigilant, always watching our backs. Our safety is never guaranteed.

author: Agência Diadorim
title: Partido de Trump apostou milhões em propagandas anti trans nas eleições nos EUA — e perdeu
content:
O Partido Republicano dos Estados Unidos apostou — e muito — em campanhas contra os direitos das pessoas trans para tentar conquistar votos nas eleições de meio de mandato no país.

Até 25 de outubro, o partido do presidente Donald Trump havia investido 183 milhões de dólares em anúncios de televisão sobre questões trans, segundo levantamento da AdImpact divulgado pela Associated Press.

 Foram cerca de 217 mil veiculações em todo o país.


O investimento contrasta com as prioridades dos eleitores.

Segundo pesquisa AP-NORC, apenas um em cada dez eleitores registrados considera as questões trans prioritárias. Já oito em cada dez apontam a economia ou o custo de vida como assuntos importantes.


A baixa prioridade atribuída ao tema, porém, não significa que ele seja irrelevante na escolha dos candidatos. Pesquisa do The 19th/YouGov, realizada em setembro com 2.357 adultos, mostra que 45% dos entrevistados afirmam ter maior probabilidade de votar em um candidato favorável à proibição da participação de atletas trans em equipes esportivas femininas.


Por outro lado, na mesma pesquisa, 42% consideram que os políticos não deveriam se concentrar em questões relacionadas às pessoas trans. As opiniões também variam conforme o direito em discussão: 45% são contrários à proibição ou restrição de cuidados de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade, enquanto 38% apoiam essas medidas. Outros 51% acreditam que pessoas trans enfrentam muita discriminação nos Estados Unidos.


A estratégia republicana, utilizada por Donald Trump em 2024, também foi desenhada para pressionar os democratas.

 Segundo a Reuters, enquanto alguns candidatos tentam deslocar o debate para a economia, outros adotam posições mais conservadoras.


Como a

Agência Pública

 mostrou, a tática parece não ter funcionado. Em

entrevista

, a socióloga e cientista política Gisele Agnelli apontou que a promessa central que elegeu Donald Trump em 2024 — a

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra — “não se materializou na percepção de grande parte dos eleitores. Os democratas exploraram essa frustração com uma campanha essencialmente pragmática, concentrada no custo da alimentação, da moradia, dos combustíveis e dos serviços de saúde”, avalia.


Partido republicano utilizou propaganda anti trans para tentar pressionar democratas e conseguir votos nas eleições dos EUA


Da campanha eleitoral às propostas de lei anti trans nos EUA


A mobilização em torno dos direitos trans não se limita à publicidade eleitoral.

No Congresso norte-americano, propostas buscam restringir a participação de meninas e mulheres trans em competições esportivas femininas, o uso de banheiros conforme a identidade de gênero e conteúdos escolares relacionados à transgeneridade.


Uma dessas propostas, o H.R. 28, foi aprovada pela Câmara dos Representantes em janeiro de 2025, mas não se tornou lei. Outras seguem em diferentes etapas de tramitação.


Esporte, educação e acesso a espaços públicos também estão entre os temas de projetos apresentados por parlamentares brasileiros, especialmente ligados ao campo conservador.


A ofensiva anti trans no Brasil


O Partido Liberal (PL), legenda da família Bolsonaro, é apontado pela

Observatória

 como o partido que mais apresenta projetos de lei anti-LGBTQIA+ no Brasil.


Nas eleições deste ano, a sigla elegeu 121 deputados federais e se consolidou como a maior bancada da Câmara. Entre os eleitos estão Nikolas Ferreira (MG) e Lucas Pavanato (SP), ambos com mais de 3 milhões de votos e conhecidos por seus recorrentes discursos transfóbicos.


Entre janeiro de 2019 e maio de 2026, a Observatória identificou, nas Assembleias Legislativas, 81 projetos de censura escolar, incluindo propostas contra a chamada “ideologia de gênero”.


Outros 70 projetos tratam do uso de banheiros, com restrições ao acesso conforme a identidade de gênero. Há ainda 40 propostas que buscam limitar a participação de atletas trans em competições esportivas.


Na área da saúde, foram identificados 39 projetos relacionados ao processo transexualizador, com restrições ao atendimento de menores de idade. Outros 17 tratam da definição de gênero nas políticas públicas.


Na Câmara dos Deputados, foram apresentados outros 20 projetos sobre atletas trans, 19 relacionados ao processo transexualizador, 18 sobre censura escolar, 13 sobre definição de gênero e 12 sobre banheiros.


Ofensiva antitrans

author: dev
title: Lorenzaccio de David Bobée ou l'insuffisance politique
content:
Acclamée par la critique, l'adaptation de

Lorrenzaccio

 de Musset par le metteur en scène David Bobée nous plonge dans l'impuissance politique de l'Italie du XVI

e

 siècle pour mieux nous renvoyer à notre impuissance contemporaine, c'est ce que raconte France Inter. Adèle Aldokas, y a surtout vu une complaisance narcissique, de l'art institutionnel qui ne critique pas grand chose et un public qui « à la fin, se lève, incapable de se soulever. »


Après le couronnement du bouffon, la lumière tombe et le public se lève pour applaudir généreusement. C'est la preuve que le spectacle a plu et que le public est d'accord : nous n'arrivons pas à nous libérer de la tyrannie, les roitelets se succèdent et la République démocratique reste un idéal.


Mais est-ce vraiment pour cela que le public se lève ?


Une chose est sûre, la performance des acteurs est remarquable. Félix Back est stupéfiant et sa prestation unanimement saluée. Sa présence est délicate, toute en contrastes et de nuances, d'une virtuosité assurée. Et pourtant le début de la pièce est dominé par Mexianu Medenou, dont le charisme et la puissance corporelle fascinent, effraient, révulsent. Les deux acteurs portent la pièce, avec aisance, et on s'émerveille encore de la justesse de Greg Germain (Philippe Strozzi), de Catherine Dewitt (Maria ; Le Cardinal), de Djamil Mohamed (Tebaldeo) ou encore, parmi les autres, d'Yassim Aït Adbelmalek (Maffio ; Capponi). Et c'est sans doute le plus important : ce jeu des acteurs qui fait de la pièce de David Bobée un grand moment de théâtre.


Les fans de Bobée, par ailleurs, ne seront pas déçu-es. Nous retrouvons sa patte et son esprit : une esthétique néo-baroque, par le mélange des techniques, et une approche

woke

 assumée, qui fait la part belle aux acteur-ices noir-es et racisé-es. Un rôle muet est même proposé à Jules Turlet (Pierre Strozzi), et l'homosexualité (auquel invite ce joli mot Valois de Musset : « mignon ») est au rendez-vous.


On aura entendu dire qu'il y avait peut-être un peu trop de son et de lumière, de vidéos, que ça pouvait occulter parfois le jeu virtuose de Félix Back, que ce théâtre regardait un peu trop du côté du cinéma, ou que les beaux chants de Nicolas Moumbounou tranchaient avec son personnage grossier de sire Maurice. On aura entendu dire, au contraire, que cette musique, ces lumières, ces vidéos, ces fumigènes (malgré les crises de toux), rendaient dynamiques et accessibles une pièce que le texte de Musset pouvait parfois alourdir (c'est, on s'en souvient, un « théâtre pour un fauteuil »). L'hémoglobine qui dégouline allégrement plaît ou déplaît, question de goût. La scène de la mort de Louise et même celle de l'assassinat d'Alexandre (adaptée de Sand) ont suscité quelques rires, mais on pourrait invoquer le mélange des genres, en plus du mélange des techniques, un grotesque plus ou moins voulu ou bienvenu. Le tout reste réussi : on ne s'ennuie pas, le public en redemande.


Il faut bien sûr saluer cette présence forte, sans concession, décisive d'acteurices racisé-es et d'un muet. Du reste, on sait, par les quelques portraits d'époque d'Alexandre, qu'il n'était pas blanc. Il est toujours bon de rappeler le métissage profond de l'Italie d'hier et d'aujourd'hui, entre Normands, Lombards, Arabes, Espagnols plus ou moins maures, qui ont envahi violemment Sicile, Calabre, Campanie, loin des migrations du désespoir et des exils pacifiques actuels pourtant stigmatisés. La pièce le clame : le problème n'est pas là, il réside dans la fascisme. C'est le péril d'aujourd'hui.


Pourtant, on peut aussi (et on doit le faire) interroger les limites de ces présences. On aura entendu demander, non sans raison : « cette inclusivité est-elle réelle ? », « Pourquoi n'avoir pas surtitré toute la pièce, si on veut inclure les sourd-es ? » On se flatte de pouvoir mettre en scène des « minorités », mais c'est dans l'écrin d'un théâtre bourgeois. On se flatte d'applaudir à cette « intégration », mais pour qui vote-t-on quand on va voter ? Pour qui travaille-t-on ? Que produit-on et que consomme-t-on ? Que fait-on concrètement, sinon bavarder, comme les Républicains de la pièce ? On est content-e de voir que les Noirs et les Arabes peuvent se produire sur une grande scène, tout comme les Blancs, qu'ils peuvent être homosexuels, qu'ils peuvent bien assimiler les codes de la République, et on oublie finalement que cette République n'en a que le nom, et que ses valeurs, par nature, excluent la vraie diversité …

title: Calendar of Racism and Resistance ( 16 – 30 April 2025)
content:
As anti-migrant, anti-equalities, anti-abortion, misogynistic and anti-LGBTQI rhetoric in electoral campaigning are increasingly interlinked, we reflect this in the coverage below which also includes information on the influence of the Christian Right as well as the religious Right generally.

17 April: Centre-left parties in Italy file a complaint with the communications watchdog against the far-right League, led by Matteo Salvini, for using AI-generated racist, Islamophobic and xenophobic images in its campaigning. (Guardian, 18 April 2025)

17 April: Polish president Andrzej Duda fails to sign off on legislation, approved by parliament, expanding hate crime laws to include sexual orientation, sex/gender, age and disability, referring it instead to the Constitutional Tribunal on grounds that it violates free speech. (Notes from Poland, 17 April 2025)

21 April: After shadow justice secretary Robert Jenrick calls for the legal team representing Hamas in its application for removal from the list of proscribed groups to be struck off, the International Association for the Defence of Democratic Lawyers calls for better safeguards for UK lawyers. Fahad Ansari has since been subjected to racist abuse and Riverway Law lawyers fear for their safety. (X [IADL Law], 21 April 2025)

22 April: Migrant charities accuse Yvette Cooper of pandering to racism in the run-up to local elections as she orders officials to publish data on crimes committed by foreign nationals. (Guardian, 22 April 2025)

24 April: In a campaign speech on the Kent coast ahead of May local elections, Reform leader Nigel Farage demands the government creates a ‘minister for deportations’. (Mail Online, 24 April 2025)

25 April: Following a knife attack at a private school in France which left one student dead and several injured, the mayor of Nantes criticises national politicians for exploiting the attack on social media, adding that the issue is the ‘mental health of adolescents’. The interior minister denounces the ‘savagery’ of school attacks, blaming society for encouraging ‘laxity’, deconstructing order and hierarchy, giving ‘birth to all this violence’. (Libération, 24 April 2025)

26 April: As thousands join an anti-immigration rally in Dublin, Ireland, carrying ‘Irish Lives Matter’ signs, chanting ‘get them out’ and wearing ‘Make Ireland Great Again’ caps, Dublin city councillor Gavin Pepper calls for mass deportations and Conor McGregor shares a video supporting the protest and criticising the government. United Against Racism leads a counter-demonstration. (Irish Times, 26 April 2025)

28 April: Yvette Cooper announces an amendment to the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill which will ban all foreign nationals on the sex offenders’ register, whatever their sentence, from claiming asylum. (Guardian, 28 April 2025)

16 April: Following far-right attacks in France on students in Albi, Nancy and Nanterre, the Solidaire Étudiants union office in Montpellier, and provocations from La Bastide at Bordeaux Montaigne University, students and left-wing organisations form student anti-fascist committees. (Left Voice, 16 April 2025)

24 April: School student Justin P is taken to a psychiatric unit after stabbing four fellow students, killing 15-year-old Lorène, at the Notre-Dame de Toutes-Aides private school in Nantes, France. Students at the school say that the teenager had previously expressed support for Adolf Hitler and Nazism and that he had tried to form a romantic attachment with Lorène, who had refused his advances. (Le Monde, 24 April 2025; Yahoo News, 25 April 2025; La Dépêche, 25 April 2025)

25 April: Jean Messiha, a French far-right polemicist and supporter of Eric Zemmour, tweets in relation to Justin P that ‘the young bastard who stabbed several people in Nantes’ was a ‘radicalised young far-leftist’, adding ‘far-left and Islamised scum, same fight against France’. (Contre Attaque, 25 April 2025)

25 April: In France, it is revealed that Justin P placed a 13-page document entitled ‘Immune Action’ on the school’s digital workspace prior to the attack. An analysis by Contre Attaque says that the document, which calls for a ‘biological revolt’ against globalisation so that ‘the natural balance, however cruel’ can ‘regain its place’ against a ‘globalised ecocide’, is redolent of eco-fascism. (Le Monde, 24 April 2025; Yahoo News, 25 April 2025)

author: CNT Valladolid
title: Fuego al orden colonial: racismos, cuidados, trabajo y derechos
content:
Tengo mu poco dinero

pero no me quita el sueño.

Con dos duros me mantengo,

de mi libertad soy dueño.


El día 22 de octubre, dentro de las jornadas de inauguración del nuevo local de CNT en Valladolid, tuvimos una mesa redonda sobre ‘¿Qué sociedad queremos construir? Racismos, cuidados, trabajo y derechos’. En ella compartieron desde mesa sus conocimientos y experiencias sobre estos temas las siguientes personas, a las que agradecemos su generosidad:


Pastora Filigrana, investigadora y autora de

El pueblo gitano contra el Sistema-Mundo

 (Akal, 2020)


Gabriela Poblet, investigadora y autora de

Criadas de la globalización

 (Icaria, 2024)


Mónica Gortyare, activista de Articulación Antirracista de Madrid y  de Asamblea Regularización Ya de Madrid


Como en otras de estas jornadas, la mesa fue ocasión de abrir unos cuantos melones, que afectan no sólo a qué sociedad queremos, sino a qué movimientos sociales queremos pertenecer y qué mejorar dentro (y fuera) de nuestro sindicato. Pues como sindicato actuamos dentro de unas fronteras que causan desde hace años la muerte de miles de personas que quieren cruzarlas, donde se niegan o regatean derechos a quienes las cruzan, y dentro de una sociedad incapaz de superar la histórica persecución y exclusión del pueblo gitano, pero no siempre parece que nos afecte.


Muertes y discriminaciones ocurren bajo una indiferencia social a la que quizás somos menos ajenos de lo que pensamos, por sesgos, inercias y privilegios que tendríamos que revisar. Porque aunque como sindicato queramos ser de toda la clase trabajadora, es evidente que hay una buena parte de ella, la gitana, la migrada y la racializada, que no forma parte aún del mismo. No se trata de preguntarnos cómo conseguir más afiliades, sino de cómo apoyar y respaldar la lucha de los colectivos racializados que ya existen, que ya militan y que ya tienen fuertes redes de apoyo tejidas. Porque si no estamos todes, no hacemos nada.


Pastora Filigrana, desde su experiencia personal, su trabajo profesional y activista como abogada de trabajadoras migrantes del campo, puso sobre la mesa que el racismo no es una actitud o un prejuicio, sino un criterio estructural de distribución de la riqueza en el sistema-mundo, que despoja a unes y les hace instrumentos del bienestar y el enriquecimiento de otres -igual que lo es el patriarcado-. En este contexto, el antirracismo desde un sindicato no es una concesión solidaria, sino un elemento fundamental para ser inclusivo e interseccional.


Todas las intervenciones subrayaron que no es cosa de recursos o de puertas abiertas, sino de ser conscientes de que bajo el chantaje de la ley de extranjería hay miles de personas excluidas que arriesgan por manifestarse o movilizarse contra los convenios que se les aplican, fraudulentos cuando existen. También se trazó un paralelismo con las antiguas leyes antigitanas, que muestran cómo la legislación ha sido históricamente una herramienta de racismo institucional para limitar derechos, restringir el acceso al trabajo y mantener al pueblo gitano en una situación de exclusión.


Gabriela Poblet empezó su intervención recordando que la colonización no es una cosa de hace siglos, sino que sigue activa en fenómenos como los corralitos de los países de la llamada “América latina”, que evaporan los ingresos de todas las clases populares de un país por el ataque contra los bancos locales de los oligopolios financieros. Un método de esclavización a escala masiva no tan visible como las galeras de siglos pasados, pero igual de abusivo, pues somete a miles y miles al chantaje de la precariedad.


Son estos fenómenos los que incentivan que poblaciones migrantes acaben ocupando trabajos precarizados que no hace tanto eran cubiertos por las poblaciones rurales de los propios países del norte global, también sometidos a un proceso de vaciamiento no hace tantos años.


Es preciso referirse sin eufemismo ni coartadas paternales a estos trabajos de criada u otros a los que se ven empujadas muchas mujeres sin derechos laborales para mantener los privilegios de la población blanca adinerada que puede pagarse ese tráfico, y que no forma una patronal propiamente dicha -incluso amparando la explotación en el derecho a la intimidad de un hogar-.

author: Stelinsky
title: Μικρά μεγάλα εσωτερικά νέα #60
content:
Φραστική επίθεση δέχτηκε στο λιμάνι της Τήνου η πρόεδρος της «Φωνής Λογικής» Αφροδίτη Λατινοπούλου από παρέα Ρομά. Πιο συγκεκριμένα, σύμφωνα με μαρτυρίες, έπειτα από αυτήν την τυχαία διασταύρωσή τους στο λιμάνι, η παρέα άρχισαν να της φωνάζουν ότι είναι ρατσίστρια και έχει μιλήσει υποτιμητικά δημόσια για τους Ρομά. Η ίδια απάντησε πως δεν έχει πρόβλημα μαζί τους παρα μονάχα με όσους παραβαίνουν. Να θυμίσουμε για την ιστορία, ότι σε τηλεοπτική εκπομπή στο Action24, τον Μάη του 2025, όταν αποκάλεσε η Λατινοπούλου τους Ρομά γύφτους (με την ατάκα «Πολεμάμε να φύγουμε από την εγκληματικότητα των γύφτων»), η δημοσιογράφος την διέκοψε λέγοντας «Εννοείτε τους τσιγγάνους, τους Ρομά», η ίδια απάντησε «Εγώ τους λέω γύφτους, εσείς φυσικά μπορείτε να τους πείτε όπως θέλετε». Φαίνεται πως οι δρόμοι δεν ξεχνούν όμως και ο τόπος είναι μικρός. Πάντως γυρνώντας σπίτι της, η γνωστή για τις ρατσιστικές της απόψεις ευρωβουλευτής του βόθρου, φαίνεται πως ειδοποίησε τους μπάτσους για το συμβάν.

Καταγγελία εξέδωσαν κάτοικοι της Αμοργού για επίθεση σε σπίτι με πιθανο ρατσιστικό υπόβαθρο στις 19/09:

«Καταδικάζουμε τη δολοφονική επίθεση στη Λαγκάδα Αμοργού – Στεκόμαστε αλληλέγγυοι στον νεαρό Αμοργιανό, τη σύντροφό του και την οικογένεια του.

Ως κάτοικοι και φίλοι της Αμοργού εκφράζουμε τον βαθύτατο αποτροπιασμό, την οργή και την απόλυτη καταδίκη μας για τη μαφιόζικη και προσχεδιασμένη επίθεση που σημειώθηκε στη Λαγκάδα. Άγνωστοι, κινούμενοι με εγκληματική ψυχραιμία από ταράτσα σε ταράτσα, πέταξαν ενεργοποιημένο δυναμίτη μέσα από το παράθυρο της κρεβατοκάμαρας, όπου κοιμόταν ένας νεαρός μόνιμος κάτοικος με τη σύντροφό του. Το αποτέλεσμα αυτής της τυφλής δολοφονικής ενέργειας ήταν ο τραυματισμός του νεαρού, ο οποίος χρειάστηκε να υποβληθεί σε χειρουργική επέμβαση, ενώ η κοπέλα υπέστη σοβαρότατο ψυχολογικό σοκ.

[…] Είναι μια ευθεία, δολοφονική επίθεση ενάντια στην ίδια τη ζωή, την ασφάλεια και την ειρηνική συμβίωση όλων των ανθρώπων που επιλέγουν να ζουν, να εργάζονται και να δημιουργούν στα νησιά μας.[…] Τέτοιες πρακτικές τρομοκρατίας είναι ξένες προς τις αξίες, την κουλτούρα και την καθημερινότητα της Αμοργού». [Κυψέλη– Σχετικά με τις ρωγμές και τις καθιζήσεις στα σπίτια από τον μετροπόντικα] Έντονο διάλογο έχει προκαλέσει στο κέντρο της Αθήνας το ζήτημα με τα σπίτια και τις πολυκατοικίες που από την άνοιξη έχουν προβλήματα λόγω της γραμμής 4 μετρό που ανοίγεται και περνάει υπόγεια από περιοχές της Κυψέλης. Συγκεκριμένα πάνω στο πρώτο μισό της διαδρομής πλατεία Κυψέλης με Ευελπίδων, έχουν επιβεβαιωθεί ρωγμές, καθιζήσεις, ενώ κάτοικοι έχουν δηλώσει ότι έχουν νιώσει μέχρι και δονήσεις από τις εργασίες. Αρκετός κόσμος έχει εγκαταλείψει τα σπίτια του από το πρώτο διάστημα ενώ σε 25 τουλάχιστον πολυκατοικίες έχουν σημειωθεί σοβαρές ζημιές στα 400 μέτρα διάνοιξης. Παράλληλα, δεν υπήρχε καμία ενημέρωση από τον δήμο ή τις εμπλεκόμενες εταιρείες που να αφορά την εγγύτητα, τα σημεία και το χρονοδιάγραμμα αυτών των εργασιών ως προς τους κατοίκους. Ο ίδιος ο Δούκας σε σχέση με αυτό σε συνέντευξη τύπου στις 25 Αυγούστου με την Πρωτοβουλία Κατοίκων Κυψέλης είπε ότι η «Ελληνικό Μετρό» δήλωσε ότι είχε επίγνωση των ζημιών που έχουν προκληθεί αλλά τηρούσε σιγή ιχθύος ακόμη και όταν έγινε παύση των εργασιών. Ενδιαφέρον επίσης προκαλεί ότι στις αρχές Σεπτέμβρη ο πρώην πρόεδρος της «Ελληνικό Μετρό» Χρήστος Καραδήμας παραιτείται μετά από όλα αυτά τα προβλήματα με τον Σπυρίδωνα Χρυσανθόπουλο να αναλαμβάνει χρέη μεταβατικού προέδρου ενώ οι πληγέντες κάτοικοι τρέχουν ήδη νομικά την υπόθεση και εκθέτουν τον υφυπουργό Υποδομών, Νίκο Ταχιάο που παρίστανε για μήνες τον ανίδεο. Από τις πλημμύρες του θεσσαλικού κάμπου, τα Τέμπη και το τσιμέντο που «αφρίζει» στους δρόμους όπου τα σπίτια μας διαλύονται δίπλα από τις κατασκευές του μεγάλου κεφαλαίου (και εν προκειμένω της ελληνικής εταιρείας AVAX του ομίλου ΑΒΑΞ), το κράτος και οι εταιρείες δείχνουν την πλήρη απαξίωσή τους ως προς την ανθρώπινη υπόσταση. Στον παρακάτω σύνδεσμο η ανακοίνωση της Πρωτοβουλίας Κατοίκων Κυψέλης για το Μετρό: https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1642558/ [Θεσσαλονίκη – Για το εργοστάσιο παραγωγής drones] «Η STARK Defence είναι μια γερμανική εταιρεία αμυντικής τεχνολογίας/ βιομηχανίας (αμυντική τη λένε). Ιδρύθηκε το 2024 και μέσα στο 2026 άνοιξε γραφεία στην Αθήνα και στη Θεσσαλονίκη. Χρηματοδοτείτε από εταιρίες κολοσσούς ανάμεσα στους χρηματοδότες και το NATO Innovation Fund, σε άμεση συνεργασία με τις ελληνικές ένοπλες ομάδες και παρουσία σε όλον τον κόσμο. Η εταιρεία δημιουργεί εργοστάσιο …

author: MissyRedaktion
title: Filmtipps 06/26
content:
Dre (Katy O’Brian) ist gestresst und genervt: Eigentlich will sie in ihrem Club einfach nur eine nice Party samt Drag-Show veranstalten, aber alles geht schief. Zuerst sagt der Hauptact (Dominique Jackson) ab, um lieber Werbung für einen angesagten Drink zu filmen, dann verabschiedet sich ein*e Gogo-Tänzer*in, weil es woanders mehr Gage gibt, und die Toilette ist verstopft, sodass Dres Frau Lizzy (Riki Lindhome) ihr ausgerechnet ihren problematischen Schwager Barry (Quincy Dunn-Baker) vorbeischickt. Als wäre das noch nicht genug, fängt plötzlich eine Besucherin an, andere Tanzende zu beißen. Nach anfänglicher Überforderung und Panik erkennt die in der Lagerhalle übrig gebliebene Gruppe, dass sie sich inmitten einer Zombie-Apokalypse befindet und gezwungenermaßen zusammenarbeiten muss, um irgendwie am Leben zu bleiben.

Tina Romero, Tochter der Horrorgröße George A. Romero, schafft es mit ihrem Film, sowohl das Erbe ihres berühmten Vaters zu ehren als auch – zwischen der nötigen Albernheit und ein paar Jump Scares – die Themen aufzugreifen, die ihr wichtig sind. Zwischen all den handysüchtigen Zombies stellt sie Fragen zu Wahlfamilie, Loyalität und Drogenkonsum und zeigt, dass es immer Verbündete braucht, egal, ob es um den Kampf um Menschenrechte oder gegen Zombies geht. Avan Amir Weis

„Queens Of The Dead“ USA 2025 ( Regie: Tina Romero. Mit Katy O’Brian, Jack Haven, Jaquel Spivey, Nina West, Tomás Matos, Margaret Cho u. a., 99 Min., Start: 29.10. )

Als sich die Sandkastenfreundinnen Hani, Kasih und Saya nach langer Zeit wiedersehen, steht ein Mehrfamilienhaus in Flammen. Ein Anschlag? Saya (Manal Raga a Sabit) wird als Hauptverdächtige festgenommen. Im Dschungel der Behauptungen über ihre Freundin wendet sich Kasih (Bayan Layla) selbst an die Presse, um zu erzählen, wie es wirklich war. Zuvor stellt sie sich den Zuschauenden als Erzählerin dieses Lehrstücks vor und legt mit didaktischem Zeigefinger offen, wie die Biografien der drei Freundinnen als exemplarische Folie für postmigrantische Erzählungen dienen. Ein wilder Mix aus Stilmitteln und Erzählweisen – TV-Beitrag, Animation, Netflix-Serie –, ohne Chronologie und im (scheinbar) hohen Tempo, verstärkt das Gefühl des Kontrollverlusts und führt uns in ein Labyrinth, in dem nichts ist, wie es scheint. Zwischen den Sprüngen in Raum, Zeit und Perspektive bleibt jedoch eines konstant: die Kameradinnenschaft dreier Frauen, die sich gegen Misogynie und Rassismus verbünden und sich jeder Vereinnahmung widersetzen. Milena Aboyans gelungene filmische Adaption des gleichnamigen Romans von Shida Bazyar demaskiert die politische Deutungshoheit über Narrative und kommentiert scharfsinnig die mediale Verwertung von postmigrantischen Realitäten. So macht der überbordende formale Anspruch von „Drei Kameradinnen“ einen gesellschaftlichen Zustand aus Ambiguität und Missständen spürbar, der aktueller kaum sein könnte. Julia Tautz

„Drei Kameradinnen“ DE 2026 ( Regie: Milena Aboyan. Mit Bayan Layla, Manal Raga a Sabit, Brikena Ray u. a., 92 Min., Start: 05.11. )

Jede gute Abiparty muss mit einem Crush beginnen – und einem gebrochenen Herzen enden. Als Farasha (Mariam Dawoud) und Faris (Eren M. Güvercin) gerade ihren wohlverdienten Schulabschluss im Club feiern, treffen sie zum ersten Mal aufeinander und die Gefühle strömen über. Er, groß und mit Wangenknochen wie ein türkischer Timothée Chalamet, und sie, mit großen braunen Augen und einem breiten, niedlichen Lächeln, sind wie verzaubert voneinander. Die beiden verbindet etwas, vielleicht ist es das Wasser, das sie statt eines Wodka-Energy bestellen, vielleicht sind es aber auch die Einser-Abischnitte, die sie als zwei Nerds enttarnen.

Der Abend könnte nicht besser laufen, bis Farasha um Mitternacht nach Hause muss. Kurz darauf kracht es. Ein Autounfall und die Nachricht, dass Farasha gestorben ist. Für Faris bricht eine Welt zusammen. Die erste große Liebe und dann soll sie nur wenige Stunden gehalten haben? Auch Farasha will sich mit so einem Ende nicht zufriedengeben und besucht Faris vierzig Tage lang in seinen Träumen. Voller Herzschmerz und Trauer nimmt der neue Film von Fatih Akin das Publikum mit auf eine Coming-of-Age-Geschichte, die ganz selbstverständlich ein muslimisches Trauerritual aufgreift und dabei das Leben junger Menschen zeigt, ohne auf Pseudo-Jugendsprache oder überholte Klischees zurückzugreifen. Aleyna Dilan Karakurt

author: Mike Ludwig
title: ICE Cancels Deportation Flights for Afghan War Refugees But Continues to Jail Them
content:
Around 8,000 Afghans are at risk of being deported by the Trump administration back to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Attorneys for an Afghan physician and refugee going by the pseudonym Ahmad say he worked as a doctor in support of United States and NATO forces during the U.S.-led war on Afghanistan. Facing persecution from the Taliban after the U.S. withdrawal in 2021, Ahmad fled to join thousands of other Afghan allies who assisted the war effort and were offered asylum in the U.S. under the Biden administration.

“Mr. Ahmad was an ally to the United States against the Taliban and helped his family members escape to refugee camps outside the country,” said Katie Blankenship, a managing operator of the legal aid group Sanctuary of the South, in a statement. “When he fled Afghanistan, he faced grave danger in his journey to the United States.”

Now Blankenship says Ahmad faces the cruelty of the U.S. immigration system. Ahmad has been in the custody of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) since December 2024, when he claimed asylum at the U.S.-Mexico border. Ahmad remains locked up inside the Adams County Correctional Center, a Mississippi prison run by CoreCivic that contracts with ICE, where Blankenship says he is becoming increasingly desperate to be released and receive treatment for pre-existing medical conditions, including a tumor in his neck.

“He’s so desperate to get out of Adams because his health is deteriorating so much,” Blankenship told Truthout in an interview. “I am worried for him physically, and I am worried for him mentally — he is deteriorating.”

Blankenship has reason to worry. Despite claims by ICE that immigration prisoners receive adequate health care, reports of medical neglect within ICE’s privately run jails and prison camps are widespread. A 2025 investigation by Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff uncovered dozens of credible reports of medical neglect, and detainees have staged hundreds of hunger strikes in protest of inhumane conditions at ICE facilities across the country amid President Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

At least 60 people have died in ICE custody since Trump took office, including Mohammad Nazeer Paktiawal, an Afghan special forces veteran and father of six children. Paktiawal fought alongside U.S. troops but died in March shortly after being arrested by ICE agents near his home in Texas. Family members said they pleaded with officers to give Paktiawal his asthma inhaler.

In a November 11 joint statement, Sanctuary of the South, the Council on American Islamic Relations-Legal Defense Fund, the Mississippi American Civil Liberties Union, and the Atlanta chapter of Asian Americans Advancing Justice said that Ahmad should be welcomed to the U.S. and celebrated for resisting the Taliban. Instead, his condition is worsening behind bars.

“This is normal procedure for ICE, to keep people locked up for as long as possible,” Blankenship said, adding that ICE’s private contractors are paid for each detainee under their watch. “The longer they are locked up the more money they get.”

At least 60 people have died in ICE custody since Trump took office, including Mohammad Nazeer Paktiawal, an Afghan special forces veteran and father of six children.

Despite promises made by previous administrations to protect Afghans who helped the U.S. from Taliban retribution, the Trump administration dismantled the federal program for resettling Afghans who served as allies to the U.S. following the invasion of Afghanistan in 2002, in addition to revoking asylum protections known as Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Afghan refugees.

As a result, about 8,000 Afghans are at risk of deportation back to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan, which could amount to a death sentence, according to human rights advocates. Additionally, more than 1,000 Afghans have been stranded at a former U.S. Army base-turned-refugee camp in Qatar since the Trump administration suspended the resettlement process last year.

The As Sayliyah refugee camp in Doha was scheduled to shut down on September 30, leaving the Afghans stranded there with few options but to return to Afghanistan. author: Karen Gullo
title: European Commission Plan to Give Frontex Trusted Flagger Status Is A Threat to Free Speech
content:
EFF and 27 other human rights organizations

called

 on the European Commission today to retract a dangerous proposal granting its border agency Frontex to request that national authorities issue takedown orders for social media content and giving it “trusted flagger” status under the Digital Services Act (DSA), the EU regulation governing online platforms and content moderation in the region.

The extraordinarily improper proposal not only disregards the provisions of the DSA but also places a mechanism of enforcement overreach in the hands of a law enforcement agency that has

failed to safeguard people

 against serious human rights violations at EU borders.

Under the

proposal

, Frontex has the power to “monitor publicly accessible social media content, detect developments relevant to external border management, and support action against illegal online content linked to border-security risks.” Granting Frontex trusted flagger privileges on top of its existing mandate risks creating a powerful mechanism for over-enforcement, stifling the free expression of migrants, asylum seekers, and other marginalized groups. We warned the Commission of these risks in a

letter

.

The DSA is supposed to make online platforms more accountable and protect users’ fundamental rights, not give the EU power to sic its border police on people for exercising their right to free expression.

EFF and other rights organizations have for years

sounded alarms

about potential abuse under the DSA’s trusted flagger provision, which gives “Digital Services Coordinators” the ability to award entities—including law enforcement agencies—a privileged channel to alert online platforms about illegal content. We’ve taken the firm position that law enforcement cannot be trusted to properly flag illegal content. In July, we

told

 the Commission that giving law enforcement trusted flagger status could undermine fundamental rights and said that police agencies like Frontex should not be made trusted flaggers. 

The EU proposal gives Frontex decision-making power over free expression that is not envisaged under the DSA. First, content removal orders can only be issued by relevant national authorities. The DSA does not foresee a role for entities like Frontex to request such orders. Second,

trusted flaggers

 notify platforms of suspected illegal content—platforms must prioritize these notices and they have sole responsibility to decide to remove content. It’s not flaggers’ role to request removal orders from national authorities. Combining these powers blur enforcement and flagging functions, which the Commission’s own

draft guidelines

 on trusted flaggers explicitly caution against. 

“The risk of Frontex utilizing its power as both a Trusted Flagger and authority that can demand removal orders, to surveil user-generated speech, and over-flag content under the guise of  ‘border security risk’ is clear. This will likely result in platforms over-censoring content and chilling the speech of already marginalized groups, particularly those from migrant and asylum-seeking communities,” the letter says. 

We urge the Commission to rescind the proposal. It undermines the DSA, threatens fundamental rights of citizens and non-citizens, and is enforcement overreach that does not align with international human rights standards.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian border guards kill a Kurdish kolbar
content:
Iranian border guards shot and killed a Kurdish border kolbar on 14 November in the border area of Baneh, Kurdistan Province.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that in the early hours of Saturday, Iranian border guards opened fire on a group of kolbars from close range and without prior warning in the Surkew border area, killing 34-year-old Tayeb Rostami.


The authorities transferred Rostami’s body to the forensic medicine department in Baneh before handing it over to his family, who buried him later that evening.


Rostami was the father of one child, and his wife is reportedly pregnant.


Since the beginning of this year, Iranian border guards have shot and killed at least eight kolbars in various border areas of Kurdistan. Another kolbar died this year from injuries he sustained when border guards shot him last year.

author: Mag
title: Ein Flüchtlingsbekämpfungs-Deal nach dem anderen: Deutschland und die EU und ihre »Migrationspartnerschaften«
content:
Dossier


„

Das Treffen des Europäischen Rats am 20./21.10. wird zum Abschottungsgipfel: Unter dem Label »Migrationspartnerschaft« werden Abkommen mit einer Reihe von Staaten in Afrika und Asien vorbereitet. Dahinter steckt eine Auslagerungs- und Abschiebepolitik in neokolonialer Manier. Menschenrechtlich begründete Tabus scheinen sich für die EU erledigt zu haben. In einem PRO ASYL vorliegenden Beschlussentwurf des Europäischen Rates wird gefordert, nach der Schließung der Fluchtroute über die Ägäis nunmehr auch die zentrale Mittelmeerroute dicht zu machen. Auch die Abschiebungen von Griechenland in die Türkei sollen erhöht werden…

“

Beitrag von und bei Pro Asyl vom 20. Oktober 2016

. Siehe ganz unten die Hintergründe im LabourNet und hier dazu:


Abschiebezentrum: Offenbar Einigung mit Ruanda – Befürworter hoffen auf abschreckende Wirkung, Kritiker sehen „Flucht vor jeglicher Kontrolle“


„

Österreich und vier weitere EU-Staaten wollen abgelehnte Asylwerber und Asylwerberinnen künftig in ein Abschiebezentrum in Ruanda bringen. Entsprechende Pläne dürften Innenminister Gerhard Karner (ÖVP) und drei Amtskollegen und eine Amtskollegin aus Deutschland, Griechenland, Dänemark und den Niederlanden laut Diplomaten am Montag in Wien vorstellen. Zuvor hatten bereits der „Standard“ und Reuters über die Einigung berichtet. (…)


Die Teilnahme der Innenminister Österreichs, Deutschlands, Dänemarks, der Niederlande und Griechenlands an der jährlichen Wiener Migrationskonferenz hatte seit Tagen Spekulationen über eine Einigung genährt. Immerhin wurde zur „Vienna Migration Conference“ des in Wien ansässigen Internationalen Zentrums für Migrationspolitik (ICMPD) auch der ruandische Innenminister Vincent Biruta erwartet. Ruanda wird seit Monaten als möglicher Standort für ein Abschiebezentrum kolportiert.


Außerdem kommt am Montag die dänische Premierministerin Mette Frederiksen zu einem Arbeitsbesuch nach Wien. Die Innenminister der selbst ernannten „Gruppe der Umsetzer“ hatten wiederholt betont, dass bis Ende des Jahres ein Vertrag mit einem Land außerhalb der EU stehen soll. Erste Abschiebungen dorthin solle es 2027 geben, wie es bisher außerdem hieß.


Befürworter hoffen auf abschreckende Wirkung


Nach Ruanda dürften abgelehnte Asylwerber gebracht werden, die nicht in ihre Herkunftsländer abgeschoben werden können. Die Pläne sind Teil der Bemühungen in Europa, die Zahl der Abschiebungen zu erhöhen und die irreguläre Migration einzudämmen. (…)


Die EU-Kommission begrüßte die Initiative. Die Vorbereitungsarbeiten der fünf Mitgliedsstaaten seien aufmerksam verfolgt worden, sagte der zuständige Sprecher am Montag in Brüssel. Die Finanzierung von „Rückführungszentren“ sei prinzipiell Sache der Mitgliedsstaaten, aber die EU könnte begleitende Maßnahmen unterstützen, so der Sprecher weiter. Das müsse „von Fall zu Fall und auf der Grundlage konkreter Anträge der betreffenden Mitgliedsstaaten“ geprüft werden.


„Beschämend“: NGOs kritisieren Pläne scharf


An den Plänen gibt es scharfe Kritik. Ärzte ohne Grenzen Österreich bezeichnete diese am Montag als „beschämend“. Abschiebezentren in Drittstaaten fügten „der Serie unmenschlicher Behandlung von Geflüchteten ein weiteres Kapitel hinzu“. Petar Rosandic von der NGO SOS Balkanroute bezeichnete die kolportierte Einigung als eine „Bankrotterklärung gegenüber den Menschenrechten und eine Flucht vor jeglicher Kontrolle“

…“

ORF-Meldung vom 16.11.2026

 


Siehe aktuell:

Das ist euer GEAS 2026: Maskierte kroatische Polizisten prügeln an der kroatisch-bosnischen Grenze 53 Menschen zurück, fünf Schwerverletzte


Siehe zum Hintergrund das Dossier:

Migrationspakt und GEAS: Neuer Anlauf in der EU-Flüchtlingspolitik (???)


Dämpfer für „Return Hubs“: Albanien lehnt weitere Abschiebezentren für Geflüchtete ab


„

Mehrere EU-Staaten wollen bis Jahresende zu einer Vereinbarung mit Drittstaaten über Rückkehrzentren für abgelehnte Asylbewerber kommen. Jetzt winkt Albanien ab. author: anred
title: Embarcación: cuando la destrucción del monte prepara el terreno para la catástrofe
content:
El violento temporal que azotó a Embarcación, en la provincia de Salta, el jueves 12 de noviembre dejó alrededor de 150 personas que necesitaron atención médica, viviendas dañadas, escuelas afectadas y árboles, postes y tendidos eléctricos derribados. Pero detrás de la devastación provocada por las lluvias y los fuertes vientos hay una historia que no comenzó con la tormenta: décadas de desmontes, avance de la frontera agropecuaria y explotación de los bienes comunes que transformaron profundamente el territorio.

Por Adrián Flores, para Red Eco Alternativo.


Salta – La localidad de Embarcación, en el departamento General José de San Martín, fue el epicentro de un fenómeno meteorológico de enorme intensidad. Las precipitaciones, las ráfagas de viento y la actividad eléctrica provocaron voladuras de techos, caída de árboles y postes de media tensión, cortes de electricidad y daños en establecimientos educativos. La magnitud del temporal obligó a desplegar operativos de emergencia y suspender las clases en las escuelas afectadas.


La violencia de esta tormenta también debe leerse en el contexto de los fenómenos climáticos extremos asociados a El Niño, cuya intensidad puede incrementar las precipitaciones y elevar el riesgo de inundaciones en distintas regiones. El escenario del Súper Niño vuelve todavía más preocupante esta situación. Pero estos fenómenos no actúan sobre territorios intactos: encuentran ecosistemas profundamente degradados por décadas de explotación.


Aquí se cruzan dos dimensiones de una misma crisis. Por un lado, un modelo de producción y consumo capitalista basado en la explotación intensiva de la naturaleza, que contribuye al calentamiento global. Por otro, la expansión de la frontera agropecuaria, los desmontes y la destrucción de los bosques nativos, que reducen la capacidad de los territorios para absorber y regular las lluvias.


En Embarcación, ambas dimensiones convergen dramáticamente. La misma matriz extractivista que impulsa la destrucción del monte profundiza las condiciones para que los fenómenos meteorológicos extremos se conviertan en catástrofes sociales. Las tormentas tienen causas meteorológicas, pero sus consecuencias están profundamente condicionadas por las decisiones económicas y políticas que transforman los territorios en mercancías.


Topadoras sobre territorios ancestralesMientras Embarcación enfrenta las consecuencias del temporal, las comunidades originarias del departamento San Martín continúan resistiendo el avance de los desmontes y el despojo territorial.


A principios de enero de 2026, en Misión Chaqueña, una comunidad wichí de más de 2.000 habitantes ubicada a 48 kilómetros de Embarcación, sus integrantes detectaron nuevamente a personas que derribaban árboles y quemaban sectores del bosque nativo. La respuesta fue inmediata: decenas de mujeres se organizaron y cortaron el camino para impedir el avance sobre su territorio ancestral.


El conflicto involucra al empresario agrícola salteño Claudio Ferrari, quien desde 2023 pretende apropiarse de una franja de monte que rodea a la comunidad. Aquel año, trabajadores vinculados al empresario comenzaron a abrir picadas, talar árboles y colocar postes para alambrar la zona. Ferrari sostuvo que había comprado esas tierras, aunque, según el abogado que acompaña a la comunidad, no presentó documentación que respalde sus pretensiones.


La defensa del territorio también tuvo consecuencias represivas. El miércoles 7 de enero de 2026 fueron detenidos Leonardo Pantoja y Marta Herrera cuando se presentaron en un destacamento policial para denunciar la tala del monte y las amenazas atribuidas al empresario. Marta fue liberada, mientras Greenpeace reclamó la inmediata libertad de Pantoja.


La comunidad cuenta con carpeta técnica, relevamiento georreferenciado y registro de Asuntos Indígenas. Sin embargo, sus integrantes denuncian obstáculos para acceder a la Justicia y señalan que el empresario pretende avanzar sobre tierras ocupadas ancestralmente por el pueblo wichí.


No se trata solamente de una disputa por la propiedad de la tierra. Es la defensa de un territorio que sostiene la identidad, la cultura y las condiciones materiales de vida de generaciones.

author: Malik Miah, Barry Sheppard
title: United States: Trump and Republicans routed in mid-term elections
content:
The Democratic Party won sweeping victories in the United States midterm elections on November 3, in a dramatic refutation of President Donald Trump and the Republican Party he controls.

These results were not a vote of confidence in the Democrats but were a rejection of Trump and Trumpism. The majority of US voters do not trust either party.

Going into the elections, Republicans held small minorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

All 435 members of the House are elected every two years and the Democrats won a decisive majority of 254-256 seats with a few results still to be finalised at the time of writing.

One-third of the 100-seat Senate is elected every two years for a six-year term and the Democrats now hold a majority of 54-56 seats.

This is the biggest change in Congressional seats since 1974, when the Democrats swept to victory and Republican President Richard Nixon was driven out of office, in a scandal resulting from him sending thugs into the Democratic Party headquarters.

The Democrats also made sweeping gains in state and local elections.

In Texas, considered a Republican stronghold, Democratic candidate and Mexican American Gina Hinojosa was elected governor — the first Latinx elected to this office in any state.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim ever elected to the Senate, despite facing a virulent Islamophobic campaign against him, where Trump called him a “terrorist”.

Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first African American woman elected as governor in Georgia, in the nation’s “deep South”.

Native American Deb Haaland was elected governor of New Mexico and Minnesota’s Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American elected to the Senate.

The first openly gay Senate candidate, Chris Pappas, was elected in New Hampshire.

In Mississippi, African American Senate candidate Scott Colom leads by a narrow margin in a race too close to call, and in Alaska, Native American Mary Peltola has a slight lead in the race for the Senate.

Eight candidates endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) were elected to Congress, including Chris Rabb (Pennsylvania), Rashida Tlaib and Donavan McKinney (Minnesota), Melat Kiros (Colorado), Angela Gonzales-Torres (California), Darializa Avila Chevalier, Claire Valdez and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (New York).

DSA candidate Nithya Raman won the race for Mayor of Los Angeles, Janeese Lewis George won the mayoral race in Washington DC and Claudia Jimenez in East Bay, California.

The DSA grew rapidly following Donald Trump’s election in 2016 and on the wave of support for self-described democratic socialist Bernie Sanders — who is not a member of DSA. DSA seeks to strengthen the progressive wing of the Democrats and is criticised by the revolutionary left for advocating progressive reforms within the capitalist system, rather than its overthrow. Nevertheless, Trump labels DSA and left Democrats as “communist” and the Democratic Party as “socialist”.

A large turnout from young people eager for progressive change, and from the Black and Latinx communities were key to the Republican defeat.

Black community organisers led in Southern states. They made it clear they were making the elections an act of defending Black people from the Republican drive to go back to “Jim Crow-type” oppression in the South.

There is no mass (even mini-mass) working class electoral party, or parties of the oppressed nationalities in the US and the Green Party is weak. So there is no other choice in elections than between two capitalist parties, and results have to be analysed in that reality.

Some of the main factors for the anti-Republican vote include that the Trump administration is the most corrupt in US history. Add to that the Iran war, Trump’s cruel anti-immigration policy against Latinx communities, and Trump’s tariffs on imports that have driven up inflation, outpacing wage rises and impacting living standards and affordability.

At the same time, Trump and his billionaire friends have gotten richer, as have millionaires and capitalists in general. Trump has increased his own wealth by more than $3 billion and his immediate family by another $3 billion, since he took office in 2025.

Trump’s tariffs have cost working class families, on average, a minimum of $1000 — which continues to rise.

Trump’s war on Iran has made the price of petrol and diesel skyrocket. Farmers, whose equipment largely runs on diesel, turned against Trump …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: ICE-Style Raids Hit Record High in the UK – but Most Result in No Arrests
content:
Immigration enforcement raids in the UK have reached a record high, but most operations result in no arrests.


The Home Office’s immigration team is carrying out more “enforcement visits” than ever before but while these raids leave traumatised people in their wake, the majority haven’t broken any immigration law, the

Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) has revealed.


Out of 23,500 Home Office raids conducted in 2025 – an average of more than 60 per day – more than 15,500 (66% or two-thirds) didn’t result in an arrest. 


The figures include raids on homes and businesses, and spot checks in public places like streets, train stations and ports.


The TBIJ investigation also found that warrants are being used less frequently, featuring in only a quarter of raids compared to 40% a decade ago. 


Experts said this indicates that the Home Office is carrying out “fishing expeditions” based on “weak evidence and hearsay”. 


Kevin Barker, a former immigration officer, told TBIJ: “You’re not allowed to apply for a search warrant if the intelligence you’ve got is old or an anonymous allegation that can’t be corroborated… but it doesn’t stop them from doing the visit.”


Anyone can send an anonymous tip-off, and last year, 80% of tip-offs came from members of the public – compared to less than 4% from both the police and immigration authorities.


In January, home secretary

Shabana Mahmood said

 the Labour government had “

surged enforcement activity to the highest level in British history so illegal migrants in the black economy have nowhere to hide”. 


But Concepta Cassar, head of policy at Migrants’ Rights Network, said the government’s objective is to show it has control over an “invented political problem” where migrants are scapegoated for government policy failings. 


“Thousands upon thousands of lives are impacted,” Cassar said, adding that some businesses are repeatedly targeted despite nobody having been found to be breaking the law. 


“People don’t realise that we have ICE. They’re like ‘ICE is coming to the UK’. No, it’s here,” Cassar said. “They’re not a militarised force yet but we have the same need for community defence and the need to look out for each other.”


Green party deputy Mothin Ali warned that “people are being humiliated and whole communities terrorised”, adding: “This is racist harassment dressed up as immigration enforcement.”


The Home Office said enforcement visits were “based on robust intelligence and risk assessments, compliant with policy”.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: 6- Cuttings will regrow – Sitting-in for Grandmother Cottonwood
content:
On July 27th, 2026 the U.S. government and Fisher industries cut down three ancient cottonwood trees in a small town called Lochiel, Arizona in order to build not just one but two border walls. This area is the habitat of the endangered Mexican Wolf as well as jaguars, bears, foxes and many other bizarre, beautiful bugs and animals. It is also the home of the Tohono O’odham people, important to many indigenous tribes on both sides of the border. When the three grandmother cottonwoods were cut, one brave comrade stood in front of construction equipment, preventing the destruction of the last ancient tree and the construction of the border wall. In that last tree, we began our tree sit. With the support of hundreds of activists, the land owners, nearby towns and tribes, and even the local sheriff department, we halted construction of the walls for 75 days.

For 75 days, activists sat in the remaining cottonwood as ground support grew into a sprawling camp. It was the first tree sit to stop border wall construction and was briefly the first binational tree sit in history, with a sit erecting on the Mexican side for three days in August. During these 75 days, O:shad camp, jaguar in O’odham, held morning ceremony in the easement, the road which enforced the border. Ceremony frequently extended to effectively halt all construction vehicles for the day, or days at a time. People fell in love, they danced in the mud, cooked communal meals, all while defending the land. Utopia felt nearby.

Then, on October 5th, hundreds of border patrol officers, accompanied by turning point usa, invaded O:shad camp. They cut down the grandmother cottonwood and forcibly removed the tree sitter without a proper extraction team, risking her life. Activists on the ground circled the trunk to protect the tree and continue their resistance against the wall. More than 10 activists were arrested and many more brutalized. Though on private property and with no warrant, they ransacked the camp and destroyed our belongings.

Indigenous and non-white activists were singled out and beaten much worse than white comrades. Border Patrol violently pushed, pulled and dragged, but also kneeled on throats, punched eyes, pushed skin into barbed wire. They specifically targeted our medic (who is Indigenous) to be violently dragged, beaten, and arrested. They prevented our media team from capturing what happened, while escorting Turning Point USA to film the day in order to spread their right wing propaganda.

The next day, as Border Patrol expanded their boundaries further into private property to make way for the wall, five more of us were taken, and lawyers were unable to find them in the system while border patrol ignored calls from their lawyers, friends and family.

A day later, my comrade locked herself to a cement truck and stayed in a stress position without food or water for 7 hours while Border Patrol covered her with an emergency blanket despite the hot climate. One officer told her and the other officers that they should drive her to the middle of nowhere where no one would be able to hear her scream. They began to move the vehicle with her still above the tire; we all thought she would be killed. Two comrades who ran towards her, worried for her life, were tackled, brutalized, and arrested – one was sexually assaulted during her arrest. Finally they brought in an expert extractor who took her out of lockdown and she was taken to detention and then federal prison. She is now facing federal assault charges.

The rest of us were shot with pepper balls, tear gassed, leaving us vomiting, injured, bruised and emotionally exhausted. After the tree sitter was removed from the grandmother tree in Lochiel, a comrade reinstated the sit on the mexico side. Cut off from ground support by border patrol, she went over two days without food or water. When mexican firefighters and Fisher construction workers went to pull her out, she free climbed further up the tree. They destroyed her platform and life sustaining materials, leaving her to perch in the cottonwood branches without a platform or supplies. She suffered dehydration and starvation in high heat but still managed to keep a backpack on her, which she filled with clippings of the Abuela tree so that no matter what happened, the trees offspring could be replanted.

The following day the wall continued.

In total 30+ of us have been arrested, and many more brutalized, injured, and traumatized. We are the …
