author: mark
title: [EN, FR, DE] Call to Action: Resist Frontex’s expanding powers on December 18, 2026!
content:
[

FR

,

DE

 below]


On 27 October 2026, the European Commission presented its proposal for a new Frontex Regulation. The proposal would massively expand Frontex’s powers, staff, budget and activities, both inside and outside the EU. At the same time, some of the already very weak Fundamental Rights safeguards would be further weakened. The proposal would expand Frontex’s surveillance of people on the move, even before they ever reach the EU’s borders, and give the agency a stronger role in surveilling social media content about people’s movement.


The new regulation would further extend the reach of the EU’s border regime, strengthening Frontex’s role in the externalisation of EU borders and consolidating its position as a key actor in organising and coordinating deportations. The agency would now be able to conduct deportations between non-EU countries and transfers to so-called “return hubs” outside the EU, where people can be detained in places they have never set foot in. Rather than addressing the violence of deportations, these plans seek to make them easier to organise and enforce. This will further expose people on the move to violence within and beyond Europe.


We refuse to accept this expansion as inevitable.


You can read more details about the new regulation proposal on this blog post:

https://abolishfrontex.org/blog/2026/11/05/bigger-stronger-more-violent-the-eus-plans-for-frontex/


More resources and wider powers for Frontex should not be the response to the violence of the EU border regime. They will reinforce it. Action is urgently needed.


We oppose this proposal of the new regulation and call for an International Action Day on or around 18 December 2026, International Migrants Day, asking groups in all countries to participate in any way you can, organising big or small actions or integrating our demands into your existing plans. We call on the European Commission to withdraw its proposal and on the European Parliament and the Council to reject it, as a first step to abolishing the agency altogether.


There are many ways to take action: banners, posters, flyer distributions, public gatherings, speeches, art installations and demonstrations. Be creative, organise collectively, and make our resistance visible.


We will not stand idly while deportations are expanded, borders are pushed further beyond Europe, and violence against people on the move is normalised.


Please reach out to info[at]abolishfrontex.org or via Instagram (@abolishfrontex) if you would like to collaborate or are planning an action in your city, so that we can connect efforts and share your activities through our communications.


No more powers for Frontex. Freedom of movement for all. Abolish Frontex.


[FR]


Appel à action : le 18 décembre 2026 opposons-nous à une nouvelle augmentation des pouvoirs de Frontex


Le 27 octobre 2026, la Commission européenne a présenté sa proposition concernant un nouveau règlement pour Frontex. Cette proposition prévoit une extension massive des pouvoirs de cette agence de l’Union européenne. Elle concerne notamment ses effectifs, son budget tout comme ses activités tant au sein de l’UE comme en dehors de l’UE.


Dans le même temps, certaines des garanties en matière de droits fondamentaux, déjà très réduites, seraient encore affaiblies.


La proposition étendrait la surveillance exercée par Frontex sur les personnes en migration, avant même qu’elles n’atteignent les frontières de l’UE, et conférerait à l’agence un rôle accru dans la surveillance des contenus publiés sur les réseaux sociaux concernant les mouvements de population.


Le nouveau règlement élargirait aussi la portée du régime frontalier de l’UE en renforçant le rôle de Frontex dans l’externalisation de ses frontières et en consolidant sa position d’acteur clé dans l’organisation et la coordination des expulsions. L’agence serait désormais en mesure de procéder à des expulsions entre pays non membres de l’UE et à des transferts vers des « centres de retour » “return hubs” situés en dehors de l’UE. Dans ces centres les personnes retenues pourraient être placées en détention dans des pays où elles n’ont jamais mis les pieds ! Plutôt que de s’attaquer à la violence inhérente aux expulsions, ces projets visent à faciliter leur organisation et leur mise en œuvre. Cela exposera encore davantage les personnes en migration à la violence, tant en Europe qu’au-delà.

author: Steven Methven
title: Cuts to Benefits Are Not the ‘End to Neoliberalism’ We Were Promised
content:
Tomorrow, the government will publish the Milburn report. That’s a long-awaited review into Britain’s one million young people not in employment, education or training – the so-called NEETs. Its contents, though, won’t come as a huge surprise, with its author, Tony Blair-era health secretary Alan Milburn, taking to the Sunday morning news rounds to pitch his plans while others briefed its contents to the press.


They’re trying to get ahead of what could be

a significant rebellion

 amongst backbench Labour MPs. And who can blame the rebels? After all, with swingeing cuts incoming, they’re the ones who’ll have to explain to young voters with disabilities and other health issues – as well as angry parents – why their lives are apparently worth less than those just a few years older than them.


In politics, life comes at you fast. But not so fast that we can’t remember what prime minister Andy Burnham pledged just four months ago – an

end to neoliberalism in this country

. That’s a tricky term to define, and while Burnham mentioned deregulation, privatisation and the fantasy of trickle-down economics as its major symptoms, there’s a simpler understanding near at hand. Neoliberalism is when a state decides that corporations, rather than citizens, are its clients.


Far from killing neoliberalism off, there’s more than an element of it in Milburn’s NEET plans. 


The shape of his proposals are familiar, the usual carrot-and-stick approach to welfare aimed at the bottom line, rather than the underlying conditions that put people in need of it. First, the cuts. Milburn will recommend that under-25s will

no longer be able to claim sickness and disability benefits

. Instead, there’ll be a one-stop “youth allowance”, capped at the standard rate of universal credit. So that will be a sharp cut to those who might expect to receive the additional universal credit health element. 


Personal independence payments will also be restricted: under 25s will no longer be able to access PIP. Instead, they’ll be able to

apply to “local funds” for help

 with specific “short-term expenses,” though those with the most severe needs will have their existing entitlements protected. 


Who knew that disability or debilitating illness take on a special reality when a person turns 25? Obviously, they don’t. But that ever-present national thought is at the heart of these proposed cuts: the problems – even the health problems – of the young are always a little bit unserious. They won’t be helped by empathy or care, that thought goes on, but only discipline and downplaying.


In his

government report released last month

, professor Peter Fonagy lists in detail the material conditions driving the mental health crisis in the country’s youth. Increased poverty, insecurity and crippling housing costs. Atomisation, loneliness and lack of opportunity. Growing existential dread around the climate, technology and the political future. An education system impoverished by alienation, comparison and intense scrutiny. 


Burnham has called the number of young people on existing benefits

“a moral failure”

. And it’s a profound one for sure. But it’s not their moral failure. It’s ours.


So will our collective failure be addressed in this review?


Unlikely. Instead, what’s been briefed is that the new, pared-back youth allowance will likely be contingent on recipients engaging with programmes aimed at getting them back into work. And while the scope of the cuts are crystal clear, that positive package remains vague. The papers have been told there’ll be investment for employment advisers, mental health support and internships, backed up by – potentially –

a new legal duty on the government

 to furnish every young person with a route into work. 


Great – but maybe let’s get that in place before the cuts? 


No, no. Young people must always get the stick first. And business? It’s the carrot for them.


“I think we should subsidise wages,”

Milburn told Laura Kuenssberg

 on Sunday, “Because young people today are walking into the workplace often with a mental health problem, ADHD or anxiety, and if you’re a small business, that’s a cost that you’ve got to absorb. The state has a responsibility to help them with that.”


The state has a responsibility to help

businesses

 to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on businesses to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on…


Stop the merry-go-round, it’s making us sick.

author: Unknown
title: “Gen Z Regulates” : A New Wave of Unrest in Germany?
content:
For months, unrest has been spreading across Europe. In

Spain

, a movement against evictions and gentrification culminated on November 11 in a countrywide general strike. In

France

, student revolt set off the most intense street confrontations since the

Yellow Vest movement

. Albania has seen wave upon wave of clashes since last February. On Halloween, the European youth protests finally reached Germany.


Under the motto

“Gen Z regelt”

 (“Gen Z regulates”), tens of thousands took to the streets of nearly 40 German cities on October 31. While a large-scale uprising like the

one

 in France remains unlikely, the first cracks in the pacification of society are starting to show. In this report, two anarchists describe their experiences in two different demonstrations and discuss the potential of the events.


More demonstrations on the same theme are scheduled for

November 20

.


A stylish banner in front of the “Gen Z Regelt” protest in Göttingen. What would Goethe have said?


Germany in Crisis


The demonstration on October 31 took place in a general context of crisis. In Germany, as elsewhere around the globe, inflation has run rampant over the last six years, driven by the pandemic, Putin’s invasion of Ukraine and the consequent loss of cheap natural gas from Russia, and, most recently, the US-Iran war.


Another growing influence on the economy is the climate catastrophe. It is

estimated

 that Germany will lose around 30 billion euros a year as a consequence of its impact. In one week, a heatwave at the end of June

killed

 close to 10,000 people. Unlike countries that have long-term experience with temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius, only 10% of homes in Germany have air conditioning; with the exception of intensive care units and operating rooms, most hospitals and nursing homes don’t have it, so people who experienced heat stroke were treated in overheated rooms. Senior citizens and those with preexisting health problems were especially hard hit: in at least one nursing home, temperatures

reached

 up to 50 degrees Celsius.


A protester in the German city of Essen asks to stop some of the impacts of climate change.


Who dies as a consequence of climate change is determined mostly by class. Germany also faces a housing crisis—

something like 53% of people live in rented homes

—and the cheapest flats are generally located right beneath the roofs of buildings several stories high. These buildings were built to keep heat in, so during heat waves, temperatures in the flats at night often stayed above the outside temperatures at same time.


On top of this, the government comprised of the neoliberal left (SPD) and Christian conservative (CDU/CSU) parties has introduced an unpopular austerity program in order to push through a massive increase in military spending, which started after the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It would take another article to list all the financial cuts involved. Workers and middle-class people will have many billions less in “social benefits”—in other words, they get less back from the work and resources that the state and capitalists take from them.


Some 12% of all jobs in Germany are

directly in state institutions

, in addition to fully state-owned companies and other organizations connected to the state, like the public health insurance agencies and public media companies. Many of these have stop hiring because of the financial situation. At the same time, German economic growth is stagnating. Consequently, “Gen Z” career entrants confront a context in which companies are trying to figure out how to use artificial intelligence to replace them amid an employment market that is already much worse than previous generations faced. This is undermining the last vestiges of a social contract between companies and the state on one side and segments of the youth on the other.


Study, get degree, and you can have a middle-class life? Not anymore.


Finally, some international fashions trends like ski glasses are reaching German youth.


Unemployment is rising among university and college graduates. The social situation isn’t as catastrophic as it has become in other countries, but by contrast with many other countries, people in Germany do not have much experience helping each other directly. German society has focused on the state as the only thinkable source of support when people lose their jobs or experience other setbacks.


As a result, anger has spread …

title: Horizontes Postcapitalistas
content:
Horizontes Postcapitalistas


Argentina 2026-11-14 – enviado por Andrés L R: andresenbsas@gmail.com 


Es un gusto presentar este audiovisual, en pleno estreno.


Integro el grupo de personas que, desde diferentes países, en forma colectiva, construimos este proyecto.


La Red de Estudios en Postcapitalismo busca aportar al pensamiento y la práctica para el postcapitalismo.


[ 

Nueva revista: 

https://rep.enesmerida.unam.mx/revista-horizontes-poscapitalistas

/

 ]


Es decir, pensar imaginar compartir estudiar cuidar, qué y cómo, crear hacer construir tejer sembrar ese modo de mundo ya no capitalista, esas formas de autonomía, que, desde abajo, recuperan lo comunitario priorizando la defensa y protección de la biodiversidad que integramos.


Este audiovisual, hace foco en las circunstancias dadas que atravesamos como humanidad, analiza las artimañas y los avasalladores golpes que el sistema capitalista ejecuta, a traves de sus operadores, para traspasar las crisis profundas que padece.


Sobre la base del análisis y observación, del profesor William I. Robinson, veremos la crisis institucional en curso, el surgimiento del nuevo complejo económico hegemónico mundial y la oleada de expansión capitalista que padecemos.


Que sea un aporte para el pensar y el hacer.


Intentar ver dónde estamos paradxs y a qué nos enfrentamos.


Y también abrir la pregunta ¿Con qué herramientas contamos?


«Hora Cero; Crisis de Época del Capitalismo Global»


https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bUjk9rptWXI


.


REVISTA HORIZONTES POSCAPITALISTAS


/rep.enesmerida.unam.mx/revista-horizontes-poscapitalistas/


EDITORIAL Número 2. Noviembre, 2026. Precisiones y límites del concepto postcapitalista.


Tras haber sembrado en nuestro primer número una cartografía de experiencias vivas, les invitamos a recorrer las páginas de este segundo número de la revista Horizontes Postcapitalistas, titulado Precisiones y límites del concepto postcapitalista. Este proyecto editorial nace de la profunda convicción de que el conocimiento no es un ejercicio académico abstracto, sino un acto ético y político de co-construcción y cuidado mutuo.


En tiempos donde las lógicas de la competencia y el individualismo tienden a aislarnos, apostamos por pensar y escribir en común como una forma genuina de resistencia. Nuestro objetivo para esta entrega es dar continuidad a la labor de documentar el hacer postcapitalista, proponiendo un ejercicio de diálogo crítico que abone al desarrollo conceptual desde la experiencia, la escucha y la reflexión situada. Creemos firmemente que es en ese encuentro donde logramos ensanchar las grietas por las que ya germinan otros mundos posibles.


Este número abre con un texto colectivo elaborado por el Grupo de Investigación Colectiva del Semillero de Saberes de la REP, el cual ofrece delimitaciones fundamentales sobre las praxis y filosofías milenarias no capitalistas y los buenos vivires en las ciudades, las selvas y los campos. A partir de ahí, las páginas se despliegan como un mapa en movimiento para asomarnos a las geografías de lo posible, un tránsito por las orillas de un sistema que se resiste a morir pero que ya no tiene el monopolio del porvenir.


Este viaje no busca certezas acabadas, sino rastrear las grietas donde los pueblos ensayan la vida en común. Así, al andar por la experiencia de la cooperativa Acapatzingo en Iztapalapa y la política subalterna de los Panchos de la mano de Libertad Castro Colina, o al beber de la sabiduría maya ancestral para perfeccionar la comunalidad con el plan de vida junto a Franklin Velasco García, comprendemos que el postcapitalismo no es una teoría fría, sino un caminar guiado por la memoria y el arraigo.


Ese mismo pulso nos lleva a detenernos, con Raquel Méndez Villamizar, en los apuntes decoloniales del banco de tiempo Kual Kan de Yhali Rosa Lombera, y  a reflexionar con Víctor Hugo Bonilla Muñoz sobre las monedas comunitarias y la autodependencia compartida a partir de la propuesta de Claudia Yadira Caballero, recordándonos que medir el tiempo y el valor de otra manera es fracturar la lógica del capital.


El camino se expande hacia horizontes más amplios al encontrarnos con el Tejido Global de Alternativas con la reseña de Saharai Martínez Arellano, o al conocer  los derechos de la naturaleza leídos por Valentina Campos Cabral a partir de la propuesta de Alberto Acosta. Este tramo se enriquece con una introducción a la caja de herramientas audiovisuales de Territorios de Vida …

author: dev
title: Cerner le capitalisme, entre son avant et ses après
content:
Nous avons déjà eu l'occasion de dire tout le bien que nous pensions de l'excellent pavé

Mondes Postcapitalistes

 dirigé par Jérôme Baschet et Laurent Jeanpierre, paru l'année dernière à la Découverte (nous nous étions entretenus avec eux ici :

Explorer et inventer les mondes postcapitalistes

 et avions publié

les bonnes feuilles

). Nous proposons cette semaine cette interview écrite et au long cours (déjà parue en épisodes chez nos amis de

À bas bruit

). À partir d'une mise en perspective historique, ainsi que de l'expérience de l'insurrection indigène zapatiste à partir de la fin des années 1990 au Mexique, Jérôme Baschet souligne, avec force, l'exceptionnalité anthropologique et historique du capitalisme. Depuis-là, il convient de s'employer à la réouverture de futurs

postcapitalistes

. La critique de l'organisation générale du monde se doit d'être complétée par la figuration anticipatrice d'

autres

 mondes, postcapitalistes ceux-là. L'anticipation la précise, la diversifie, l'approfondie ; elle lui confère une densité utopique concrète. Jérôme Baschet revient enfin sur les expériences préfiguratives et les pratiques de résistance susceptibles de dissiper l'épais nuage de suie brouillant nos perspectives : l'abolition du monde de l'économie ne peut plus être ajournée. Se dessine alors un ardent désir de basculement : dynamiter le capitalisme en crise pour laisser place au déploiement d'une multiplicité de mondes postcapitalistes –

faire rupture

.


Dans les années 1980-1990, tu as suivi les séminaires de J. Le Goff à l'EHESS ; ce très grand promoteur de la Nouvelle histoire a aussi été ton directeur de thèse. De quelle manière ta formation initiale d'historien médiéviste a-t-elle modelé les réflexions que tu as menées sur le capitalisme, et que tu poursuis aujourd'hui avec ce livre ? En d'autres termes, dans quelle mesure l'examen du passé est-il pourvoyeur de matériau pour l'analyse (critique) du présent ?

C'est bien volontiers que nous pouvons inscrire le démarrage de notre entretien dans la pensée de Jacques Le Goff, historien magnifique et généreux, qui a renouvelé la compréhension des sociétés médiévales et à qui nous devons notamment l'idée d'un long Moyen Âge prolongé jusqu'au xviiie siècle.


Je dirais d'abord que la connaissance historique de ce qui n'est pas le capitalisme et a existé avant lui peut contribuer à aiguiser notre réflexion au moment de considérer des mondes non capitalistes qui n'existent pas encore. Cela fait partie de la gamme des possibles non capitalistes, soit qu'on cherche à y déceler des éléments potentiellement inspirants (par exemple les pratiques communautaires paysannes ou, peut-être, l'essor des communes), soit pour garder à l'esprit que certains d'entre eux ne sont pas franchement désirables. Ainsi, par exemple, au moment de prôner une relocalisation généralisée comme dimension d'une transition postcapitaliste, on devra prendre soin de la différencier du lien des humains au sol, qui était l'une des bases de la domination sociale dans le monde médiéval.


Par ailleurs, regarder le monde capitaliste depuis un univers historique qui ne l'était pas encore peut nous aider à en saisir les traits spécifiques. Ce jeu de contraste permet de voir mieux : c'est la vertu de la comparaison historique. Par exemple, on peut comprendre que dans un monde féodo-ecclésial fondé sur le lien des humains à leur lieu (ils doivent en principe être baptisés, vivre et payer les redevances puis être enterrés au même endroit), la pire condamnation judiciaire, hormis la peine capitale, soit le bannissement, une quasi-mort sociale ; alors que dans le monde moderne, où prévaut un principe d'unification spatiale et d'amplification des circulations, la peine essentielle est la prison, soit une localisation forcée, à l'inverse de la délocalisation forcée qu'est le bannissement. Plus largement, c'est un contraste radical que l'on peut établir entre le présent capitaliste et le monde d'avant le marché, d'avant l'autonomisation de l'économie, d'avant la modernité.


Enfin, à un niveau très général, mais essentiel, il faut répéter que la connaissance du passé a une vertu critique fondamentale : faire voir que le capitalisme n'a pas toujours existé rappelle le caractère contingent des dominations qu'il impose. C'est une évidence trop souvent oubliée : le capitalisme est un système socio-historique spécifique et, comme tous les systèmes historiques, il est apparu à un certain moment, il connaît divers …

author: ACG
title: The Proletariat and the Possibility of Revolution
content:
We re-publish below a text from the Spanish historian


Agustin Guillamón

, author of among other books, The Friends of Durruti Group 1937-1939 and

Ready for Revolution

:

The CNT Defense Committees in Barcelona, 1933-1938. This is the first of two interesting texts from Spanish writers that we will be putting up on the ACG website.


Introduction


The difference between Miquel Amorós and myself doesn’t lie in one wanting revolution and the other rejecting it, nor in one defending autonomy and the other not. We both start from a radical critique of capitalist society and the conviction that emancipation cannot be the work of institutions separate from those who struggle. We both reject the integration of struggles into state institutions and deeply distrust any organisation that seeks to replace direct worker action. However, when we try to define what this autonomy means, what relationship it should have with the transformation of society, and, above all, who can carry this transformation to its ultimate consequences, a fundamental difference emerges between us.


I would say that this difference can be formulated as follows: Amorós emphasises the concrete reconstruction of autonomous forms of life, while I consider it necessary to ask about the social subject capable of transforming these necessarily partial experiences into a general transformation of capitalist relations. This is not about denying the value of autonomous experiences, nor about postponing emancipation to an indefinite future. It is about determining what social force can transform what today appears as a limited experience into a general way of organising life. This question necessarily leads to the proletariat, and in it, in my view, lies the essential difference between our respective positions.


Amorós begins with a historical observation that cannot be ignored. The traditional forms of the workers’ movement have been profoundly weakened by the evolution of capitalism. Political representation, union integration, the fragmentation of labour, and the transformation of lifestyles have destroyed a good part of the conditions that allowed the proletariat to constitute itself, at certain historical moments, as a visible, organised revolutionary force capable of directly intervening in society. Faced with this situation, passively awaiting a future revolutionary recomposition would be a form of impotence. If emancipation has any real content, it must begin in the present.


Hence the importance that autonomy, community, and concrete utopia acquire in Amorós’s work. Revolution cannot be a promise that indefinitely justifies the acceptance of a subjugated life. We must reclaim now the capacities that capitalism has taken from us: To decide collectively, to produce and reproduce life without delegating it, to rebuild community ties, to recover knowledge, and to create spaces where human relations are not entirely determined by commodities and the state. This “concrete utopia” precisely expresses the desire not to postpone freedom until an uncertain future.


This demand strikes me as profoundly revolutionary. A revolution that doesn’t transform life would be a purely political revolution and, therefore, insufficient. We don’t want to change those who govern only to continue living under social relations we don’t control. We want the production, reproduction, and organisation of our existence to cease appearing to us as external powers. Emancipation cannot be reduced to modifying the administration of a society that remains essentially the same.


But precisely for this reason, I consider it necessary to raise a question that cannot be resolved by appealing solely to autonomy: What happens when an autonomous experience, even if real and transformative for those who participate in it, continues to develop within a capitalist society whose general relations remain intact?


An autonomous experience can profoundly transform the lives of those who participate in it and yet continue to exist within the market. It can create cooperative relationships and still need money; it can function without internal hierarchies and still have to buy goods produced by other workers; it can collectively organise a space and still remain subject to the property relations that govern the whole of society. It may even explicitly reject the logic of profit and yet depend, for its own reproduction, on an economy that remains dominated by that logic.

author: Unknown
title: Evrensel'in manşeti: Yaşamak için birleş!
content:
Sayfamızdaki yüzlerce isim, Türkiye’nin devasa bir işçi mezarlığına dönüştüğünün kanıtı... İSİG Meclisi kayıtlarından alınan bu liste, çalışırken ölen en az 38 bin işçinin anısını ve hesap sorma iradesini taşıyor.

Türkiye, sermayenin kâr hırsı ve cezasızlık politikalarıyla devasa bir işçi mezarlığına dönüştürüldü. AKP iktidarı boyunca fabrikalarda, madenlerde ve şantiyelerde en az 38 bin 500 işçi iş cinayetlerinde yaşamını yitirdi. İş güvenliğinin bir ‘maliyet kalemi’ olarak görüldüğü bu düzende katledilenlerin isimleri gazete sayfalarına sığmıyor. Arka planda gördüğünüz yüzlerce isim, o 38 bin 500 canın sadece yüzde 4’ü...

Endüstriyel yangın ve patlamalar sadece son 9 yılda yüzde 315 arttı. Türkiye’de her 100 bin emekçi başına yalnızca 2.8 müfettiş düşüyor. Agresif ekonomik büyüme, emperyalist rekabet, üretim baskısı, sendikasızlaşma, kamusal denetimsizlik ve nihayet kâr hırsı katliam rejimini derinleştirdi. Dolayısıyla Türkiye’de iş cinayetleri “münferit kazalar” değil.

İşçi katliamlarını teknik ihmal ve bireysel kusurlarla açıklamak yetersiz ve artık kimse inanmıyor. Mezbahaya dönmüş şirketlerin ve endüstriyel tesislerin derhal kamulaştırılması şart. Sermaye zırhını giymiş patronlara verilecek en büyük ceza üretim araçlarının ellerinden alınması ve halka verilmesi. Bunun tek yolu da işçi sınıfının birleşik mücadelesi.

Evrensel Yazarı Kansu Yıldırım işçilerin ‘erken ölüm’ünün politik ekonomisini kaleme aldı. Yıldırım, “Sermaye zırhını giyinmiş patronlara verilecek en büyük ceza hapis ya da para cezası değil, üretim araçlarının ellerinden alınması ve halka verilmesidir. Tüm fabrikaların iş organizasyonu sürecinde işçi temsilinin gücü artırılmalıdır. Hepsinden önemlisi ise bu denetim ve kontrol sisteminin işçi sınıfının elinde olmasıdır” ifadelerine yer verdi.

Gazetemiz Muhabiri Emirhan Durmaz katliamın ardından HABAŞ’ı takip etti. Durmaz ele aldığı haber-analiz ile emperyalist rekabet, gümrük ve HABAŞ arasındaki ilişkiyi irdelerken, “Aliağa’da işçiler neden ölüyor?” sorusunu yanıtladı.

Yazarımız, İş Güvenliği Uzmanı Deniz İpek beş soruda işçi katliamlarını değerlendirdi ve “İşçilerin kendi seçtikleri temsilcilerin çoğunlukta olduğu işçi sağlığı ve güvenliği komiteleri kurulmalıdır. Bu komiteler çalışma koşullarını denetleme, gerekli bilgilere erişme ve tehlike karşısında üretimi durdurma yetkisine sahip olmalıdır. Sendikalaşma, grev ve çalışmaktan kaçınma haklarının fiilen kullanılabilmesi, bu denetimin güvencesidir” ifadelerini kullandı.

Yazarımız-Hukukçu Ahmet Ergin, cezasızlığın işçi katliamlarını nasıl teşvik ettiğini şöyle anlattı: “Cezasızlık politikasının temel dinamiği, yargı uygulayıcılarının, kendilerini, devleti ve dolayısıyla çoğu zaman kamu görevlisi olan failleri korumakla görevli görmeleridir. Bu nedenle iş cinayetlerinde kamu sorumluluğuna neredeyse hiç gidilmemesi kolaylıkla anlaşılabilir. Ama bizde yasanın deyimiyle işverenler, yani sermayedarlar da korunmaktadır.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Krizden Çıkış Yolu Olarak Komünizasyon
content:
Yazan: Bruno Astarian


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


1. Komünizmin Dolaysızlığı


1.1. Tanım ve Köken


Dolaysızlık kavramını, anında olma kavramıyla karıştırmamalıyız. Komünizmin dolaysız olması derken, proleter devrimin amacının artık bir geçiş toplumu yaratmak değil, doğrudan komünizmi kurmak olduğunu kastediyoruz. Yani: siyasi iktidarı ele geçirmek, diğer toplumsal katmanlarla ittifaklar kurmak ve bu alanda bir geçiş aşamasına geçmekten (devletin kademeli olarak ortadan kalkması vb.) daha karmaşık bir şey.


Komünizmin “dolaysızlığı” fikri, bir anda ortaya çıkmadı. Bu fikir, 1960’lar ve 1970’lerdeki krizle birlikte, solun siyasi güçsüzlüğünün ve solcuların “çalışmayı reddetme” olgusunu kavrayamamasının bir sonucu olarak ortaya çıktı. Bugün, tüm programatik girişimler gülünç görünmektedir. Çalışma karşıtı dürtüye gelince, bu dürtü bugün 1970’lerdekinden daha güçlüdür (Çin’de, Bangladeş’te ve hatta son derece sanayileşmiş ülkelerde bile).


1.2. Bir Süreç Olarak Komünizasyon


Komünizasyon, sihirli bir değnek sallanarak komünizmin kurulacağı anlamına gelmez. Komünizm, devrimin ilerlemeleri ve geri çekilmeleriyle şekillenen bir mücadele süreci aracılığıyla kurulacaktır. Bunun anlamı şudur: Devrimcilerin gerçekleştireceği eylemler,

burada ve şimdi

, emeğin ve değerin, ve geri kalan her şeyin (aile, vatan) ortadan kaldırılmasını hedefleyecektir. Devrim, kapitalist mülkiyete saldırdığında, bunu proletaryaya daha önce sahip olmadığı mülkiyetin mülkiyetini vermek için değil, her türlü mülkiyet biçimine derhal son vermek için yapar. Şu anda bu süreci ayrıntılı olarak açıklamak mümkün değildir. Ancak, bizi nelerin beklediğine dair daha net bir fikir edinebilmek ve zamanı geldiğinde devrim ile karşı devrimi birbirinden ayırt edebilmek için, bu süreci daha kesin bir şekilde tanımlamak gereklidir.


2. Krize Verilen Tepkiler ve Komünizasyon


Kriz patlak verdiğinde, proletarya isyan eder; zira emek gücü satın alınmamaktadır ve bu durum onu toplumsal ilişkilerin ve doğayla olan tüm bağlarının dışında bırakmaktadır. İsyan ederek proleterler krize bir tepki ortaya koyarlar; bu tepki, kendi içinde tüm olasılıkların matrisini oluşturur ve komünizmin doğabileceği tek yerdir. Teori, komünizmi her zaman aynı şekilde tanımlamasa da, tüm tanımları ve stratejileri, proletaryanın krize yanıt verirken yaptıklarına dayanmaktadır. Ancak, krize bir yanıt söz konusu olabilmesi için proletaryanın genelleşmiş bir ayaklanması gerekir; bir veya birkaç işletmeyle sınırlı kalan çatışmalarda ise, bu çatışmalar ne kadar “örnek niteliğinde” olursa olsun, krize bir yanıt söz konusu olamaz.


Krize verilen yanıt, iki temel faktöre bağlıdır: proletaryanın bireyselleşmesi/kitleselliğin ortadan kalkması ve mücadelenin ihtiyaçlarını karşılamak amacıyla kapitalist mülkiyetin toplumsallaştırılması — patronlar olmadan işe dönmek için değil. Eğer mevcut kriz, büyük ölçekli bir proleter ayaklanmasını tetikleyecek kadar şiddetli hale gelirse, çağımızın tarihsel özellikleriyle damgalanmış bu iki faktörle bir kez daha karşı karşıya kalacağız. Proletaryanın kitleselliğinden uzaklaşması, post-Fordist sermaye tarafından çoktan başlatılmış bir süreç olduğu için daha da belirgin hale gelecektir. Kitlesel işçiliğin olduğu “eski güzel günlere” dönmek istemek, karşıdevrimci bir hayaldir. Kapitalist mülkiyete gelince, bunun iki özelliği vardır:


Bir yandan, hiçbir şey onun egemenlik alanından kaçamaz. Sermaye, hayatın tamamını o kadar ele geçirmiştir ki, ne yaparsanız yapın, her zaman onun mülkiyeti içinde bulunursunuz. Kriz patlak verdiğinde, proletaryanın kapitalist mülkiyete el koymaktan başka seçeneği kalmaz. En basit gösteri bile onu belediyeye ait asfaltı işgal etmeye zorlar. Bugün bunu yapmasına izin veriliyor. Yarın ise bu yasadışı olacak. Proletaryanın krize tepki olarak gerçekleştirdiği her eylem, onu sermayenin mülkiyetinin bir kısmını ele geçirmek için sermayeyle yüzleşmeye zorlar ve böylece, salt özne olmaktan ibaret olan kendi varoluşuna nesnellik kazandırır.

1

Öte yandan, kapitalist mülkiyeti oluşturan malların kullanım değeri, değer artışı gereklilikleri tarafından güçlü bir şekilde belirlenmektedir. Bu nedenle krize verilen yanıt, her şeyden önce …

author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: La politica tra piazze e maranza
content:
Mobilitazioni e decreti.


La classe politica italiana (ma si potrebbe benissimo estendere in generale alla classe politica europea, per tacere ad esempio di Trump) mostra tutta la sua incapacità a comprendere le gravi falle che il sistema capitalistico ha provocato nella società oppure, che forse è più vicino al vero, la sua pervicace volontà a mantenere a tutti i costi il sistema esistente.


Lo scatenamento dei più tremendi spiriti animali del capitalismo e del sistema politico mondiale degli ultimi anni si traduce in guerre, instabilità economica, crisi sociali, peggioramento progressivo delle condizioni di vita delle classi sfruttate. La risposta da parte delle classi dirigenti è ovunque la repressione, la criminalizzazione delle mobilitazioni che la società esprime, il fomentare l’odio sociale e l’anestetizzare l’opinione pubblica con opportuni diversivi.


Quanto sta accadendo in queste settimane in Italia è la perfetta fotografia di questo stato delle cose. Le piazze piene di una protesta spontanea e incontenibile, animata principalmente da giovanissimi e studenti, i blocchi e le manifestazioni promossi da agricoltori ed autotrasportatori contro il caro carburanti e il carovita, in particolare al Sud, hanno provocato nel governo una reazione che qualcuno ha definito infantile-adolescenziale, definizione corretta se vivessimo in un mondo giusto ma così non è, e che si è tradotta nell’ennesimo decreto sicurezza e nell’introduzione nel codice penale dell’ennesimo reato, con cui si tenta di imbrigliare le proteste degli ultimi anni. Questo per quanto riguarda in prima istanza i cosiddetti maranza, termine comodo per liquidare la profonda insoddisfazione che investe il mondo giovanile, mentre nei confronti di autotrasportatori e agricoltori i fascisti al governo hanno fatto ricorso al più classico dei metodi: il bastone e la carota. Dapprima sono state mandate le forze dell’ordine per identificare camionisti e agricoltori che bloccavano le strade, il giorno successivo è stato varato un decreto che distribuisce briciole per sedare momentaneamente la protesta.


Dall’altra parte, l’opposizione parlamentare rappresentata dal centro sinistra non ha saputo neppure cavalcare la protesta, anche solo per mettere in difficoltà un governo in palese affanno che pur vuole battere alle prossime elezioni politiche. Senza considerare l’incredibile presidio milanese convocato dalla Cgil e dal Pd per dire no alla violenza, in generale leader ed esponenti del “campo largo” si sono limitati a criticare il governo per i provvedimenti presi, precisando che alla repressione dei comportamenti violenti vanno affiancate politiche sociali che affrontino il malessere giovanile e diano una risposta al carovita e alla crisi di salari e retribuzioni. Senza peraltro entrare nel merito delle questioni, tutto chiuso in un linguaggio ormai logoro e stereotipato, rappresentazione di un teatrino veramente distante dalle questioni sociali e dalla gravità della crisi che ci attanaglia. A cosa servono dichiarazioni di principio, prese di posizioni, manifestazioni di solidarietà, quando va bene, se tutto ciò rimane un flatus vocis, buono per i media e per animare uno sterile dibattito?


Il governo della destra fascista, o delle destre destre, come preferiscono definirlo i benpensanti convinti così di poter continuare ad alimentare il mito della destra liberale e ragionevole, che tanto ragionevole nella sua storia non è stata quando si è trattato di difendere l’ordine costituito, esprime al meglio la sua idea di società gerarchizzata, ordinata, controllata e prona al volere dei potenti. Naturalmente la maschera democratica viene adattata al caso. Quindi se la destra fa quello che ha sempre fatto, qualche interrogativo potrebbe suscitarlo quella parte politica che continua a definirsi sinistra (tolto l’alibi del centro). Pierluigi Bersani, uno degli esponenti più in vista di quella “sinistra” che si è fatta investire dalla furia neoliberista, ha sostenuto in un noto programma televisivo che di fronte alla gravità della crisi mondiale in atto occorrono risposte radicali. Non ha poi chiarito in cosa consistano e soprattutto come dovrebbero attuarsi queste decisioni radicali, tuttavia ha ragione. Eppure le menti più illuminate della sinistra italiana, come Bersani, continuano a pensare che correttivi al capitalismo cosiddetto selvaggio e un nuovo protagonismo statale siano sufficienti a ridare vita ad un rinnovato patto sociale di stampo socialdemocratico …

author: Politisches Cafe in der K9
title: Filmvorführung: Die Utopie leben! Der Anarchismus in Spanien, 18.11., 19.30 Uhr, K9, Kinzigstr. 9
content:
Politisches Café


in der K9 Kinzigstr.9


10247 Berlin nähe U-Samariterstr.


Vor 90 Jahren sorgte die spanische Revolution in aller Welt für Hoffnungen, nicht nur den Faschismus zu stoppen Die spanische Revolution war auch ein utopischer Ort für sehr unterschiedliche Linke. Wir wollen im November zwei denkbar unterschiedliche Filme zum Thema spanische Revolution zeigen.


18.11. um 19.30. Uhr Abend 1: „Die Utopie leben! Der Anarchismus in Spanien“ (im Original Vivir la utopía: El anarquismo en España)


Der Anarchismus in Spanien (im Original Vivir la utopía), ist eine im Jahr 1997 unter der Regie von Juan Gamero für den Sender TVE produzierte Dokumentation. Das Werk beschäftigt sich mit den anarchistischen und anarcho-syndikalistischen Bewegungen während des Spanischen Bürgerkrie ges 1936-1939. Dabei geht sie insbesondere auf den Bereich des Alltagsleben und die Kollektive Selbstverwaltung ein und versucht die radikalen Veränderungen aufzuzeigen, die sich in diesen Jahren ergaben. Der Film besteht in erster Linie aus Interviews mit dreißig Anarchistinnen, die von ihren Erfahrungen in dieser Zeit berichten, wobei die einzelnen Interviews durch kurze Filmsequenzen, in der Regel Material aus der Zeit des Bürgerkrieges, voneinander getrennt werden.

author: infolibre
title: Συγκεντρώσεις – πορείες για την επέτειο της εξέγερσης του Πολυτεχνείου, την Τρίτη 17/11
content:
Την Τρίτη 17 Νοεμβρίου συμπληρώνονται 53 χρόνια από την αντιδικτακτορική εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου, και Φοιτητικοί σύλλογοι, σωματεία, πολιτικές οργανώσεις και κοινωνικές συλλογικότητες, καλούν σε πανελλαδικές κινητοποιήσεις. Σε μια Ευρώπη που εξεγείρεται, το Πολυτεχνείο του 1973 δεν μνημονεύει απλά την εξέγερση ενάντια στη χούντα αλλά δείχνει τον δρόμο για τους αγώνες του σήμερα, ενάντια στον πόλεμο, την φτώχεια, τους πολέμους και την υποτίμηση των ζωών μας. 53 χρόνια μετά, η κοινωνία βρίσκεται εν βρασμό και η ιστορία δείχνει πως κανένα δικαίωμα δεν είναι δεδομένο και κανένα δικαίωμα δεν κερδίζεται από μόνο του, αλλά με συλλογικούς αγώνες για ελευθερία και αξιοπρέπεια.


Καλέσματα:


Αθήνα: προσυγκεντρώσεις στις 13.00, σε Νομική Σχολή και Κάτω Πολυτεχνέιο, 15.00, σε πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος και Άγαλμα Κολοκοτρώνη και 17.00 στα Προπύλαια

Όλοι και όλες στο τριήμερο αντίστασης και μνήμης του Πολυτεχνείου 15-17/11και στις πορείες της 17 Νοεμβρίου!


Καλέσματα 17/1


ΑΘΗΝΑ: 16:00 Πλ. Κλαυθμώνος


ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗ: 17:00 Πολυτεχνείο ΑΠΘ


ΒΟΛΟΣ: 18:00 Θόλος


Φέτος συμπληρώνονται 53 χρόνια από την εξέγερση του Πολυτεχνείου, την κορυφαία στιγμή του αντιδικτατορικού και αντιιμπεριαλιστικού αγώνα στον ελλαδικό χώρο. Μέσα στο φλεγόμενο διεθνές κλίμα της εποχής, η εξέγερση του Νοέμβρη συνδέθηκε άρρηκτα με τα παγκόσμια κινήματα, τον Μάη του ’68 στη Γαλλία και τις απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις σε Χιλή και Ταϊλάνδη, μέχρι το τεράστιο αντιπολεμικό κίνημα αλληλεγγύης στο Βιετνάμ. Η λαϊκή ορμή, με πυροδότη τη νεολαία, λειτούργησε ως καταλύτης για τη ριζοσπαστικοποίηση των μαζών και ως τροχοπέδη στα σχέδια του ιμπεριαλισμού και της ντόπιας αστικής τάξης.


Έξι χρόνια πριν από την εξέγερση, στις 21 Απριλίου 1967 η Χούντα πήρε σάρκα και οστά με στρατιωτικούς όρους. Προέκυψε ως λύση της εγχώριας αστικής τάξης –στον βαθμό εξάρτησης της από τον αμερικανικό ιμπεριαλισμό– απέναντι στην εξάντληση των μεταπολεμικών μηχανισμών ενσωμάτωσης των λαϊκών δυνάμεων, σε μια περίοδο έντονων γεωπολιτικών διεργασιών. Κεντρικό ρόλο στην επιβολή και υποστήριξή της είχαν οι ΗΠΑ-ΚΥΠ, καθ’ υπόδειξη των οποίων υλοποιήθηκε ο σχεδιασμός της. Το καθεστώς εξάντλησε το αντικομμουνιστικό του μένος με απαγορεύσεις, διώξεις, βασανιστήρια και φυλακίσεις. Στοχοποίησε κάθε αγωνιστή και αντιφρονούντα, εξυπηρετώντας τους ιμπεριαλιστικούς σχεδιασμούς ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ, με απώτερο σκοπό τη διάλυση των εργατικών πολιτικών οργανώσεων και συνδικάτων και την ανεμπόδιστη κερδοφορία των καπιταλιστών.


Σήμερα, μέσα σε ένα κλίμα οξυμένων ιμπεριαλιστικών ανταγωνισμών, αλλά και των λαϊκών και προλεταριακών …

author: Perseus
title: Η είσοδος των αναρχικών στο Πολυτεχνείο, η κατάληψη του Γκίνη και το άνοιγμα της πύλης της Στουρνάρη (Βίντεο)
content:
Η είσοδος των αναρχικών στο Πολυτεχνείο, η κατάληψη του Γκίνη και το άνοιγμα της πύλης της Στουρνάρη (Βίντεο)


Πλάνα από όσα συνέβησαν στην πάνω πλευρά του Πολυτεχνείου την Κυριακή 15 Νοέμβρη 2026, όταν συγκροτημένο σώμα αναρχικών αψηφώντας τις απαγορεύσεις και την καταστολή, κατέλαβε το κτίριο Γκίνη εν όψει του τριημέρου για την φοιτητική εξέγερση του πολυτεχνείου το 1973. 


Video

 by AthinaFassa @Kinimatini


Thumbnail photo: @hekate.o (Instagram)


Ακολουθεί η σχετική ανακοίνωση της Κατάληψης Γκίνη “Μιχάλης Καλτεζάς”:


Καταλαμβάνουμε και ζωντανεύουμε ξανά το ιστορικό κτίριο

Γκίνη


Ενάντια στις απαγορεύσεις, την αποστείρωση και την καταστολή


Υπερασπιζόμαστε την εξεγερτική παράδοση του Πολυτεχνείου


Περιφρουρούμε την ακηδεμόνευτη πολιτική μας παρουσία στο τριήμερο 15-17 Νοεμβρίου 2026


Εδώ και δεκαετίες, κράτος και κεφάλαιο επιχειρούν μεθοδικά να επιβάλλουν τους όρους της καπιταλιστικής κανονικότητας, της απόλυτης πειθαρχίας και εν τέλει μιας υποταγμένης ζωής, προσπαθώντας να διαμορφώσουν τους πολιτικούς, κοινωνικούς και ταξικούς συσχετισμούς εντος των κοινωνιών για να εδραιωθεί στη συλλογική συνείδηση το “τέλος της ιστορίας”


Οι εξεγερτικές και επαναστατικές παραδόσεις με τα απελευθερωτικά προτάγματα και τις πολύμορφες δράσεις πρέπει αποσυντεθούν εντός της ιστορικής λήθης, προκειμένου να αποδεχτούν οι καταπιεσμένοι και οι υποτελείς τάξεις ότι το κρατικοκαπιλιστικό οικοδόμημα είναι μονόδρομος. Το όραμα για μια κοινωνία ισότητας και αλληλεγγύης, συλλογικής αντίστασης και ανατροπής, οφείλει να εξοβελιστεί για την επικράτηση των κυρίαρχων αξιών της εκμετάλλευσης, του ατομικισμού και της παραίτησης.


Όμως όσα και να μηχανεύονται οι κυρίαρχοι αυτού του σάπιου κόσμου, οι αντιστάσεις των καταπιεσμένων ξεφυτρώνουν ανα τη γη ανεξέλεγκτα και γεωμετρικά, με τις τελευταίες μόνο εξεγέρσεις σε Γαλλία και Αλβανία και το μπαράζ κοινωνικών διεκδικήσεων και συγκρούσεων σε Σερβία, Ιταλία, Πορτογαλία, Ισπανία,κι αλλού, να υπενθυμίζουν πως “τίποτα δεν τελείωσε”.


Εξέγερση ενάντια στην υποτίμηση των ζωών μας


Σε μια παγκόσμια συνθήκη πολλαπλών και διαδοχικών κρίσεων, ολοένα και μεγαλύτερα κοινωνικά κομμάτια ασφυκτιούν μπροστά στη δυσκολία εκπλήρωσης βασικών αναγκών, όπως η διατροφή και η στέγαση, λόγω του αυξανόμενου κόστους διαβίωσης που σαρώνει πλέον ακόμη και τις λεγόμενες εύρωστες οικονομίες. Η πιεστική αυτή συνθήκη έχει βγάλει στους δρόμους εκατομμύρια διαδηλωτές, που παρά την αυξημένη καταστολή συνεχίζουν τις κινητοποιήσεις, τις απεργίες, τις συγκρούσεις, τους εμπρησμούς κτιρίων και τις απαλλοτριώσεις υλικών αγαθών.


Την ίδια στιγμή, οι αγώνες ενάντια στη φτωχοποίηση και την υποτίμηση των ζωών μας συναντώνται με τη διευρυνόμενη αντίδραση για την εξάπλωση των πολεμικών μετώπων, για την οργανωμένη και σύσσωμη πολεμική προετοιμασία των κρατών και το αντίστοιχο αυξανόμενο πολλαπλό κόστος που πληρώνουν οι εκμεταλλευόμενοι και καταπιεσμένοι σε όλες τις εκφάνσεις της καθημερινότητας. Η νέα πολεμική κανονικότητα είναι εδώ, και δεν μπορεί κανείς πλέον να κλείνει τα μάτια.


Με τη γενοκτονία και τις σφαγές στα κατεχόμενα παλαιστινιακά εδάφη να συνεχίζονται από την πολιτικοστρατιωτική συμμαχία ΗΠΑ-Ισραήλ και των υπολοίπων κρατών συνοδοιπόρων τους-συμπεριλαμβανομένου του ελληνικού- τη Μέση Ανατολή να φλέγεται σχεδόν στο σύνολό της, τον πόλεμο Ρωσίας/Ουκρανίας-ΝΑΤΟ να μαίνεται στην καρδιά της Ευρώπης, τα μέτωπα του πολέμου πληθαίνουν, αφήνοντας πίσω χιλιάδες νεκρούς, πόλεις και οικοσυστήματα κατεστραμμένα. Στα ενεργά πολεμικά μέτωπα, ολόκληροι πληθυσμοί αντιμετωπίζονται ως αναλώσιμη ύλη, ως ζωές που δεν μετράνε. Όπως δεν μετράνε δεκαετίες τώρα οι ζωές των μεταναστριών, που δολοφονούνται στα θαλάσσια και χερσαία σύνορα της Ευρώπης-Φρούριο, που βασανίζονται από τα σώματα ασφαλείας και φυλακίζονται στα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης στο εσωτερικό των “δυτικών παραδείσων” ως ζωές μη άξιες να βιωθούν.


Η απειλή του πολέμου ως διαρκής συνθήκη


Μέσα σε αυτό το περιβάλλον, όπου η απειλή του πολέμου γίνεται διαρκής συνθήκη και οι σειρήνες της παγκόσμιας πολεμικής σύρραξης ηχούν πιο δυνατά, τα κράτη αναδιατάσσονται και εντείνουν τους μεταξύ τους ανταγωνισμούς, τόσο εντός όσο και μεταξύ των μπλοκ εξουσίας στα οποία συστρατεύονται. Επενδύουν στον μιλιταρισμό, καλλιεργούν τον φόβο και επιβάλλουν την κοινωνική πειθάρχηση, οχυρώνονται πίσω από εθνικιστικές και πατριωτικές κορώνες, που προσφέρουν το εύφορο έδαφος για να βγαίνουν από τις τρύπες τους τα φασιστικά σκουπιδια και τα ακροδεξιά τάγματα εφόδου, και να εντείνουν τη δράση τους χύνοντας το …

author: ACG
title: When Anarchism Ceases to Be Anarchist: Liberalism, Subjectivism and the Loss of the Revolutionary Horizon
content:
Below is the second of two texts produced by Spanish libertarian writers., this time from a member of the Spanish anarchist organisation Liza, based in  Granada and Madrid. We reproduce these texts, not because we necessarily agree 100 per cent with their arguments, but because they make valuable and stimulating arguments, necessary for the strengthening and development of anarchist  communism.


There is a discussion within anarchism that for too long has been relegated to the background. It is not a question of determining who possesses an anarchist certificate of authenticity or of establishing a doctrinal orthodoxy. It is a question of examining what conception of society, freedom, power, conflict and social transformation really sustains a given position and what political consequences follow from it.


Table of Contents


Anarchism is not only a negation of the state, an abstract defence of individual freedom, a cultural sensibility, or a collection of horizontal practices. In the anarchist tradition, emancipation implies transforming the social relations of domination and developing forms of self-management capable of replacing them through a revolutionary process. Felipe Corrêa has synthesised this conception through three articulated elements: revolution, critique of domination and defence of self-management.


This definition allows us to establish a fundamental starting point. Anarchism cannot be defined only by what it rejects. Its specificity also lies in the social relations it seeks to build and in the forces capable of making them possible. The question is not only whether a position is anti-state, anti-capitalist or pro-freedom, but also to determine what it means by these concepts, what social relations it identifies as the foundation of domination and how it intends to transform them.


It is from this perspective that it becomes important to examine the liberal and subjectivist influences that run through certain sectors of contemporary anarchism. The problem is not the intellectual origin of each concept considered in isolation. This is what happens when certain categories modify the way in which society is understood to the point of displacing the analysis of social relations, organisation and revolution.


1. Liberalism does not necessarily enter through the front door


When one speaks of liberal influences within anarchism, the most immediate reaction is to seek an explicit defence of the market, private property, or the minimal state. That search can overlook much deeper forms of influence.


Luigi Fabbri already warned about the so-called “bourgeois influences” within anarchism. The problem was not necessarily that the anarchists affected by them consciously became defenders of the bourgeoisie. It consisted of the incorporation of categories produced by bourgeois society that could alter the understanding of organisation, solidarity, social struggle and revolution.


Liberal influence can operate, therefore, by preserving the libertarian vocabulary while transforming the categories through which reality is interpreted. Autonomy, freedom, resistance or emancipation can maintain a radical appearance while detached from the material relations that provide them with political content.


Displacement appears when the individual becomes the privileged unit of analysis, when autonomy is separated from collective organisation, when immediate resistance replaces strategy, or when subjective will begins to explain phenomena determined by historical relations. It also appears when identity displaces material positions, when personal transformation is presented as equivalent to social transformation, or when the critique of the State replaces the analysis of the relations of domination in which it is inserted.


It is not a question of affirming that every defence of individual autonomy is liberal. Nor is it a question of reducing anarchism to a sociology of classes. The question is different. The individual and the collective are not confronting realities. They are in a historical relationship of mutual constitution. The individual acts within social relations that he has not created and these relations can be reproduced or transformed through conscious and collective action.


Ideological filtering becomes problematic precisely when this relationship breaks down and one of its terms goes on to explain the other. When society appears as the result of autonomous individuals who subsequently relate …

Anarchism and art: Democracy in the cracks and on the margins. Mark Mattern. State University of New York Press, x+187 pp., ISBN: 978-1-4384-5920-2

Anarchism and Art takes its cue from British theorist Colin Ward’s observation that anarchist modes of social organizing can multiply and exist side-by-side with and ‘in spite of’ antithetical authoritarian societal ‘trends’ (p. 5). These practices are regarded as prefigurative: they model aspects of the future society anarchists seek to establish (p. 2). As such, anarchists regard them as powerful tools for revolutionizing the entire political, social, and economic order in times of upheaval (Gordon, 2007, p. 38). We have an unfolding example of what this entails in northern Syria, where anarchists have seized territory in three decentralized ‘cantons’ and are remodeling society based, in part, on anti-sexist organizing pioneered by fighters in the People’s Defence Forces and Women’s Defence Units (Strangers in a Tangled Wilderness, 2015, pp. 33–35). However, perusing Anarchism and Art for a discussion of prefiguration’s role in anti-state social transformation is a futile exercise. ‘Revolution’ does not even make it to the index.

Instead, Mattern subsumes anarchist modes of prefiguation within a ‘participatory democracy’ model of social change that ‘does not advocate the complete abolition of the state’ (p. 29). Over a page and a half, he sketches out his hypothetical program for reconstructing society along ‘participatory democracy’ lines, effectively purging anarchism’s anti-statist history and principles from his framework (pp. 21–22). This echoes the argumentative style of philosopher Simon Critchley, who, with a cursory nod toward contemporary anarchist-inspired activism, has coined his own hypothetical formulation, ‘neo-anarchism,’ to encapsulate a ‘politics at a distance from the state’ perpetually incapable of superseding what it opposes, a formulation Critchley champions in his much-praised statement, Infinitively Demanding, as the only option for ‘new social mobilizations’ (Critchley, 2008, p. 148).

What we have, then, is a study that must, perforce, decouple its field of inquiry from post-statist ends to make its case. Accordingly, Mattern gently nudges the movement’s revolutionary ambitions regarding ‘state and capital’ to the sidelines, suggesting that ‘in the last several decades’ anarchists have ‘broadened’ their ‘focus’ to encompass other pressing matters, notably animal rights, the environmental crisis, patriarchy, white supremacy, speciesism, and heterosexism (p. 30). In fact, anarchists have long engaged with such issues, and the implication that they are now treated as spheres of domination apart from ‘state and capital’ is disingenuous (Gelderloos, 2010); but on the plus side, putting ‘state and capital’ in its place helps grease the elision of ‘anarchism’ with ‘participatory …

I RESOLUTION DU CONGRES NATIONAL DE L’UNIONE SINDACALE ITALIANA (PARME — DECEMBRE 1919) :

II RAPPORT SUR LES « CONSEILS D’USINES ET D’ENTREPRISES » PRESENTE PAR MAURIZIO GARINO AU CONGRES DE L’UNION ANARCHISTE ITALIENNE (tenu à Bologne du 1er au 4 juillet 1920).

UN MOUVEMENT QUI A SON HISTOIRE

LES NOUVELLES CLASSES OUVRIERES

V. GRIFFUELHES LE SYNDICALISME REVOLUTIONNAIRE

L’histoire des classes ouvrières, de leur mode de vie, de leur statut, de leur fonction ; celle des poussées ou des explosions de ces mêmes classes ; celle enfin des organisations et des idéologies qui s’efforcent ou affirment en exprimer les volontés, le rôle ou le destin, sont évidemment imbriquées, interdépendantes, mais elles ne sont pas identiques. Cette constatation banale est souvent oubliée dans les polémiques ou les affrontements entre les diverses écoles socialistes.

Chaque fraction a tendance à substituer à la société ouvrière complexe, intégrée dans une société globale en mouvement, une image, ou une formule, dont elle se sert pour construire ses hypothèses, justifier sa politique, tracer ses perspectives. Si bien que les débats se nourrissent de mots ou de schémas, parfois vrais à l’origine, parce que correspondant à un moment ou à un lieu déterminés de la mêlée sociale, mais qui finissent avec le temps, par ne plus être que des pièces de musée. Ce qui fait des discussions une bataille vaine, détachée des réalités, à peine humanisée par la nostalgie des anciens ou le besoin d’exaltation des nouveaux. Et l’extrême érudition finit par brouiller la connaissance des banalités du présent visible.

Même le syndicalisme révolutionnaire - ou syndicalisme libertaire, ou anarcho-syndicalisme - n’échappe pas à cette regrettable pratique. Et pourtant il n’est pas né bien net, défini et définitif. Il n’acquiert ses caractéristiques qu’après avoir passé par une série d’expériences, il est produit de ces expériences, et il ne cessera pas de prendre forme, d’acquérir son langage, de s’enrichir d’idées-forces et de méthodes d’action, d’être partiellement ou totalement absorbé par la société totale.

Dans son travail sur les Bourses du Travail et la C.G.T., publié aux environs de 1910, Paul Delesalle constate et prévoit ces naturelles transformations : « ce qui caractérise le mouvement syndicaliste français, c’est son évolution constante ». Dans une classe ouvrière produite par une société déterminée, les formes d’organisation sont multiples, de même que les idéologies qui habillent ou utilisent ces organisations sont diverses. Le syndicalisme révolutionnaire ne sort pas du cerveau d’un théoricien. Il est pratique qui cherche une doctrine pour se propager et se multiplier.

La variété des situations, des cas, des tentatives, se montre infiniment plus riche que les formulations les plus subtiles. Et tel qui avait raison en une conjoncture précise, se trouve dépassé, éliminé quand il s’accroche à ses vérités d’hier pour justifier ses errements d’aujourd’hui. Il nous apparaît donc bien inutile d’établir un modèle unique, et vénérable, d’un syndicalisme révolutionnaire qui, de 1890 à 1976, en Suède comme en Espagne, aux Etats-Unis comme au Japon, en Argentine comme en Italie, se serait manifesté suivant des canons identiques. Non plus que d’en figer les traits ou les objectifs présents. Ni même de l’opposer à des formes ou des conceptions d’organisation révolutionnaire présentées comme mieux enracinées dans les classes productrices et reflétant plus naturellement leurs intérêts ou leurs espoirs.

Ce serait oublier l’essentiel, à savoir la nature propre, conditionnée, multiple, normalement contradictoire, du syndicalisme révolutionnaire, pour la vaine commodité d’une querelle de mots. Alors qu’hier comme aujourd’hui nous fournissent un matériel humain et des situations sociales en abondance. La vie quotidienne des classes ouvrières, la vie …

title: 19-летнего анархиста Дмитрия Сюткина приговорили к 9 годам заключения
content:
19-летнего анархиста Дмитрия Сюткина приговорили к 9 годам заключения по «террористическим» статьям. В то же время в суд поступило новое дело против него — о госизмене.

Центральный окружной военный суд в Екатеринбурге вынес приговор 19-летнему уральскому анархисту Дмитрию Сюткину — 9 лет заключения. Об этом он сам сообщил в письме, которое его собеседница получила 13 ноября.

Неизвестно, когда именно был оглашен этот приговор — карточка дела на сайте ЦОВС до сих пор не опубликована, даже в обезличенном виде. Известно только, что Сюткина обвиняли сразу по семи уголовным статьям: «подготовка к теракту» (часть 1 статьи 30 УК, часть 1 статьи 205 УК), «cклонение к террористической деятельности иного лица» (часть 1.1 статьи 205.1 УК), «публичное оправдание терроризма» (часть 2 статьи 205.2 УК), «участие в террористическом сообществе» (часть 2 статьи 205.4 УК), «участие в террористической организации» (часть 2 статьи 205.5 УК), незаконное хранение и незаконное изготовление взрывчатки (часть 1 статьи 222.1 УК и часть 1 статьи 223.1 УК).

Как заметили «Огни свободы», 9 ноября в Свердловский областной суд поступило еще одно уголовное дело против Сюткина — «о государственной измене» (275 УК). Первое заседание назначено уже на 23 ноября. Дела по этой статье всегда рассматриваются российскими судами в закрытом режиме, без слушателей.

Впервые Диму задержали в возрасте 16 лет в 2023 году из-за поста, посвященного сбору на адвоката для одного из поджигателей военкомата. Тогда подростка опросили и отпустили.

Вскоре с ним связался «куратор» из Сибирского батальона, который предложил Диме «помощь с выездом за границу». author: Das Eclipse-Komitee
title: Die extreme Rechte mit antiautoritären Aktionen verdunkeln
content:
Anfang 2026 haben Anarchist:innen in Großbritannien zu die folgende Kampagne öffentlich gemacht. Bis zur Wahl 2029 treffen sie sich zu vier Kongressen, nehmen jeweils an den 1.-Mai-Demos in eigenen Blöcken teil und werden am Wahltag ihren Widerstand gegen die Herrschaftsordnung erklären. Dabei verfolgen sie den Ansatz, verschiedene anarchistische Strömungen zusammen zu bringen. Sie gründen keine neue Föderation, sondern streben an, bestehende anarchistische Strukturen und Gruppen zu stärken und zu verbinden. Unter anderem stellen sie dazu diese Zines zur Verfügung: https://wearetheeclipse.com/flyers-and-zines/ Hier findet sich der „Über“ und das „Manifest“.


ÜBER (die Eclipse-Kampagne) von: https://wearetheeclipse.com/about/


Eclipse 2029 ist ein Projekt zur Wiederbelebung der anarchistischen Bewegung im Vereinigten Königreich, um dem Narrativ des Wahlkampfs entgegenzuwirken und unsere Fähigkeiten zu stärken, Widerstand gegen eine voraussichtlich an die Macht kommende rechtsextreme Regierung zu leisten.


Wir streben den Aufbau einer widerstandsfähigen Gemeinschaft durch eine Reihe jährlicher Zusammenkünfte an (die jeweils mit einer Sonnenfinsternis zusammenfallen und bis zur Wahl im Jahr 2029 stattfinden).


Wir wollen eine gemeinsame Plattform für gegenseitige Verteidigung und Zusammenarbeit zwischen anarchistischen Gruppen schaffen und zudem autonome direkte Aktionen von Affinitätsgruppen unter dem Namen „Eclipse-Komitees“ fördern. Die Plattform wird in Form einer Website und von Publikationen einen sichtbaren Raum bieten, um diese Aktionen zu teilen und die Bewegung miteinander zu vernetzen.


Jedes Treffen wird einem bestimmten Zweck dienen, um zum Aufbau der Bewegung beizutragen.


Das erste Treffen im Februar 2026 zielt darauf ab, bestehende anarchistische Gruppen zusammenzubringen, um gemeinsame Grundsätze für strategische und taktische Einheit zu entwickeln, nach denen wir arbeiten können. Damit soll ein Raum für die Kommunikation zwischen verschiedenen Projekten und Gruppen geschaffen und der Austausch von Fähigkeiten und Ressourcen gefördert werden, um unsere gemeinsamen Ziele zu erreichen.


Das zweite Treffen wird sich auf den Austausch von Kompetenzen und die Bildung neuer Affinitätsgruppen – „Eclipse-Komitees“ – konzentrieren, die in ihrem lokalen Umfeld aktiv werden sollen.


Das dritte Treffen wird ein breiterer Aufruf an Nicht-Anarchist*innen sein, den Wahlkampf abzulehnen und sich unserem Widerstand anzuschließen.


Wir werden jedes Jahr Blöcke bei den Maikundgebungen organisieren, um diese für die anarchistische Bewegung zurückzugewinnen, und wir werden am Tag der Parlamentswahl eine Demonstration organisieren, bei der wir die Gründung unserer Widerstandsbewegung offiziell verkünden werden.


DAS MANIFEST DES ECLIPSE-KOMITEES


Brennt in euch nicht die Wut unter der beunruhigenden Sonne dieses Imperiums?


Etwas läuft grundlegend schief. Trotz all der Arbeit, die wir in den Aufbau einer neuen Welt gesteckt haben, sind die Probleme der gegenwärtigen Welt nach wie vor allgegenwärtig. So können wir nicht weitermachen: wirkungslos, zersplittert und ängstlich. Wir können es uns nicht leisten, das Feuer in unseren Herzen zu verraten, indem wir weiterhin so tun, als wären wir machtlos.


Wie lange können wir das noch ertragen?


Wir können Widerstand leisten und neue Visionen entwickeln. In unseren Gemeinschaften. In unserem Alltag.


Dies ist ein Aufruf, uns zu versammeln.


Wir werden nichts von dem korrupten Staat verlangen, der uns in diese Lage gebracht hat. Stattdessen fragen wir uns: Wie können wir die Macht nutzen, die wir haben? Wie werden wir eine Welt schaffen, die dem Ansturm eines sich rasch entfaltenden Krieges gegen uns, eines Krieges gegen das Volk, Widerstand leistet?


Draußen zeichnet sich eine komplexe Landschaft ab, und wir können sie untergraben. Gemeinsam. Wir können uns der Unausweichlichkeit widersetzen und sie verhindern, dass die extreme Rechte bei den bevorstehenden Parlamentswahlen 2029 neue Schrecken für unsere Gemeinschaften hervorbringt.


Könnt ihr euch eine Sonnenfinsternis vorstellen und spüren, wie sich ihre Freiheit nähert?


Die Kräfte des imperialen Kapitalismus, des Patriarchats und der Zerstörung werden zunehmend instabil. Der Neoliberalismus verfault zum Faschismus. Das globale Imperium bricht zusammen, während unser Planet zerstört wird und Millionen unter Kriegen und ökologischer Zerstörung leiden.

An Anarchist FAQ

The Anarchist FAQ presents a compelling vision of parenting based on freedom, mutual respect and trust in children’s natural capacity for self-regulation, challenging the authoritarian assumptions embedded in conventional family structures. Its strongest contribution is connecting the personal and political, arguing that raising children without coercion, punishment or imposed moralism is itself a form of anarchist practice. It places freedom, mutual respect and autonomy at the heart of parenting. It challenges us to reject the authoritarian structures of the traditional family and recognise that raising free, confident and independent children is an essential part of building a free society.

Introduction:

What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Anarchists have long been aware of the importance of child rearing and education. We are aware that child rearing should aim to develop

“a well-rounded individuality”

 and not

“a patient work slave, professional automaton, tax-paying citizen, or righteous moralist.”

 In this section of the FAQ [see

here

] we will discuss anarchist approaches to child rearing bearing in mind

“that it is through the channel of the child that the development of the mature man [or woman] must go, and that the present ideas of . . . educating or training . . . are such as to stifle the natural growth of the child.”

 [Emma Goldman,

Red Emma Speaks

, p. 132 and p. 131]


If one accepts the thesis that the authoritarian family is the breeding ground for both individual psychological problems and political reaction, it follows that anarchists should try to develop ways of raising children that will not psychologically cripple them but instead enable them to accept freedom and responsibility while developing natural self-regulation. We will refer to children raised in such a way as

“free children.”


Work in this field is still in its infancy (no pun intended). Wilhelm Reich was the main pioneer in this field (an excellent, short introduction to his ideas can be found in Maurice Brinton’s

The Irrational in Politics

). In

Children of the Future

, Reich made numerous suggestions, based on his research and clinical experience, for parents, psychologists, and educators striving to develop libertarian methods of child rearing (although he did not use the term “libertarian”).


In this and the following sections we will summarise Reich’s main ideas as well as those of other libertarian psychologists and educators who have been influenced by him, such as A.S. Neill and Alexander Lowen. We will examine the theoretical principles involved in raising free children and will illustrate their practical application with concrete examples. Finally, we will examine the anarchist approach to the problems of adolescence.


Such an approach to child rearing is based upon the insight that children

“do not constitute anyone’s property: they are neither the property of the parents nor even of society. They belong only to their own future freedom.”

 [Michael Bakunin,

The Political Philosophy of Bakunin

, p. 327] As such, what happens to a child when they are growing up

shapes

 the person they become and the society they live in. The key question for people interested in freedom is whether

“the child [is] to be considered as an individuality, or as an object to be moulded according to the whims and fancies of those about it?”

 [Emma Goldman,

Op. Cit.

, p. 131] Libertarian child rearing is the means by which the individuality of the child is respected and developed.


This is in stark contrast to standard capitalist claim that children are the

property

 of their parents …

author: The Elephant
title: Alternative Leadership As A Decolonial Paradigm
content:
Sarova Stanley, Nairobi | 11 November 2026


Theme: Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency


Dr. Kawive Wambua;


The leadership and team of Inuka Kenya Ni Sisi!;

Representatives of civil society;

Distinguished guests;

Fellow Kenyans:


Good morning.


Thank you for inviting me to join you at the launch of the Inuka! Angaza Kura Campaign.


Your theme, “Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency,” brings us to the central question of our democracy: The Constitution proclaims Sovereignty of the people, but who truly exercises power in Kenya?


Is it the citizen whose taxes sustain the state, whose labour builds the economy, and whose vote confers authority? Or is it the officeholder who, once elected, hijacks power and behaves like the master, relegating citizens to subjects?


What must the citizens do to reclaim their agency, their power? 


You have asked me to reflect on “Alternative Leadership as a Decolonial Paradigm.”


The language may sound academic, but the issue is profoundly practical.


It concerns the relationship between a Kenyan citizen and the person entrusted to serve them. It concerns whether a police officer offers protection or inspires fear; whether a public office provides a service or demands a favour; whether public money builds opportunity or finances private privilege.


Above all, it concerns whether independence has become an everyday experience of dignity and quality services for us. 


From subjects to citizens


The colonial state was organised to control people and extract resources. Its authority flowed downwards. The population was expected to comply, while those who governed were insulated from meaningful accountability to the governed.


Independence was supposed to transform that relationship.


Yet changing the nationality of those occupying public office could not, by itself, dismantle the habits, incentives and institutions of domination, without changing the mindset of the office holders. Understanding leadership to be service and sacrifice, rather than entitlement and a life of privilege at the expense of basic needs for the people. Imagining leadership as an opportunity to ensure protection of the rights of the people and to uphold and affirm the dignity of the people you serve. Ensuring that, as a leader, you remain loyal to the purpose- service with openness and accountability. These are the minimum standards demanded by the constitution we gifted ourselves. 


Whenever leadership demands obedience without accountability, the colonial model or inheritance survives. Whenever citizens must seek political patronage to obtain public services, it survives. Whenever criticism is treated as disloyalty, it survives.


Decolonising leadership therefore requires us to confront the exercise of power in our own time.


We must ask whether the state serves citizens as people with rights, or manages them as subjects who should remain grateful for favours.


A hospital is a public responsibility. A road is a public investment. Education is an investment in the nation’s future. Every service by leaders is part of their duty to us, funded by our taxes, not a favour. 


None of these should become a personal gift for which citizens owe a politician their silence. Service should not be in exchange for citizens losing their freedom to exercise their right to demand accountability. Service must never be at the cost of citizens losing their agency, their power to oversee leaders, the government. 


An alternative must be radically different in word and deed. 


Comrades,


The word “alternative” carries an obligation.


Those of us who seek to offer alternative leadership must demonstrate how we would govern differently. We must affirm our allegiance to the Constitution, whose main objective is to restrain, or in other words, limit the exercise of power.  Alternative leadership must affirm citizens’ right to seek accountability and readiness to vacate office should citizens unequivocally so demand. The Alternative leadership must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and the people of Kenya, and affirm the sovereignty of the people. Demonstrate an understanding that leadership is a privilege to serve, not a title deed to rule over the people. Our utterances and actions as alternative leadership must so demonstrate. 


It is insufficient to condemn arrogance in government while practising it within our political parties. We cannot promise inclusion while silencing young …

Given that we live in a society that promotes ignorance and superficiality, perhaps it shouldn’t be all that surprising that current day anarchist discussions of historic inter-anarchist debates usually miss the point when it comes to colonialism (and imperialism more generally.)

Anarchists do not somehow become immune to colonial society’s influence simply by making abstract and hollow declarations of opinion. Knowledge and comprehension require actual commitment and curiosity, and these are sadly rare qualities among the European, Euro-American and Euro-Canadian anarchists of today.

This article is an attempt at a brief analysis of what’s been missing in recent anarchist discussions of three historic inter-anarchist debates. The term “debates” is used here in the widest sense of a general disagreement rather than some formally-held event or correspondence. Specifically, I refer to the debates between Luigi Galleani and Ricardo Flores Magón over the Mexican Revolution, between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta on the First World War, and between Emma Goldman and Reginald Reynolds on Palestine.

In the case of Reynolds, we should note that he considered himself a fellow traveler and sympathizer of anarchism, wrote regularly for the anarchist periodicals edited by Vernon Richards, and married the socialist-turned-anarchist Ethel Mannin, but did not self-identify as an anarchist, so my phrase “inter-anarchist debate” must also be understood in the broadest sense.

The anarchist periodical Tinderbox and the anarchist website The Transmetropolitan Review (TTR) have recently invoked the Galleani-Magón debate, though without even being aware of it in the former case.

The individual who writes articles at the TTR website claimed in May of this year that the historic anarchist Partido Liberal Mexicano (PLM) made a “fateful alliance with Pascual Orozco,” the latter being a bourgeois revolutionary who, with the help of Pancho Villa, took control of Ciudad Juárez in 1911. The author makes no distinction between the on-the-ground forces of the PLM and the Junta (leadership board) of that organization, which, from Los Angeles obviously could not directly control the actions of every individual on the frontlines in Mexico, even if they had wanted to.

TTR goes on to sell the lie that at the time, “the PLM was willing to work with anyone against Madero, and they took positions in Orozco’s rebel government alongside oligarchs and hacienda owners, something which further isolated the PLM from anarchists.”

In reality, Magón and the rest of the Junta, in their periodical, Regeneración, called for violent resistance to Orozco once he took control of Juárez, denouncing him as bourgeois and openly accusing him of being on the wrong side of the revolution, specifically because he was trying to disarm other revolutionaries and was friendly with the rich.

To be clear where TTR wasn’t, the anarchists they claim the PLM isolated …
