author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: Scott Timcke
title: The Stories Shaping Africa’s AI Future
content:
In the boardrooms of Addis Ababa and the tech hubs of Nairobi, a new worldmaking project is underway. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the central arenas where African states negotiate their position in an unequal global order. To speak of “AI in Africa” is not simply to describe the arrival of a technology, but to encounter a set of competing discursive frames through which political desires, developmental ambitions, ethical claims, and governance priorities are translated into technical agendas. As national strategies and regional protocols are rolled out, what comes into view is a struggle over how Africa is imagined within this machine age, and what kinds of futures that imagination makes thinkable.


These frames are not simply different ways of describing a new technology. They are competing scripts for what Africa is, what AI is for, and who ought to shape its future. Some cast the continent as a site of leapfrogging and renewal; others as a zone of exposure, extraction, sovereignty, moral repair, or improvised adaptation. Each brings some actors and possibilities into focus while pushing others to the margins. That is why the issue is not only what AI means for Africa, but what pictures of Africa are being called into view through AI discourse.


The first terrain is shaped by promise and protection. One of the most pervasive registers is promissory. In the African renaissance 2.0 frame, visible in the

AU Continental AI Strategy

, AI appears as a

leapfrogging

 device through which Africa can bypass the chokepoint of traditional industrialization and enter prosperity through technical modernization. Here, the ethical subject is the developmental state or planner charged with delivering growth, inclusion, and renewal. What comes into view is capacity, competitiveness, and beneficial transformation. What recedes from view are the historical and political-economic conditions that make acceleration so attractive in the first place: debt, infrastructural dependence, uneven ownership, and the possibility that AI may deepen rather than overcome inherited asymmetries.


Running alongside this is a protective register. In this vulnerability frame, Africa is not late but exposed to surveillance, bias, exclusion, and systems introduced into settings where safeguards are weak and redress is limited. As the

CIVICUS report on AI surveillance in Africa

 suggests, the issue is not only future risk but already existing forms of technologically mediated harm. The ethical subject here is the harm-bearing population—the data subject, precarious worker, surveilled citizen, and linguistically marginal user most likely to absorb the costs of badly governed AI. This frame is ethically indispensable because it foregrounds rights, harm, and institutional fragility, including the uneven but growing architecture of data protection on the continent. Its limit, however, is that it can cast Africa chiefly as a site to be protected rather than one from which technological futures are actively contested and shaped.


A second terrain is shaped by structure and sovereignty. Alongside these promissory and protective registers sits a more structural critique. In the

anti-colonial frame

, AI appears as a socio-technical order built through unequal material relations: not only data extraction, but also mineral supply chains, outsourced labor, environmental degradation, foreign-owned infrastructures, and asymmetrical control over the institutions that govern digital life. From this perspective, Africa is not outside the AI order looking in; it is already deeply inserted into it, though often on subordinated terms. The ethical subject is the dispossessed worker, community, or polity whose labor, resources, and data are drawn into AI systems while ownership and value are captured elsewhere. What becomes visible is the political economy of AI—an approach that makes it harder to sustain the comforting idea that Africa’s main problem is simply one of readiness or delayed entry. But the frame has limits. In foregrounding dispossession, it can flatten internal differentiation, externalize agency too completely, and become so totalizing that the uneven realities of negotiation and strategic inhabitation recede from view.


The sovereignty frame shifts the question from extraction to control: AI is cast as a problem of authority over infrastructure, procurement, standards, and rulemaking, a concern visible in South Africa’s

National …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: CNN, NYT Push Dubious Reports on Iran That Critics Liken to Iraq WMD Lies
content:
The reports seem to manufacture consent for Trump to escalate strikes on Iran and its water infrastructure.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Major corporate media outlets pushed multiple stories on Monday seemingly aimed at manufacturing consent for the U.S. to intensify strikes on Iran and target civilian infrastructure while doing so — reports that were likened by critics to the media’s pro-war propaganda blitz when the U.S. invaded Iraq in the early aughts.

The New York Times published a story that framed dams in Iran as a mysterious “riddle,” with the country having built the “puzzling” water infrastructure for no apparent reason. Dams are used for many reasons — agriculture, manufacturing, energy, flood management, recreation, and to provide populations with water — but the Times, with a heavy hand, suggested that Iran’s dams are used for military purposes.

“Why does it seem that wherever we have dams, there is a missile strike close by?” the Times quoted one Iranian German academic as saying, noting that the U.S. and Israel have carried out many airstrikes near dams during the war. The reporting echoed similar articles in Israeli publications.

The Times even noted Iran’s historic, decades-long water crisis, and observed that dams in Iran often serve civilian purposes; one U.S. strike in July hit a hay storage shed for wild sheep, an environmentalist told the Times. However, the report treats recent arrests of environmentalists in the country as another reason for suspicion, though environmentalists and climate activists are commonly criminalized across the world.

Media critics and opponents of the war expressed anger at the Times report online, saying that it was published to justify the U.S. carrying out strikes on Iran’s water infrastructure — which could lead to disastrous results for the already ailing civilian population.

“Speculation is not evidence. Spatial proximity is not causality. Even those who attacked Iran have not made such claims linking dams to missiles!” wrote Kaveh Madani, former Iranian environmental official and director of the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment, and Health. “This reductionist, sensational narrative is irresponsible journalism with potentially dangerous consequences for civilian water infrastructure.”

Critics had similarly harsh words for CNN after it published a report on Monday evening with an even more provocative claim. CNN asserted, citing U.S. officials, that intelligence sources have supposedly found that Iran is developing plans to use a chemical weapon or radiological device — a “dirty bomb,” as CNN deems it — in Washington, D.C.

The outlet said it’s unclear whether or not Iran would follow through with the supposed plan. Still, it claimed that the Iranian government could use people already inside the U.S. to smuggle bomb materials into the capital, not just drumming up support for preemptive “defensive” strikes on Iran, but also potentially endangering people in the U.S. who the Trump administration may “suspect” are smuggling such weapons.

The Trump administration, accordingly, drummed up bloodthirsty sentiment in response to the report. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that it would “cause an all-out war” if Iran attacked D.C., suggesting that the U.S.-Israeli war that has killed roughly 3,500 people in Iran as of June, damaged thousands of civilian sites, and reportedly wiped out all of Iran’s senior leadership has not already amounted to “all-out war.”

President Donald Trump once again struck a genocidal tone when asked about the report on Tuesday, saying that, if Iran even threatens to attack D.C., “they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before.”

Jake Tapper, who has long been criticized for cheering U.S. and Israeli assaults, featured the report on his evening program.

The report was met with immediate skepticism from critics of the war, however. Critics likened it to the media coverage in the months and years leading up to the U.S.’s invasion of Iraq, when major news outlets breathlessly parroted lies about Saddam Hussein’s “weapons of mass destruction.” The parallels run deep: In December 2002, just months before the invasion, CNN even reported on an intelligence report that suggested that Iraq had a “dirty bomb.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

author: David Swanson
title: Anti-Bases Movement Going Strong on Jeju Island
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, November 17, 2026


The photo above is an old one. The base protest has been happening on Jeju Island for years. Now the destruction has been done, the base been built, and the war ships come and go. On Tuesday, there were no U.S. Navy ships present, just Korean war ships, one of them likely to soon be sent to the war on Iran, as well as a submarine, and Chinese cruise ships arriving. There is also a new rocket-launching platform that is taken out miles off the coast to launch rockets. A week ago, someone

died

 in a rocket operation. Hanwha, the company involved, has many branch corporations. One of them is Hanwha Defense USA which builds U.S. warships in Philadelphia.


The massive base on Jeju Island was created in large part for the U.S. Navy, and the protests denounce the latest U.S. wars.


As part of a display along a road approaching the base is this image of the beloved Gureombi Rock, almost all of which was destroyed by the base construction.


A sign indicates the number of daily protests as of today: 7,124.


Every morning for 7,124 mornings, protesters have taken their message to the base.


Every late-morning for 7,124 late-mornings, a Catholic mass has been followed by a noon protest at the base.


Protesters suspect that this ship, docked at the base, may soon be sent to join Trump’s war on Iran, on behalf of the people of Korea who have zero interest in participating in such reckless, murderous crimes. To the left above is the rocket launcher. Top center is a world cup stadium.

title: Avrupa | Yüzbinlerce genç 20 Kasım'a hazırlanıyor: “Geleceğimiz için, onların savaşlarına karşı”
content:
Gençlik ve öğrenci örgütleri tüm Avrupa ülkelerinde 20 Kasım Cuma günü, “Fight for Our Future, Not Their Wars” (Geleceğimiz için, onların savaşlarına karşı) sloganıyla ortak eylem gününe hazırlanıyor. Uluslararası Gençlik Grevi Koalisyonu'nun 11 Kasım'daki açıklamasına göre 25'i aşkın ülkede kıtadaki yüzlerce kentte okul boykotları, üniversite eylemleri ve gösteriler planlanıyor.


Koalisyon etkinliğe yüz binlerce gencin katılmasını bekliyor. Ancak henüz ülkeler özgülünde doğrulanmış bir katılım tahmini bulunmuyor. 


Savaş değil sosyal haklar için bütçe


Haziranda Köln'deki uluslararası buluşmanın ardından gelişen koalisyon, 10 Ağustos'ta ortak grev çağrısını duyurmuştu. Hareketin manifestosu, askerî harcamaların artırılması ve eğitim, sağlık ve sosyal hizmetlerdeki kesintiler arasındaki dolaysız bağdan yola çıkıyor. Manifesto'nun temel yönelimleri kendi ifadeleriyle şöyle özetleniyor: 


Savaş ve sosyal haklar:


“Askerî harcamalar tarihsel rekor düzeylere ulaşırken eğitim, sağlık, konut ve kamu hizmetleri yeniden silahlanmayı finanse etmek için feda ediliyor.”


Gençliğin geleceği:


“Bu geleceği reddediyoruz.”


Uluslararası örgütlenme:


“Geleceğimizi tehdit eden, bizi sömüren ve baskı altında tutan sistem uluslararası olduğu için mücadelemiz de uluslararasıdır.”


Hareketin siyasal yönelimi:


“Otoriterliğe ve baskıya karşı, demokratik haklarımızı savunmak için köklü bir sistem değişikliği. Irkçılığın ve patriyarkanın sona ermesi, bütün ülkelerde aşırı sağın yenilgiye uğratılması için.”


Manifestonun imzacıları arasında Türkiye'den Özgür Üniversite Hareketi, Almanya'dan YUNA – Demokratische Jugend ve Internationaler Jugend Verband, Avusturya'dan Ronahî – Youth Building Bridges bulunuyor. 


Manifesto, zorunlu askerliğin kaldırılmasını, kamu hizmetlerine yatırım yapılmasını, erişilebilir konutu, iklim adaletini ve demokratik hakların korunmasını talep ediyor. NATO'nun ve Avrupa Birliği'nin yeniden silahlanma politikalarını eleştirirken işgal, sömürgecilik, ırkçılık, patriyarka ve aşırı sağa karşı mücadeleyi de ortak programına dahil ediyor.


Gençlik koalisyonu yalnızca bir günlük protestoyu değil, ülkeler arasında kalıcı bir öğrenci ve gençlik hareketi oluşturmayı hedefliyor. Okul ve üniversite boykotlarının yanı sıra genel toplantılar, yürüyüşler ve işgal eylemleri de tartışılan mücadele biçimleri arasında.


Fransa'dan Almanya'ya: Farklı mücadeleler buluşuyor


Fransa'da liselilerin eğitim koşullarına ve sosyal eşitsizliklere karşı sürdürdükleri protestolar, Avrupa'daki seferberliğinin önemli dayanakları arasında. İtalya'da Rete della Conoscenza ve öğrenci örgütleri, eğitim hakkını ve militarizm karşıtlığını ortak gündeme taşıyor. Birleşik Krallık'ta Socialist Students, 200'ü aşkın okul, kolej ve üniversitede ders bırakma hazırlığı bulunduğunu açıklıyor.


Almanya'da Gen Z regelt girişimi 39 kentte gösteri çağrısı yapıyor. Eğitim ve sağlık hizmetlerinde kesintilere, hayat pahalılığına, iklim politikalarına ve zorunlu askerliğe karşı çıkan hareket, 20 Kasım'ı yeni bir seferberlik aşaması olarak görüyor.


Ancak gençlik hareketinin bütün bileşenleri aynı örgütsel çatı altında değil. Almanya Federal Öğrenci Konferansı, Gen Z regelt'in örgütsel şeffaflığına ilişkin çekinceler ileri sürerek eylemini ayrı düzenliyor.


Uluslararası Barış Bürosu ve Stop ReArm Europe ise 20–22 Kasım arasında “Welfare, not Warfare” (Savaş değil, sosyal refah) sloganıyla sendikaları, barış hareketlerini ve sivil toplum örgütlerini eyleme çağırıyor. Bu etkinlikler gençlik greviyle bağlantılı, ancak ondan ayrı örgütleniyor.


Göçmen gençler hareketin neresinde?


Uluslararası grev manifestosu, ırkçılığa ve aşırı sağa karşı mücadeleyi açıkça ortak talepler arasına alıyor. Ancak göçmen gençlik örgütlerinin koalisyonun yönetiminde ve karar mekanizmalarında nasıl temsil edildiği belirginleşmiş değil.

title: THIS IS FOX HUNTING
content:
The main fox hunting season is now in full swing all over the country and already hunts are doing everything they can to prove to the general public and the government why a full ban on hunting with hounds is needed now. Meanwhile their governing body, the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) are sitting back and allowing the pro hunt community to destroy themselves.


The video above is from the opening meet of the Warwickshire Hunt on the 31

st

 of October 2026 and shows them blatantly hunting a fox. This is just one example, but make no mistake this is happening all over the country week in and week out. 


A fox is shown fleeing from a covert on the Upton Estate, which sits on the border of Oxfordshire and Warwickshire. Moments later hounds are in cry pursuing the fox towards a covert named Shenington Hirons while a young rider is seen tracking the hounds as they hunt the fox, which then attempts to seek refuge in a hedgerow.


A West Midlands Hunt Saboteur is heard informing other sabs that hounds are marking in a hedgerow. The same young rider who was previously seen tracking hounds is sat watching, knowing full well that hounds are indicating they have located a fox. Amongst the supporters who are all eagerly awaiting a chase and a kill, are multiple young children. One even stands on a gate to try and see if the fox will break in front of her.


Supporters stand with young children waiting to see the fox break cover


The fox does break cover right in front of a hound who is immediately on its tail, followed by the rest of the pack. The young rider slowly makes his way to where the fox had broken and half-heartedly says “leave it” before sitting back and watching it unfold.


The fox breaks cover closely followed by hounds


The rider and supporters were well aware a hunt saboteur was filming the entire thing, and this pretence of pretending to stop hounds was not for the benefit of the fox but for the benefit of the cameras. However, everything that had happened before and everything that came afterwards proves that this was meant to be used as yet another smokescreen.


Hounds continued to chase the fox into an unnamed covert before it went to ground on a hill just north of the Macmillan Way. The video shows hounds still pursuing the fox and then again, marking where it has tried to seek refuge. Horse riders sit back and watch it happen, not a single one attempts to stop it, while the huntsman Jack Weedon is trying to hide between coverts, making no attempt to intervene and stop hounds.


A rider sits back and watches as hounds continue to hunt the fox


A hunt saboteur who filmed Weedon sitting back doing nothing, also caught the despicable moment that he struck his horse in frustration. This isn’t the first time Weedon has let his anger get the better of him as he was seen striking a hound at the beginning of the season and has recently received a caution under a Section 4a Public Order Offence. A stipulation of this caution was for Jack to attend an anger management class.


Huntsman Jack Weedon did nothing to intervene and stop hounds


While hounds were chasing the fox a rider was overheard stating that it had gone to ground. Yet again further evidence that the riders present were aware and complicit in the illegal hunting of this fox. As is landowner Robert Waley Cohen who continues to allow the Warwickshire Hunt to use the Upton Estate to hunt wild mammals with dogs. Section 3.1 of the Hunting Act states that if a landowner knowingly permits their land to be used for this purpose, then they too are breaking the law.


Thankfully hunt saboteurs were on hand to document this blatant display of illegal hunting and to save this fox’s life. However, this video demonstrates the impunity with which hunts are operating and shows the intentional recklessness with which they behave.


Thankfully hunt saboteurs were there to film the entire incident and save this fox’s life


They claim to be “trail” hunting but time and time again hounds are caught in hedgerows and impenetrable coverts where no possible trail could have been laid. They are intentionally putting and encouraging hounds into areas where foxes are likely to reside and then people like Warwickshire Hunt chair Sam Butler claim that accidents happen.


No trail has been laid there!

title: Just Released: Video Taken by ALF As They Liberate 9 Mice from University of New Orleans Vivisector Christopher Harshaw
content:
On September 19, 2026, nine female mice (including four so-called “breeding females”) were loaded up and spirited away from a miserable, windowless cinderblock room on the 2nd floor of UNO’s Psychology Building to begin a new life in safety and comfort. Today for the first time, video taken by the Animal Liberation Front(ALF) during the raid is being released, after it was received anonymously and exclusively by the North American Animal Liberation Press Office.

The ALF communique received after the raid can be viewed here. The raw video footage can be viewed in its entirety here. Images in this press release are stills from the footage, are anti-copyrighted and can be used without permission.

The lab was that of Christopher Harshaw, who subjects mice and rats to experiments that purportedly aim to study autism, body temperature regulation and social behavior. This involves injecting them with drugs (such as acetaminophen to induce neurodevelopmental disorders), shutting them into small lighted cabinets overnight, and putting poisonous chemicals into their water like aniline (known to cause blood disorders and spleen tumors in rodents).

Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harwshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.

Per the communique: “To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on sight it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.”

author: Tobias Schalyo
title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt? 


Lea und Josias engagieren sich seit Jahren im Tierschutz und haben selbst zwei Katzen adoptiert.


PETA: Von Snacks über Pflege bis zu Alltagsprodukten: Wo findet ihr die Überraschungen, die es in euren Kalender schaffen?

  


Adventsome

: Die wichtigste Frage ist immer: Würden wir uns selbst darüber freuen, wenn wir morgens das Türchen öffnen? Das Produkt muss zudem vegan, unisex und alkoholfrei sein und auch darüber hinaus mit unseren Werten matchen!

title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Sharepic downloaden

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

 erschien zuerst auf

author: hsa_oryx
title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.

South Suffolk Hunt Sabs.

SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!

Hunt Saboteurs Association

author: Jana Hoger
title: Update: Polizeihund bei Demo misshandelt – Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Ermittlungen ein
content:
Symbolbild


Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu

gewaltsamen Einsätzen

 der sogenannten Polizeihunde. Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.


Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.


Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.


Originaltext vom 13. Januar 2025


Gewalt gegen Polizeihunde bei einem Einsatz gegen Demonstranten in Riesa


Videos von der Demonstration zeigen deutlich wie gewaltvoll einige Diensthundeführer:innen mit den „Polizeihunden“ umgehen. Einer der

Hunde

 wurde von einem der Beamten am Hals gepackt und gegen eine Leitplanke und einen Demonstranten gedrückt. Dadurch sollte der Hund offensichtlich dazu gebracht werden, den Demonstranten zu beißen. Der Hund zeigte hierbei unübersehbare

Anzeichen

 von massivem Stress, Überforderung und Meideverhalten. Ein weiterer völlig überdrehter Hund verbiss sich in den Arm eines anderen Polizisten.


https://www.instagram.com/p/DExO_Z1Mcvv/?hl=de


PETA erstattet Strafanzeige und fordert den Einsatz von Polizeihunden zu beenden


Dieser gewaltsame Umgang der Einsatzkräfte mit den Hunden ist tierschutzwidrig. Hunde sind nicht dazu da, für die Arbeit der Polizei ausgenutzt zu werden. Wir fordern deshalb, den Einsatz von Hunden bei der Polizei endlich einzustellen. Zudem erstatten wir bei der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden Zweigstelle Meißen Strafanzeige gegen den verantwortlichen Polizisten. Ferat Kocak, Abgeordneter der Linken war als parlamentarischer Beobachter vor Ort und hat sich bereit erklärt in der Strafanzeige als Zeuge aufzutreten.


„Die aktuellen Aufnahmen aus Riesa zeigen eindeutig, dass Hunde bei Polizeieinsätzen nichts zu suchen haben. author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

author: Amy Goodman
title: Fossil Fuel Companies Are Undermining Democracy, Climate Activist Says
content:
A bloc of countries are working on a parallel process to COP to create a binding agreement on fossil fuel phaseout.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

What will it take to bring an end to the fossil fuel era? We speak to Kumi Naidoo, the president of the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, which aims to reach a binding agreement for a global transition away from fossil fuels. Currently backed by over 25 countries from the Global South, the intergovernmental process began earlier this year in Santa Marta, Colombia. Meanwhile, at the United Nations, “for 30 years of negotiations, we don’t have any mention of fossil fuels [in the outcome document]. That’s like Alcoholics Anonymous holding 30 years of conferences and not mentioning alcohol,” says Naidoo. We discuss the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative’s goals, how the oil and gas industry drives global conflict, and the Trump administration’s glaring absence from international action on climate change.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: We’re broadcasting from Antalya, Turkey, at the global U.N. climate summit, known as COP31. There are just four days remaining for nearly 200 countries to come to some agreement on the next steps to tackle climate change.

On Monday, negotiators published a wide-ranging 18-page draft document that’s been characterized as a shopping list of language and issues to be debated ahead of a Friday deadline for a final agreement. This is the global policy lead for Oil Change International.

ROMAIN IOUALALEN: So, I think this is a text that was designed to basically please everyone, and they took, you know, the best, the most ambitious demands from each group and put it in there. Obviously, throughout this week, what we’re going to see is a game of massacre in the negotiations. We’re going to see a lot of these — a lot of these recommendations or this language going to be cut by parties that don’t agree with any of this. And so, as the president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, just said, the text that we’re going to end up with is going to look very different.

AMY GOODMAN: Agreements here at COP are made by consensus, meaning every country essentially has veto power over the final text. Rich countries and fossil fuel-producing countries have historically thwarted the most ambitious climate goals.

These negotiations, of course, are happening as the Iran war has also drawn global attention to the world’s dependence on fossil fuels. So, what will it take to bring an end to the fossil fuel era? A bloc of nearly 30 countries from the Global South have started a parallel process that’s aiming for a binding agreement to transition away from fossil fuels — a fossil fuel treaty. The first official conference on transitioning away from fossil fuels was held in Santa Marta, Colombia, earlier this year. Nearly 60 countries attended. A follow-up conference is scheduled to take place next year in Tuvalu.

To talk more about what can be achieved at this U.N. climate summit and what makes the process that began in Santa Marta different, we’re joined here in Turkey by Kumi Naidoo, longtime climate justice activist from South Africa, president of the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative.

It’s nice to have you back, to see you again, Kumi. Let’s talk about what’s happened so far at this climate summit. In a moment, we’re going to be talking to the former ambassador from Nepal. They just suffered a calamitous glacier melting that led to at least 7,000 people dead and missing. That’s just one example of thousands. What has to happen here? And what is happening?

KUMI NAIDOO: We need to get serious about addressing the root cause of climate change. Eighty-six percent of what’s driving the crisis is our addiction and dependency on oil, coal and gas, what we call fossil fuels. The difficulty we have is that for 30 years of negotiations, we don’t have any mention of fossil fuels. That’s like Alcoholics Anonymous holding 30 years of conferences and not mentioning alcohol in the outcome document.

Now, there are important things that we are pushing here on to get clarity on what a just transition would look like, trying to get resources to go in the Loss and Damage Fund and so on. But what is patently clear right now is we need a parallel process, one that will lead us to a binding agreement. So, what we’ve achieved in April through …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Trapped in a massive delusion
content:
Notes from the US: The Midterms were an adjustment—voters don’t reject the system, only the system’s products that affect their wallets

The much-anticipated midterm elections produced a significant swing to the Democrats; they now control both houses of Congress – although of course the MAGA/Trump cult is contesting this.

Elation would be inappropriate, though. One of the biggest ‘complaints‘ that voters apparently had about the Republicans was the war against Iran. But because it has raised the price of groceries and petrol and has no aims; not because of the loss of life throughout the Middle East.

Neither during the campaign nor in later public and media analysis was arguably the most important issue facing us discussed: the environment. No candidate stood to make changes. Nor have plans announced by the incoming Democratic party mentioned the environment.

What’s more, although more potentially ‘radical’ congresspersons were elected than ever before, discussion has almost exclusively been about the mechanics of electioneering, party politics, personalities, who will or won’t work with whom ‘across the aisle’. Leaders blethered with furrowed brow and a smile about how it was necessary to look forward not back and not be distracted by the corruption, cruelty, crimes and catastrophes of the Trump/MAGA cult. It’s likely to be probably toothless ‘investigations’, not action.

To be fair, so much damage has been done by Trump so far – DOGE; tariffs; wealth redistribution upward; weaponisation of the law and legal system; health; neutering the media; even the demolition of parts of Washington DC, including the White House, not to mention the environment – that even to go back to the status quo ante would need a massive amount of time, money and energy.

What’s more Trump has already threatened to veto anything he doesn’t like (so really all the aforementioned reversals) and can have his vetoes prevail (the Senate requires 66% votes to overrule presidential vetoes); and his administration has already begun illegally destroying documentation necessary to be preserved as evidence.

Any attempts to oppose Trump in his final two years by ‘investigating’ his crimes in the previous two are also almost certain to be met by simple refusal to comply: they’ll ignore subpoenas; refuse to appear before committees; brush aside court orders etc. If all else fails, they may even get violent. Impeachment seems unlikely.

Credible commentary on the atmosphere and environment in the White House and ‘inner’ government circles reports chaos, in-fighting, backbiting and widespread incompetence as Trump tries to advance an ever more hubristic and absurd agenda. The appointments this week of the combative Jim Jordan as House minority leader, and last week of the ghoulish thug, Stephen Miller, as chief of staff replacing Susie Wiles (who was a touch more professional and efficient) indicate their determination to change nothing. The tone of the fascist propaganda outlets is relentlessly negative, delusional, insulting, inaccurate and alarmist… “The commies have taken over”… and they are going to eat your babies.

None of this is surprising, though. Let’s take a step back and ponder what really motivates these public figures.

When Trump last month suggested naming yet more natural and geographical features after himself (as he has done, particularly across the US capital, Washington DC), he revealed much about the nature of right-wing toxicity.

At a rally in the middle of October he announced that he was considering unilaterally ‘renaming’ the world’s largest ocean after himself. Yes it was perhaps trolling. But he did follow through with Lake Ontario in August. (It’s only a short step from that kind of thing to the way Trump ‘renames’ his opponents in order to try and denigrate them… “I’m the president. I can call him whatever the hell I want”.)

In addition to the off-putting solipsistic, dictatorial and crass nature of these moves they highlight the essence of rightwing, fascist, MAGA, Republican beliefs: me first! Me me me. No-one else matters. It’s almost inconceivable to cult members that anyone else uses, sails across, enjoys the majesty of, has shores on, marvels at or indeed even has a say over under international treaties about the sea.

One might readily assign one of the ‘early’ developmental ages elaborated by Swiss biologist and psychologist Jean Piaget, and with which parents and primary school teachers are familiar to Trump …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Two Conferences, Two Distant Venues, One Unilateralist US Policy
content:
Nearly nine years ago, in November 2017, I faced criminal charges for joining a protest against the visit of then US President Donald Trump to the Philippines. He was in Manila for the 31st ASEAN Summit hosted by then President Rodrigo Duterte. What should have been an exercise of our constitutional right to protest ended in a violent police dispersal.


Water cannons, truncheons and even a sonic weapon were used against protesters trying to march toward the summit venues. I was among the progressive lawmakers and protest leaders charged with violating the Public Assembly Act, direct assault and disobedience to persons in authority. The police accused us of inciting protesters to breach barricades.


I considered the charges politically motivated, particularly since I was a sitting member of Congress exercising my right to dissent against a visiting foreign leader. The assault and disobedience charges were eventually dropped for lack of evidence that we had personally attacked police officers.


That experience exposed a familiar contradiction: government readily invokes democracy and national sovereignty in dealing with foreign powers but becomes intolerant when Filipinos exercise those same rights to question our relationship with a powerful ally.


Trump is back in Manila, nearly nine years later. His return brings into focus issues far bigger than the visit itself: military access, economic dependence, geopolitical rivalry, climate responsibility and Philippine sovereignty.


Two international conferences in distant venues provide a useful lens through which to examine these issues: COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, and the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila.


Their agendas differ, but both reveal the unilateralist character of Trump’s foreign policy — one that puts American strategic and economic interests ahead of multilateral commitments and the concerns of less powerful nations.


America’s retreat from climate responsibility


While Trump is welcomed in Manila, the United States is drawing criticism in Türkiye for its absence from international climate negotiations. For the second consecutive year, his administration has declined to send an official government delegation to the UN climate conference.


Trump has dismissed climate change as a hoax while his government retreats from international commitments and rolls back domestic environmental protections.


This is no minor diplomatic snub. The United States is among the world’s largest historical contributors to greenhouse gas emissions and possesses enormous economic and technological resources.


Its withdrawal weakens efforts to secure climate finance, adaptation support and compensation for loss and damage — commitments particularly vital to developing countries that have contributed little to the crisis but suffer its worst consequences.


Washington’s retreat also creates space for China and other powers to present themselves as defenders of multilateral cooperation. But for countries like the Philippines, the issue is not which superpower fills the diplomatic vacuum. It is whether the international community will deliver the resources and concrete commitments needed to confront a crisis already devastating vulnerable communities.


Trump’s return: Military dependence and strategic alignment


The concerns raised in Türkiye are not disconnected from what is happening in Manila. Opposition to Trump’s visit has brought together progressive lawmakers, church groups, people’s organizations, farmers, workers, Indigenous communities, professionals and student activists.


Their protest is directed not simply at Trump but at the policies and agreements associated with his administration and the Marcos government’s unquestioning alignment with Washington.


The Makabayan bloc has filed House Resolution No. 1593 opposing the administration’s reception of Trump. At the heart of the protest is the concern that the Philippines continues to grant Washington military and diplomatic concessions without adequately examining what the country gives up in return.


The expansion of American military access under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), additional military sites and increasingly frequent joint exercises risk drawing the Philippines deeper into the strategic confrontation between Washington and Beijing.

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Minneapolis Activists Demand Resignations and Investigations Over Further Surveillance Revelations
content:
Minneapolis, MN – Activists and community members gathered the morning of Nov. 11 just steps from the Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC) in downtown Minneapolis to demand third-party investigations into Hennepin County and the resignation of two high-ranking employees who have been involved with and directed the

surveillance of activists

 calling for the plant’s closure.


Coinciding with the announcement, the Minnesota Environmental Justice Table published an open letter – “initiated by frontline community leaders impacted directly by the HERC trash burner” – for community members to

sign a petition

 pressing the county to meet them.


The two county employees named are Department of Environment and Energy Assistant Director David McNary and the department’s strategic initiative manager Angie Timmons.


“I find it deeply concerning that county resources have been used to monitor environmental justice organizers,” Jordan Area Community Council Executive Director Audua Pugh said during the announcement. “We are calling for the termination of two county employees and an independent third party investigation into these activities. David McNary and Angie Timmons both bear responsibility for allowing such conduct to take place.”


Watch the press conference below.


In a

report

 released by the Zero Burn Coalition in October, public data obtained through information requests revealed that McNary had been sharing private communications between environmental justice advocates with industry representatives to tank a legislative bill that would have given the city the option to shut down HERC.


Hennepin County Surveilled Anti-HERC Activists Since 2023


McNary’s surveillance of activists began in February 2023 with the kickoff of MNEJT’s campaign to close the trash burner. After the event, Hennepin County Environmental Engagement Coordinator Joe Vital, who attended the event, included McNary in an email with notes that included the campaign’s goals.


In a recently uncovered email from March 2023, Department of Environment and Energy Operations and Compliance Manager Randy Kiser referred to Vital as “our spy on the opposition.”


Vital, who was a community activist prior to landing his role with the county, would continue to monitor the campaign and share notes with McNary and other county employees.


According to the October report, Vital also attempted to learn the identity of a Hennepin County whistleblower through MNEJT co-founder Nazir Khan.


Timmons, whose resignation is also demanded by community members and activists, regularly shared information obtained by Vital and through other channels with McNary and Department of Energy and Environment Director Rosemary Lavin.


According to MNEJT Campaign Manager Isuru Herath, part of the county’s surveillance included photographing organizers and community members at events.


“As your constituent, I am very concerned,” Hennepin County resident and organizer Susan Delattre said during the announcement. “It’s already troubling to know that burning my trash harms other people. But now I learned that my own county government has been monitoring my friends and neighbors, including Black and brown community members, who are simply fighting for the right to breathe clean air.”


Also at the announcement was

Alec “Mac” Stewart

, one of

15 Minnesota organizers indicted

 by the U.S. Department of Justice on charges of conspiring to “impede or injure” federal immigration enforcement officers earlier this year during

Operation Metro Surge

.


Stewart drew direct parallels between the surveillance of anti-HERC activists and the indictments against the Minnesota 15 as well as the long history of the U.S. government targeting and disrupting community organizers.


“Instead of defending their constituents, they seek to surveil, disrupt, and dismantle a community-led effort to protect themselves,” Stewart said. “I say that we learned a thing or two about taking back our agency in Metro Surge.”


HERC was included as one of the 20 worst offending trash burning plants in a report published Oct. 13 by the international environmental advocacy group Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives (GAIA).


According to the report, the facility produces roughly 350,000 million tons of carbon dioxide and 72,000 million tons of incinerator ashes annually. The effect of that pollution on the community is roughly $16 million in health damages and one to two deaths annually.

content:
Fred Pedersen is minister of environment, energy, and minister responsible for Qulliq Energy Corp. following his selection to cabinet on Nov. 5.

The Cambridge Bay MLA was

chosen

stepped down

Koonoo held four portfolios. He was minister of environment, energy, languages, and culture and heritage.


Human Resources Minister Annie Tattuinee now has the languages and culture and heritage portfolios.
