Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

[1] Essen, bei dem jede Person etwas mitbringt

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. Dan materi-materi tersebut bisa berupa teks, foto, audio, video, dan lain sebagainya. Semua koleksi arsip digital AAA …

author: Indo
title: On “Sultat al-Majalis”
content:
Rather interesting text on the Arab Council Communist group “Sultat al-Majalis” formed by Lafif Lakhdar and Mustapha Khayati. Originally published in "Al-Hewar Al-Mutamadin, Issue 8699, 6th May 2026”. Can be found here.

The Arab Communist Grouping, which published the magazine Sultat al-Majalis (The Power of Workers’ Councils), was a revolutionary organization that adopted the ideas of council communism, drawing inspiration from the experiences of workers’ councils in Europe. The group was active in the early 1970s and consisted of intellectuals and workers of Maghrebi (North African) origin living in France. Its members were influenced by the events of May 1968 in France and by the left-wing critique of the existing socialist regimes of the time.

The group focused on the idea that revolution should be led by workers’ councils elected directly by the workers themselves. It rejected the traditional Leninist party model and centralized bureaucratic authority. It regarded Soviet communism, as well as its Chinese Maoist counterpart, as systems that had nothing to do with socialism. In its view, both were forms of state capitalism, owned and controlled by a new class known as the bureaucracy, which, like the bourgeoisie, was hostile to the working class and its independent movement.

The organization also launched a scathing critique of existing Arab regimes, whether self-proclaimed progressive or conservative, as well as all Palestinian organizations and the very idea of a Palestinian revolution, insofar as it remained detached from an all-encompassing Arab revolution aimed at overthrowing the existing state structures across the various Arab countries.

The first and only issue of Sultat al-Majalis was published in January 1974. Its purpose was to promote awareness of the self-organization of workers and peasants, free from the tutelage of political parties. The magazine included translations of texts by leading international theorists of council communism, articles analyzing the Arab-Israeli conflict from a class-based perspective that rejected nationalism, and studies of Arab labor movements.

Despite its limited organizational base, the group had a notable intellectual influence in independent left-wing circles and helped introduce concepts of workers’ self-management. It remains one of the distinctive experiments in the history of the Arab Left, representing an attempt to offer a third alternative outside the frameworks of Arab nationalism and official communism aligned with Moscow.

The group operated clandestinely, which meant that some of its contributors wrote under pseudonyms while others remained behind the scenes. Its initial core included young university graduates from Beirut who had been influenced by the global New Left movement but chose to work under the umbrella of the group in order to distinguish themselves from the official communist parties and the Organization of Communist Action in Lebanon.

The relationship between Lafif Lakhdar (1934–2013) and Mustapha Khayati was central to the establishment of this tendency. In his writings, Lafif Lakhdar confirmed that he and Mustapha Khayati had overseen the publication of Sultat al-Majalis.

Mustapha Khayati was a Tunisian activist and intellectual, a prominent member of the Situationist International in France, and the author of the famous pamphlet On the Poverty of Student Life. Khayati brought Situationist thought and the critique of the “Society of the Spectacle” into the Arab context, an influence that was reflected in the pages of Sultat al-Majalis.

Lafif Lakhdar was a radical left-wing Tunisian intellectual and one of the most outspoken critics of state capitalism in the Soviet Union and the Arab regimes. He argued that the genuine alternative lay in the “power of workers’ councils,” exercising self-management. This position formed the central ideological identity of the group.

The magazine served as a platform through which Khayati and Lakhdar translated unorthodox Marxist texts and analyzed Arab conflicts from an internationalist perspective.

En svensk förf. Fredrik Lindholm, har någon gång år 1909 "gjort" en skrift om anarkismen, vari han åtagit sig att framställa anarkismens uppgifter. Skriftens huvudsakliga innehåll har blivit ett upprepande av de kungamord och tsarmord, som anarkisterna anklagats för, och i vissa fall väl även utfört.

Den omfattar en period då despotismen, liksom nu i många länder, intog högsätet, då folket var helt rättslöst, då anarkisterna och andra motståndare till stats- och utsugningsmonopolen, behandlades som förbrytare och fördrevs ur landet. Ofta fanns det blott en utväg att väcka uppmärksamhet för dessa ohyggliga förhållanden: Bombens detonation.

Bomben var avsedd eller träffade en herre som i sitt dagliga liv, kanske tanklöst, undertecknat hundratals dödsdomar och förvisningar, som framställde sig vara i kompani med gud, innehade kontroll över alla kanaler till det existerande rättsväsendet, befallde över polis och militär, följaktligen utövade ensam härskarmakt eller representerande sådan makt.

Jag anser mig inte i detta sammanhang ha någon befogenhet att diskutera huruvida det var rätt eller inte. Det skulle bli en alltför vidlyftig avhandling, att framställa vad man talar för och emot i ett sammanhang som detta. Våldet har alltid karaktäriserats som ultima ratio, en sista utväg.

I anarkismens politiska och sociala tankevärld har våldet ingen plats. Såväl de politiska som sociala uttrycksformerna skapar en miljö och atmosfär, som avlägsnar ifrån våldet och främjar inbördes hjälp. Dessa förändringar bygger anarkisterna inte på en sinnets förändring som grundlag, men på fakta som att möjligheterna för det sociala välståndets fördelning uppnåtts och herraväldets och förtryckets förverkligande avlägsnats.

Den fulländning som anarkismens samhällsideal företräder bygger på orsakernas upphävande, orsakerna till våldsmentaliteten.

De invändningar som göras, bygga på helt andra förutsättningar. Den ägande som fruktar för att tjuvar och rånare skola tillägna sig hans egendom, vinkar indignerat bort pratet om att våldet skulle bli överflödigt, noggrant förbiseende att människorna under kommunistiskt-anarkistiska samhällsformer inte ha någon anledning att stjäla eller med våld försvara sig mot stöld.

Militären, som tränat in sin yrkesmentalitet och den fanatiske chauvinisten komma med sina argument! Skola vi inte försvara oss mot utländska fiender?

Här är en fråga som redan nuet borde taga klar ställning till. Finns det någon mening i att försvara sig mot utländska fiender? Vad är det man kan och vill försvara? Marken, naturen, sjöarna, kan inte försvaras, kan inte erövras. Under ett krig kan man däremot förstöra dem. Ja, måste förstöra. Fransmän och belgare förstörde stora delar av sina egna områden, direkt, när tyskarna trängde fram under världskriget, förstörde för att inte tyskarna skulle få nytta av det. Franska och belgiska sprängämnen och volymkulor träffade fransk och belgisk natur - och förstörde kanske lika mycket som "fienden", tyskarna, förstörde.

Krigets mekanisering är ett kapitel som vilar tungt på vågen när det gäller att mäta våldets uppgift i nuet. Förr, när en hord människor dreva mot varandra med pikar och muskedunder, var det hela ett farligt äventyr, som begränsades av vapnens räckvidd. Nu finnes det inte längre någon sådan begränsning. Brand-, gift- och spränggaser ha förverkat varje tanke på "försvar" och mobiliserat angreppstanken som enda möjlighet i en våldskonflikt mellan staterna. De långskjutande kanonerna understryka denna utveckling. Ett krig blir blott ett fruktansvärt förgörande av allt levande.

Enda synpunkten som talar för att med krigets våld lösa de mellanfolkliga konflikterna, är den, att vapenfabrikerna och sprängämnestillverkarna behöva experimentera och måste ha stora dividender.

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection:

https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection:

https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

OLIVIER BESANCENOT ET MICHAËL LÖWY ont publié un ouvrage intitulé Affinités révolutionnaires, Nos étoiles rouges et noires, qui entend mettre en relief les « alliances et solidarités agissantes entre les deux mouvements ». Les deux auteurs veulent, disent-ils, « éclairer ce versant ignoré, souvent délibérément, qui révèle la fraternité de leurs combats ». Cela me paraît une excellente idée[1].

Le présent ouvrage n’est cependant pas à strictement parler une réponse à Affinités révolutionnaires : en effet, le mode d’exposition de leurs idées choisi par Besancenot & Löwy, au moins dans la partie historique, ne permet pas de répondre, parce que leur argumentation est trop allusive et vague, fondée sur un exposé extrêmement approximatif des faits. C’est pourquoi, plutôt que de répondre, j’ai simplement choisi d’aborder les mêmes faits, les mêmes questions, mais à notre manière : le lecteur se fera lui-même une idée.

Это письмо я пишу сегодня, тринадцатого июня тысяча девятьсот восьмого года, дорогие братья Пракседис и Энрике, чтобы сообщить вам дело, которое, на мой взгляд, имеет капитальное значение. Идею, которую я сейчас изложу вам, я уже высказал нашему товарищу Либрадо, и он с ней согласен. Перейдём к сути.

Вы знаете так же хорошо, как и я, что ни одна революция не достигает после победы того, чтобы восторжествовали и стали практическими идеалы, которые её воодушевляли, и это происходит потому, что полагаются на то, что новое правительство сделает то, что должен был сделать народ во время революции.

Так всегда и происходило. Повсюду поднимается знамя с более или менее важными реформами; вокруг него группируются скромные люди; идёт борьба; проливается более или менее обильно кровь, и, если революция побеждает, собирается Конгресс, которому поручено облечь в законы идеалы, заставившие народ взяться за оружие и сражаться. В Конгресс идут люди всевозможных идеалов: одни передовые, другие отсталые, третьи умеренные, и в борьбе всех этих тенденций чаяния революции увядают, искажаются, и после долгих месяцев, а то и долгих лет, начинают приниматься законы, в которых даже не угадываются идеалы, за которые пролил свою кровь несчастный народ. Но допустим, произошло чудо и были приняты законы, в которых во всей своей чистоте сияют идеалы революции, – вещь, которой, конечно, никогда не бывало, потому что очень немногие депутаты имеют те же идеалы, что и народ, взявшийся за оружие; допустим, чудо совершилось и что в особом случае нашей борьбы Конгресс предпишет раздел земель, восьмичасовой рабочий день и зарплату не ниже одного песо. Можем ли мы ожидать, что землевладельцы сложат руки и позволят ускользнуть тому, что делает их могущественными и позволяет им жить в праздности? Разве владельцы всевозможных предприятий, где используются наёмные руки, не закроют свои предприятия или, по крайней мере, не сократят число нанимаемых рабочих, чтобы заставить правительство отменить закон под угрозой всеобщего голода, делая вид, что им материально невозможно платить больше за меньшее количество часов работы?

Когда ресурсы для революции иссякнут, народ окажется в положении более тяжёлом, чем то, из-за которого он был вынужден восстать. Народ, без хлеба, прислушается к речам буржуазии, которая скажет, что его обманули, и возглавит его, чтобы свергнуть новое правительство, – и тем спасутся одни от потери своих земель, а другие – от уступок рабочим.

Богатые восстанут, когда речь пойдёт о том, чтобы осуществить на практике программу либеральной партии, – в случае если чудом, истинным и единственным в истории революций народов, идеалы революции после её победы сохранились бы нетронутыми.

Как анархисты мы хорошо всё это знаем. Мы хорошо знаем, чего следует ожидать от наилучшего правительства, какое только может тяготеть над каким-либо народом, и, как анархисты, мы должны сделать всё, что в наших силах, чтобы революция, которая вот-вот разразится, дала народу все блага, какие возможно завоевать.

Чтобы достичь великих благ для народа, благ действительных, нужно действовать как анархисты, которых легко раздавить даже тем, кто считает нас вождями. Всё сводится к простому вопросу тактики. Если бы с самого начала мы называли себя анархистами, никто, кроме немногих, не стал бы нас слушать. Не называя себя анархистами, мы постепенно зажигаем в умах идеи ненависти против имущего класса и против правительственной касты. Ни одна либеральная партия в мире не имеет антикапиталистических стремлений той партии, что вот-вот совершит революцию в Мексике, и этого мы добились, не говоря о том, что мы анархисты, мы не добились бы этого, даже если бы называли себя не анархистами, какими являемся, а просто …

Es ist kaum 65 Jahre her, da war es absolut üblich, in der anarchistischen Literatur Analysen der Institutionen zu lesen, in denen sich die verschiedenen Formen der Herrschaft manifestierten. Wenn man beispielsweise über die Unterdrückung der Frauen schrieb, dann wurden die Familie und die Ehe untersucht und bloßgestellt. Wenn die Unterdrückung von Vergnügen und der Freude des Lebens zur Diskussion stand, dann wurden Religion und Gesetz ins Visier genommen. Der institutionelle Rahmen, in dem sich diese Gesellschaft abspielt wurde als Quelle der Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung wahrgenommen.

Es scheint so, als wäre dieser institutionelle Rahmen in jüngerer Zeit größtenteils vergessen worden zu sein. Von den verschiedenen Institutionen, in die unser entfremdetes kreatives Potenzial zu unserem Nachteil akkumuliert wurde, scheinen nur noch der Staat und das Kapital (und gelegentlich die Technologie) in einem bedeutenden Ausmaß Erwähnung zu finden und selbst diese werden häufig mehr als Geisteszustände, denn als konkrete soziale Institutionen behandelt. So entdecken wir beispielsweise, dass Anarchist*innen gegen Staatlichkeit (was auch immer das sein soll) sind, anstatt gegen den Staat. Auf diese Weise kann etwa ein Bookchin behaupten, gegen Staatlichkeit zu sein, während er den altertümlichen griechischen Stadt-Staat als Modell für seine demokratisierte Version der „Anarchie“ bewirbt.

Jede andere Form der Unterdrückung wird ebenfalls zu einem „-ismus“ (Rassismus, Sexismus, usw.) oder schlimmerem (Homophobie impliziert beispielsweise eine psychologische Störung, die einer Behandlung bedarf, anstatt einer sozialen Repression, die nach Revolte verlangt). Natürlich verleugnen wir nicht die Realitäten der Ideologien der Bigotterie und ihrer Durchdringung der Gedanken und Gefühle der Ausgebeuteten und Unterdrückten. Aber ohne ein Verständnis des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung und Herrschaft ist es nicht möglich zu verstehen, wie die herrschende Klasse diese Ideologien dazu nutzt, diejenigen zu spalten, die sie ausbeutet.

Selbst die anscheinend Radikalsten (weil ihre Rhetorik am extremsten ist) innerhalb des anarchistischen Millieus entgehen dem nicht. Die von primitivistischen und antizivilisatorischen Kreisen kommende Kritik richtet ihre verbalen Angriffe allzu häufig gegen eine nebulöse, schlecht definierte Zivilisation. Gewiss klingt „Für die Zerstörung der Zivilisation“ radikal. Meiner eigenen Definition gemäß stimme ich damit sogar überein. Aber meiner Definition nach ist Zivilisation nicht irgendeine nebulöse, weitestgehend mentale Kategorie, die dem Rationalismus oder dem westlichen Denken oder welcher unerwünschten Denkweise auch immer entspringt; sie ist ein Netzwerk konkreter sozialer Institutionen, die ich in meinem Alltag konfrontiere: Staat, Wirtschaft, Religion, die Familie, technologische Systeme, und so weiter, allesamt sehr reale Entitäten, die nicht von Gedankenspielen beseitigt werden werden.

Und genau hier tappt die derzeitige Tendenz in eine Falle. Wenn eine Analyse des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung, Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung vergessen wird, dann tritt Therapie an die Stelle von Revolution. Wir sind dann gezwungen, uns mit den pathetischen, weinerlichen Geständnissen eines Chris Crass zu beschäftigen oder auch der schlechten Popkultur-Psychologie der Autor*innen des Textes „Stick it to the Manarchy“ (wobei schon der Gebrauch eines Begriffs wie „manarchy“ ein sicheres Zeichen dafür ist, dass jemand nichts hörenswertes zu sagen hat), die versuchen ihren „Sexismus“, „Rassismus“, „Homophobie“ und „Klassismus“ abzulegen, die nicht länger irgendwelche Ideologien der Bigotterie sind, sondern niedere mentale Krankheiten, unter denen die selbsternannten „Privilegierten“ aller Klassen leiden.

Jede*r ernsthafte revolutionäre Anarchist*in muss sehen, dass das nur eine weitere List der Feiglinge und jener ist, die ein Interesse an der Aufrechterhaltung der herrschenden Ordnung haben, die eigentliche Entscheidung darüber, auf wessen Seite sie im Kampf gegen diese Gesellschaft stehen, aufzuschieben. Diejenigen von uns, die es mit der Zerstörung der gegenwärtigen Welt ernst meinen, um unsere Leben selbst zu gestalten, haben keine Zeit für diese selbstgerechten Gedankenspielereien, die so sehr an Selbsthilfegruppen erinnern („Mein Name ist … …

author: Unknown
title: IRGC bans civilian access to Shaho Mountains
content:
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has banned civilian access to the Shaho Mountains in Ravansar County until 21 November, citing military exercises.


Residents of several nearby villages told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) that the IRGC announced the ban through village councils and village heads on 15 November.


Residents were told that the IRGC’s Ansar Rasoul Commando Unit in Javanrud would conduct military exercises in the mountains until 21 November and that all civilian access to the area was prohibited.


The sources said a military convoy carrying heavy and medium-heavy equipment had been dispatched from the unit’s barracks and deployed around the mountains as the exercises were announced.


The IRGC previously banned civilian access to the area from 2 to 7 October during military exercises and artillery shelling of the Shaho Mountains.


The exercises and shelling take place in an area designated for environmental protection. The Shaho and Kusalan Mountains were granted protected status in 2009 under Resolution No. 303 of the Supreme Council for Environmental Protection and are managed by the Department of Environment.


Environmental activists say the IRGC has built several military bases in the area since 2007, under the pretext of countering the presence of forces affiliated with Kurdish opposition parties.


Military exercises and other military activities have caused fires in parts of the area’s pastures and forests, while the construction of military bases and roads has destroyed further sections despite protests, the activists say.


They add that IRGC forces deliberately set fire to vegetation and pastures around some military bases, with the stated aim of preventing Kurdish opposition forces from using the vegetation as cover to carry out attacks.

author: Unknown
title: Fon soruşturmasında ifade veren AKP'li Tayyar: Tera suç örgütünün kumpasıyla karşı karşıyayım
content:
Eski AKP Milletvekili Şamil Tayyar fon vurgunu soruşturması kapsamında "şüpheli" sıfatıyla İstanbul Adliyesi'nde ifade verdi. Tayyar "Alçakça iftira atan Tera suç örgütü yöneticilerinin, fon vurgunuyla mücadelemi akamete uğratmak ve sesimi kısmak için kurguladıkları kumpasın tüm detaylarını yarın yazacağım" dedi.

İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının yürüttüğü soruşturma kapsamında Çağlayan'daki İstanbul Adliyesi'nde yaklaşık 1.5 saat ifade veren Tayyar, adliye önünde basın mensuplarına açıklama yaparak "Tera suç örgütünün bir kumpasıyla karşı karşıya kaldığımı öğrendim. Onların akıl almaz bazı iddiaları vardı. Savcı Bey de o soruları yöneltti, cevabımızı verdik" dedi.

Tayyar, "Hayatımda görmediğim, tanımadığım, bilmediğim, canlı olarak bile görmediğim, telefonla dahi konuşmadığım insanların benimle ilgili akla hayale gelmeyen çirkin iddiaları. Anlaşılan o ki benim bu fon vurguncularıyla mücadele azmimi kırmak, sesimi kısmak ve bu mücadele sürecini akamete uğratmak için bir kumpas hazırladıklarını görüyorum. Ağır bir iftira ile karşı karşıyayım" ifadelerini kullandı.

Tayyar daha sonra sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda şunları söyledi: "Çağlayan Adliyesi’nden az önce ayrıldım. Tera suç örgütünün kumpasına ilişkin ifademi verdim. Ankara yolundayım. Hayatımda görmediğim, tanımadığım, telefonla dahi görüşmediğim, adlarını operasyonla birlikte ilk kez duyduğum, hiçbir dönemde övücü paylaşımım olmadığı halde alçakça iftira atan Tera suç örgütü yöneticilerinin, fon vurgunuyla mücadelemi akamete uğratmak ve sesimi kısmak için kurguladıkları kumpasın tüm detaylarını yarın yazacağım. Fon mücadelesine omuz veren herkesten istirhamım, asla geri adım atmayın. Bu şeref yoksunları gün yüzü görmesinler. Uzantıları da hesap vermekten kurtulamasınlar."

author: Unknown
title: Oil exports begin through Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
content:
Iraq’s Ministry of Oil issued a statement announcing the resumption of oil exports through the Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline.


The statement confirmed that crude oil would be exported through the old pipeline between Iraq and Turkey, with an initial export volume of 120,000 barrels per day.


Export capacity is expected to increase gradually in the coming period, with plans to reach 500,000 barrels per day.


The ministry described the reactivation of the pipeline and the resumption of exports as a “strategic step,” stating that it would strengthen Iraq’s oil export capacity and help diversify the country’s oil export routes.


The statement emphasized that reopening this export route would provide an important source of additional revenue and support the Iraqi economy.

author: Unknown
title: Kazayla ölmüyoruz; kazara yaşıyoruz
content:
Fotoğraf: schlosser-joerg/Pixabay

Askeri sanayiden bir grup işçi Ankara

Geçtiğimiz hafta HABAŞ’ta meydana gelen patlamanın bir kaza olmadığını hatta ‘işçi cinayeti’ demenin bile yeterli olmadığını biliyoruz. Yaşanan tam anlamıyla işçi katliamıydı. Bizler de işçiyiz ve her gün hatırlatılıyor canımızın bir değerinin olmadığı. Ama HABAŞ’taki olay gösterdi ki bizlerin “ölümüne çalıştırılması” devlet-sarı sendika-patron iş birliği ile tasarlanan yani kasıtlı bir şey.

Kendi fabrikamızdan sadece bir haftayı bile ele aldığımızda bu patlamaların ya da kazaların nasıl meydana geldiğini görüyoruz. Bizim fabrikamızda denetim oldu hafta başında. Ama öncesinden denetim olacağı bilgisi vardı ve koruyucu ekipmanlardan tutun da riskli makinelerin bakıma alınmasına kadar göstermelik işler yapıldı. Çalıştığımız yerin askeri sanayiye üretim yaptığını belirtmemiz gerek. Çünkü bu sektörde hem patlayıcı ve kimyasalla işin riski artıyor hem de ihracat anlamına çok göz önünde. Tüm bunların yanında denetim günü geldiğinde normalde üretimde kullanılan şeyler saha dışına saklanıyor, fabrikanın dışına çıkarılıyor. Tüm bunlar işçilerin gözünün önünde olurken, bizden üç maymunu oynamamız isteniyor. Bir arkadaşımız gülerek de olsa “Yasa dışı bir şey mi yapıyoruz biz” diye soruyor ama cevapsız kalıyor. Akabinde tatbikat, İSG eğitimi vesaire tiyatro devam ediyor. Ama şu çok net ki izinsiz bir şeyler yapılıyor. İşe yeni giren bir arkadaşımız, “Haberli denetim yapmak devletin suçu. Haliyle geldiğinde bir şey bulamaz. Habersiz gelmeleri gerekiyor” dedi. Bir başka arkadaş da “Gizli bir şeyler olduğu kesin. Çok rahatsızım. Ama girerken belge imzaladık sonuçta konuşursak başımız yanar” diye ekliyor.

Patlamanın ardından herkes üzgündü de ama öfke çok sınırlıydı. Sanki fail/failller apaçık değilmiş gibi yönsüz bir duyguydu. O fabrikada üç haftada üçüncü ölümlü olay olduğunu öğrendiğimizde ise bu ülkede patronların yargılanmayacağını bilmenin bir çaresizliği vardı. Bir arkadaşımız şöyle özetledi: “Patron bildiğin katilmiş demek ki. Ama fon olayında da gördük; hırsızı, katili patron mu değil mi diye ayırıyorlar. Onlar nasıl yırttıysa bu adam da yırtar.”

HABAŞ’taki işçiler ile bizim aramızda çok ince bir ayrım var aslında. Orada yaşandı biz de kıyısında geziyoruz. Hatta bazen bazı işleri korkarak yapıyoruz ama yine de yapıyoruz. Bir arkadaşımız oradaki işçilerin de farkında oldukları şeylere tıpkı bizim gibi müdahale edemediklerini düşünüyor: “Eminim ki o vince dair ya da kazana dair artık bilemiyorum oradaki işçiler de tedirgin olmuşlardır. Bakımını ya da riskini söylemişlerdir. Biz de burada dile getiriyoruz ama üretim devam ettiği sürece patronlar için sorun olarak görülmüyor. En basitinden iş ayakkabısı verilsin diyoruz onu bile yapmadılar. Kimyasal ile ilgili önlem almak ya da bilgilendirme yapmak söz konusu bile değil.”

Tüm bunları konuşurken fark ediyoruz ki biz işçiler kazara ölmüyoruz; kazara yaşıyoruz. Yaşarken de insani duygulardan uzaklaşıyoruz. Yani insanlıktan çıkarak yaşıyoruz. Biz burada haberleri okurken, videoları izlerken dayanamadık ama gördük ki ertesi gün işe çağrılmış işçiler. Bu mecburiyeti de en iyi biz işçiler anlıyoruz yine. Bir grup işçi oturup bu mektubu yazarken istiyoruz ki sorumlular yargılansın. Mecliste araştırma önergesi AKP-MHP oyları ile reddedildi ama eğer ısrarcı olursak üstünü örtemezler. Gözaltına alınan patron, biz baskı oluşturursak arka kapıdan salıverilmez. Bizi öldüren bu çürümüş ‘denetimsiz’ düzen, işsiz kalma korkusuyla bizi susturuyor; ölme pahasına çalıştırıyor. Eğer biz daha çok konuşursak, tüm patronlar tedirgin olur, işçiler ancak o zaman rahat eder.

author: Katharine Trendacosta
title: The Paramount-Warner Brothers Deal Could Usher in Another Age of Lost Media
content:
There are all sorts of reasons to be against the merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers-Discovery. There's the obvious problem of increasing concentration in the already pretty-concentrated film and TV industry. People have problems with Paramount's owner Skydance interfering with its news coverage and late night comedy. But one of the biggest is the way we are losing choice and access to information and culture.

In the context of the digital world, there are two major problems with these mega mergers. One, as we've said in the past, is that it further degrades the already awful state of mainstream streaming services. In short, by increasing the amount of legacy content under their control, major studios don't have to invest in either new content or well-engineered services to get users. Plus, they can pool the data they have on users together in an increasing assault on consumer privacy. A monthly subscription and more information about your habits and interests? Win-win for them.

Another problem is the disappearing of content. In the digital era, there should be no more lost media. Making and storing copies of media is easier and cheaper than it ever has been. The idea of the persistence of content online has become the adage "the internet never forgets."

However, since more and more media is locked behind subscription services under the control of fewer and fewer companies—and as physical copies, or even just digital copies that are actually owned by consumers also vanish—access to our common culture is at risk. Incentives to take information and media offline should raise huge red flags. Unfortunately, they are multiplying.

First, there's the impulse of merged companies to offset the cost of their merger by shelving projects and claiming them as tax write-offs. We saw this the last time Warner Brothers was taken over, with projects being ended in order to take advantage of a specific kind of tax benefit. It has little to do with the quality or even how much or how complete a project is—money is the driving factor and we as a culture are all poorer for it. And we all know it. That's why the outrage eventually led to Coyote vs Acme being released by a much smaller studio. But not every project can count on having the perfect storm that brings a movie or show back from the dead.

Second, there's the imposition of a new owner's own goals and beliefs upon its new acquisition. Some choices might seem kind of benign, like Discovery axing a lot of family-friendly and kid-oriented content from HBO Max. Of course, when one of the things affected is a pillar of childhood like Sesame Street, the loss of access to old episodes becomes a loss to the culture and not just a change in direction.

Another area where we might lose access to information is in the radical shift in direction for news reporting. Reporters have resigned and more are being offered buy-outs to support the change in direction. Whether this will escalate to older projects being removed from streaming services or quietly buried in the recommendation algorithm is yet to be seen, but remains a real possibility. And it's not lost on anyone that one of the outlets reporting on the chaos at CBS News was CNN, which is now owned by the same people who own CBS News. The loss of diverse sources of news, as imperfect as we may have thought they were, hurts all of us. It makes it harder to access information and diverse points of view.

Finally, media disappears as licenses expire and as studios decide they no longer want to pay residuals or backend deals to the creative people who made the work in the first place. Again, this looks like business decisions but if the works were exclusively available via streaming, those movies disappear forever. That both contributes to the idea that works are disposable and that paying the workers who made the art is not as important as shareholder value.

On top of all of this, draconian copyright regimes and the anti-user product designs they create have made it nearly impossible for people to archive this material on their own—as many used to using VCRs. It’s easy to see a crisis in access to culture and information brewing, at the same time that it should be easier than ever to preserve and make available our shared digital culture.

author: Stelinsky
title: Σχετικά µε το καµπ στο «Κλειδί» της Σιντικής Σερρών
content:
Το καμπ της Σιντικής Σερρών βρίσκεται σε χαράδρα κοντά στα σύνορα με τη Βουλγαρία, απομονωμένο από οικισμούς. Λειτούργησε στις αρχές του 2020 ως κλειστή δομή για περίπου έναν μήνα και στη συνέχεια μετατράπηκε σε «ανοιχτή δομή προσωρινής φιλοξενίας αιτούντων άσυλο», με δυνατότητα κίνησης και εξόδου από αυτό.

Στις 11 Ιουλίου 2025 ψηφίζεται η διάταξη του άρθρου 79 του Ν. 5218/2025, η οποία αναστέλλει για τρεις μήνες, από τις 14 Ιουλίου έως τις 14 Οκτωβρίου 2025, την υποβολή αιτήσεων διεθνούς προστασίας από μετανάστ(ρι)ες που έφταναν στην Ελλάδα με πλωτά από τη Βόρεια Αφρική. Συχνά αναφέρεται ως «το τρίμηνο του Πλεύρη» και προβλέπει και την επιστροφή των μεταναστ(ρι)ών στη χώρα προέλευσής τους χωρίς καμία καταγραφή των αιτήσεών τους. Λίγες μέρες αργότερα κατατίθεται ψήφισμα στο Δημοτικό Συμβούλιο Σιντικής που αποτυπώνει με αφοπλιστική ειλικρίνεια την ρατσιστική στάση του Δήμου:

«Με τον νέο Νόμο όσοι εισέρχονται παράνομα στην χώρα μετά τις 14 Ιουνίου ’25 θα αντιμετωπίζονται ως ΚΡΑΤΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ σε κλειστές δομές κι όχι ως ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ σε ανοικτές δομές όπως γινόταν ως τότε. Με απόφαση του Δημοτικού Συμβουλίου Σιντικής στις 15/7/25 ζητήσαμε το ΚΛΕΙΣΙΜΟ της δομής και μέχρι να συμβεί αυτό αποφασίστηκε η μετατροπή της Δομής από ανοικτή σε κλειστή, ώστε να αυξηθεί το αίσθημα ασφάλειας και η ποιότητα ζωής των πολιτών στον τόπο μας. Οι 800 που διέμεναν μέχρι τώρα στην δομή στο Κλειδί επειδή υπόκεινται στο καθεστώς της φιλοξενίας (μπήκαν στην χώρα πριν τις 14 Ιουνίου και κυκλοφορούσαν ελεύθερα έξω) μεταφέρονται σε άλλες δομές που παραμένουν ανοικτές. Αυτοί οι 800 αντικαθίστανται από αυτούς που μπήκαν παράνομα στην χώρα ΜΕΤΑ τις 14 Ιουνίου 2025 και θα είναι ΚΡΑΤΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ.

ΔΕΝ ΔΗΜΙΟΥΡΓΕΙΤΑΙ ΝΕΑ ΔΟΜΗ ΣΤΗΝ ΣΙΝΤΙΚΗ! ΔΕΝ ΑΛΛΑΖΕΙ Ο ΑΡΙΘΜΟΣ ΤΩΝ ΤΡΟΦΙΜΩΝ ΣΤΗΝ ΔΟΜΗ! ΑΥΤΟΙ ΠΟΥ ΕΡΧΟΝΤΑΙ ΔΕΝ ΔΙΑΦΕΡΟΥΝ ΣΕ ΤΙΠΟΤΑ ΑΠΟ ΑΥΤΟΥΣ ΠΟΥ ΦΕΥΓΟΥΝ (αυτοί που φεύγουν δεν ήταν «οικογενειάρχες» όπως θέλει να τους παρουσιάζει η αντιπολίτευση). Η ΜΟΝΗ ΔΙΑΦΟΡΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΣΤΗΝ ΗΜΕΡΟΜΗΝΙΑ ΠΟΥ ΜΠΗΚΑΝ ΠΑΡΑΝΟΜΑ ΣΤΗ ΧΩΡΑ! ΙΣΧΥΡΗ ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΚΗ ΔΥΝΑΜΗ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΙΦΡΟΥΡΕΙ ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΟΦΙΜΟΥΣ ΤΗΣ ΔΟΜΗΣ ΣΤΟ ΚΛΕΙΔΙ. ΠΛΕΟΝ ΔΕΝ ΘΑ ΚΥΚΛΟΦΟΡΕΙ ΚΑΝΕΙΣ ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΟΣ ΣΤΑ ΧΩΡΙΑ ΤΟΥ ΔΗΜΟΥ ΣΙΝΤΙΚΗΣ! ΚΕΡΔΙΖΟΥΜΕ ΣΕ ΑΣΦΑΛΕΙΑ!»

Οι τραγικές συνθήκες υλικής διαβίωσης στο καμπ είναι αποτέλεσμα σχεδιασμού, όχι αμέλειας: υπερπληθυσμός (περίπου 1.000 άτομα τον Σεπτέμβριο του ’25), κοντέινερ που μπάζουν νερά, ελλείψεις σε κρεβάτια, στρώματα, υγιεινή, σίτιση και ιατροφαρμακευτική κάλυψη. Η διερμηνεία απουσιάζει από την καθημερινότητα των έγκλειστων, καθώς οι μεταφραστές δεν μπορούν να επικοινωνήσουν μαζί τους εκτός επίσημων διαδικασιών, η επικοινωνία με εργαζόμενους και ΜΚΟ απαγορεύεται, και η μόνη σχέση με τον έξω κόσμο περνά από τον έλεγχο της ΕΛ.ΑΣ. Η χρήση βίας από την αστυνομία δεν αποτελεί παρέκκλιση του συστήματος· είναι η σκόπιμη λειτουργία του. Το καθεστώς αυτό οδηγεί σε ψυχική και σωματική εξάντληση, με απόπειρες αυτοκτονίας που δεν καταγράφονται ποτέ. Είναι, συνεπώς, λογικό και επόμενο οι άνθρωποι που παραμένουν έγκλειστοι εκεί μέσα, κάποια στιγμή να αντιδράσουν στην καθημερινή απαξίωση των ζωών τους, όπως και έγινε.

author: Stelinsky
title: Λίγες σκέψεις για την αντιµεταναστευτική πολιτική και τα κέντρα κράτησης (Ένθετο #60)
content:
Μέσα στα χρόνια, με τις αυξημένες ροές προσφύγων και μεταναστών προς στην Ευρώπη, τα ευρωπαϊκά κράτη προχώρησαν σε πολλαπλές μεταρρυθμίσεις αυστηροποίησης του νομικού πλαισίου γύρω από το μεταναστευτικό. Αποσυνδέοντας την μετανάστευση από όλους τους παράγοντες που την προκαλούν (κοινωνικούς, πολιτικούς, οικονομικούς), παρουσιάζεται εκ νέου ως «ζήτημα δημόσιας τάξης». Στο όνομα της «εθνικής ασφάλειας» και της «προστασίας των συνόρων», αντιμετωπίζεται ως ένας κίνδυνος που πρέπει να αναχαιτιστεί, πολιτική που επεκτείνεται και στο εσωτερικό των κρατών: Αστυνομικοί έλεγχοι, ατέλειωτες, δυσλειτουργικές διαδικασίες ασύλου, απελάσεις, καταστολή, παρατεταμένη κράτηση στις δομές «φιλοξενίας», όλα αυτά δημιουργούν μια κανονικότητα που μετατρέπει τη μετανάστευση σε απειλή και τους/τις μετανάστ(ρι)ες σε αντικείμενα διοικητικής διαχείρισης.

Το ελληνικό κράτος τα τελευταία χρόνια ευθυγραμμίζεται με αυτή την κατεύθυνση. Ένα πρόσφατο χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα είναι ο Ν. 5226/2025, γνωστός ως «νόμος Πλεύρη-Βορίδη», που επικυρώνει την απροκάλυπτη ρατσιστική στάση του κράτους: H πρόσβαση στη διεθνή προστασία εξαρτάται πλέον άμεσα από τη δυνατότητα εισόδου στη χώρα μέσω των νόμιμων οδών. Δημιουργείται έτσι ένας φαύλος κύκλος, όπου όσες αναγκάζονται να μετακινηθούν, μη έχοντας τα απαιτούμενα έγγραφα ή/και πρόσβαση σε νόμιμες οδούς εισόδου, βρίσκονται απέναντι σε ένα σύστημα που ήδη αντιμετωπίζει την κατάστασή τους ως παράτυπη. Η «νομιμότητα», δηλαδή, μετατρέπεται σε προϋπόθεση, καθιστώντας την τελικά προνόμιο όσων κατάφεραν να περάσουν από τις «σωστές» πόρτες.

Η μεταναστευτική πολιτική στον ελλαδικό χώρο συγκροτείται πάνω στην λογική της διαχείρισης πληθυσμών μέσω του αποκλεισμού. Αναπόσπαστο κομμάτι αυτής της λογικής είναι και όλων των ειδών οι δομές που λειτουργούν στη χώρα για τους/τις μετανάστ(ρι)ες και αιτούντες άσυλο: από τα Κέντρα Υποδοχής και Ταυτοποίησης (ΚΥΤ), τις ανοιχτές δομές «φιλοξενίας», και τις κλειστές ελεγχόμενες δομές μέχρι και τις ειδικές δομές για ασυνόδευτους ανηλίκους. Στην πραγματικότητα, οι δομές που επίσημα αναφέρονται ως «κέντρα φιλοξενίας/υποδοχής/προσωρινής διαμονής» δεν είναι τίποτα άλλο παρά αποθήκες ανθρώπων όπου ο κρατικός μηχανισμός στοιβάζει, βασανίζει και πειθαρχεί. Ανθρώπους που το ίδιο το καπιταλιστικό σύστημα ξερίζωσε από τους τόπους τους. Όταν η δυνατότητα εξόδου από την δομή και η επικοινωνία με τον έξω κόσμο διαρκώς ελέγχεται και περιορίζεται, όταν η αστυνομική επιτήρηση και καταστολή καθορίζει σε τέτοιο βαθμό την καθημερινότητα, ο τρόπος λειτουργίας τους προσομοιάζει τον τρόπο λειτουργίας μιας φυλακής. Η αθωότητα στην επιλογή των λέξεων, στον τρόπο που παρουσιάζονται επικοινωνιακά, απέχει χιλιόμετρα από την πραγματικότητα, είναι όμως εντελώς σκόπιμη.

Η διαχείριση του μεταναστευτικού δεν είναι απλώς ένα «τεχνικό» ζήτημα, αλλά πολιτική επιλογή που στοχεύει στη δημιουργία ενός μόνιμα επισφαλούς προλεταριάτου, χωρίς δικαιώματα, χωρίς φωνή, χωρίς δυνατότητα οργάνωσης. Το επικοινωνιακό πλαίσιο των προεκλογικών περιόδων λειτουργεί ως ιδεολογικός μηχανισμός που αποσπά συναίνεση μέσω του φόβου και νομιμοποιεί την καταστολή. Παράλληλα, τα εξοπλιστικά προγράμματα και η θωράκιση των συνόρων εντάσσονται στην ίδια λογική: Η μετανάστευση αντιμετωπίζεται ως στρατιωτικό ζήτημα και όχι ως κοινωνικό φαινόμενο, με τον στρατό και την αστυνομία να αναλαμβάνουν τον ρόλο διαχειριστή ανθρώπινων ζωών. Δεν πρόκειται για ανθρωπιστική κρίση που κακοδιαχειρίζεται· πρόκειται για δομική βία που παράγεται συστηματικά από κράτη, θεσμούς και νόμους. Η αντίσταση σε αυτό δεν είναι φιλανθρωπία, αλλά πολιτική πράξη. Η δομή στην Σιντική Σερρών είναι ένα από τα δεκάδες παραδείγματα όπου όλα αυτά αποτυπώνονται πεντακάθαρα.

author: Chris Walker
title: Senators Seek Details of RFK’s Samoa Trip as US Loses Measles Elimination Status
content:
Two Democratic senators want to know if Kennedy lied under oath during his Senate confirmation hearings.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Two Democratic senators have sent a letter to Children’s Health Defense, the anti-vaccine organization formerly led by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., seeking details about Kennedy’s trip to Samoa in 2019.

The letter was sent last week by Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon), the ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee, and Sen. Angela Alsobrooks (D-Maryland), a member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee. In it, the lawmakers said they are planning an investigation into evidence that Kennedy “unlawfully lied to Congress on multiple occasions,” including during his 2025 confirmation hearings.

During those hearings, Kennedy said that his trip to Samoa in 2019 — which was followed by a massive measles outbreak on the island — was unrelated to his pushing an anti-vaccine agenda, the senators wrote.

“I went there, nothing to do with vaccines,” Kennedy said during his confirmation, claiming he was instead visiting to introduce officials to a “state-of-the-art” medical information system.

“It appears this statement was false,” the senators wrote, citing reports that Kennedy had written to Samoa’s Prime Minister Tuila’epa Sa’ilele Malielegaoi in January 2019, proposing that his team “conduct [a] detailed health informatics assessment in Samoa of what happened with your MMR vaccines.”

The senators’ letter also highlighted how Kennedy’s visit to Samoa in May 2019 included meeting “with anti-vaccine activists.”

Following Kennedy’s visit, 83 people on the island died in a devastating measles outbreak, mostly children.

Kennedy’s travel to Samoa occurred while he was still in charge of Children’s Health Defense. The letter from the senators requests “all documents related to any travel to Samoa undertaken by Kennedy or other employees, officers, directors, or associates of Children’s Health Defense,” and “all documents related to meetings or communications between Samoan government officials and employees, officers, directors, or associates” of the organization.

The letter is nonbinding, meaning that Children’s Health Defense could refuse to follow through with the senators’ demands. However, when Congress reconvenes in January 2027, the Democratic senators could urge their committees to issue subpoenas to the organization, requiring them to abide by the requests.

“We intend to hold Secretary Kennedy accountable for the grave harm he has caused to vulnerable children,” the senators added. “We also intend to hold him accountable for any false statements made to Congress, a crime that undermines the Senate’s ability to fulfill its constitutional duties.”

The letter was published just days before it was announced that the U.S. was set to lose its measles elimination status, which the country had attained a quarter of a century ago. That announcement was officially made by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization (WHO)-affiliated regional body that makes such decisions, on Tuesday morning.

Since Donald Trump re-entered the White House, annual measles cases in the U.S. have risen more than 20-fold. Only 285 cases were identified in the country in 2024 — that number increased to 2,289 cases in 2025, and, as of this week, 5,739 cases have been identified in 2026, according to a tracker managed by Johns Hopkins University.

Kennedy has dismissed the alarming increase in infections over the past two years, downplaying the risks associated with measles and promoting false remedies for the illness to parents.

The loss of the U.S.’s measles elimination status “highlight[s] the importance of measles vaccination and rapid detection and reporting of suspected and confirmed measles cases,” the Johns Hopkins University tracker pointed out.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Report: Parents Deported Under Trump Have Been Denied Contact With Their Kids
content:
In some cases, mothers being detained or deported were denied information on the whereabouts of their infant children.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A new report finds that parents deported since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term have been cut off from their children or denied the opportunity to make decisions about their children’s future.

The report, published by legal advocacy group Justice in Motion on Tuesday, shines a light on the Trump administration’s moves to weaken and dismantle policies that previously provided protections for immigrant families — all while rapidly expanding the U.S.’s detention and deportation apparatus.

Justice in Motion, which partners with legal advocates in North and Central America, conducted 122 interviews with parents deported from the U.S. to Honduras, Guatemala, and Mexico since January 2025. They found that parents were repeatedly denied opportunities to contact their children after their arrest, and did not have reliable information about their children’s whereabouts and wellbeing both throughout their detention and after their deportation.

In some cases, mothers were separated from their infant children, and were not told the whereabouts of their babies during their detention or after their deportation.

A Brookings study published in May 2026 estimated that over 205,000 children have experienced the detention or deportation of a parent since the start of Trump’s second term. But little attention has been given to what happens after their deportation.

Dora Isabel Melara, a human rights attorney who spoke with deported parents, said in the Justice in Motion report that “deportation does not simply mean removing a person from one country to another; it means fragmenting a family.”

“When speaking with parents who are returned to Honduras, what I consistently observe is an emotional burden marked by desperation, uncertainty, and anguish,” she said. “Many parents arrive without clear information about their children. In most cases, the separation occurred while the parents were on their way to work or had just dropped their children off at school, without a chance to say goodbye or explain the situation to them.”

“What is not always visible from the United States is the complexity that follows that separation: the barriers to reestablishing communication… and a lack of knowledge about the legal processes necessary for reunification or custody,” she continued. “These realities prolong the separation well beyond the moment of deportation.”

Justice in Motion works to connect parents to attorneys to provide long-term support and assist in their reunification efforts after their deportation.

“Each time a parent loses contact, or a parent is denied the opportunity to make a determination about where their child should be, whether it’s with them or with someone else, it feels like a fundamental violation of the most innate responsibilities that a parent holds towards their child,” Justice in Motion’s Keeli Sorensen told Truthout.

In 2018, Trump’s “Zero Tolerance” family separation policy mandated the criminal prosecution of adults crossing the U.S. border without documentation, separating some 5,000 children from their families. Massive public outcry and nationwide protests pushed Trump to sign an executive order ending family separations in June 2018 — but his zero-tolerance framework remained in place, the report notes.

When President Joe Biden took office in 2021, the administration rescinded the 2018 zero-tolerance policy, the report says, and enacted some safeguards for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to consider children and families’ rights to stay together, under a parental rights directive. This was followed by a 10-year high of deportations under Biden, exceeding peak numbers from Trump’s first presidency.

In his second term, Trump has rescinded the majority of the safeguards for deported parents to exercise their parental rights — while ramping up family separation, detention, and deportations across the country.

“I think what we’re seeing now is grossly alarming to us because it’s just so much more widespread, it’s pervasive throughout the country, and it’s affecting families who have been here for a very long time, people who grew up here as children who are now parents,” Sorensen told Truthout.

author: Clare Hymer
title: New UK Sanctions on Israeli Groups Will Have No Material Impact, Critics Say
content:
Foreign secretary Ed Miliband has announced UK sanctions against Israeli firms involved in building illegal settlements in the West Bank, as well as an activist group that blocks aid from entering Gaza.


But the Israeli authorities driving settlement expansion and the denial of aid have not been targeted in the new measures, critics noted.


The

government said the measures

 against eight construction and property development firms would “disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support further construction in the West Bank”. 


It said that the Tsav 9 group, which has blocked aid crossings into Gaza and set trucks on fire, would also be subject to an asset freeze and ban on its members becoming directors of UK companies. 


Miliband said those who obstruct aid “must be prepared to face the consequences”.


But human rights groups said the sanctions were inadequate and did not target the primary cause of the violations: the Israeli government. 


“Sanctioning a handful of firms involved in illegal settlements is a fraction of what is needed – and targeting one activist group, rather than the Israeli authorities who continue to mastermind the denial of aid to Gaza, is not a serious response to a genocide,” said Kristyan Benedict, Amnesty International UK’s crisis response manager.


Benedict also noted that the

US already sanctioned Tsav 9 in June 2024, adding that the UK was just “playing catch-up”.

While the new measures were “a step in the right direction”, they fell “far short of the action international law demands”, he said.


“The UK must impose trade sanctions banning all services, investment and financial assistance linked to Israel’s unlawful occupation, impose targeted sanctions against Israeli officials most implicated in crimes against Palestinians – and ban, with immediate effect, all arms transfers to Israel.”


Huda Ammori, co-founder of banned direct action group Palestine Action, said Miliband was “sanctioning Israeli companies with little to no presence in Britain”, and so it would have “no material impact”. 


“He isn’t sanctioning JCB,

a British firm

 which destroys Palestinian homes and builds illegal settlements,

or Elbit [Systems]

, which makes weapons used to enforce the occupation,” she added.


Thomas Bell, acting UK director at Human Rights Watch, said: “The UK should take immediate steps to hold Israeli officials responsible for violations of international law by suspending arms transfers to Israel, suspending the UK-Israel Trade and Partnership Agreement,” and by supporting International Criminal Court cases against Israeli officials.   


The UK’s announcement comes just days before the deadline for tender for the construction of thousands of housing units in the E1 project, which threatens to cut East Jerusalem off from the rest of the West Bank and thereby make a contiguous Palestinian state impossible. 


Miliband said: “My message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.”

author: Alex Nguyen
title: Texas Attorney General Drops Lawsuit Aiming to Ban Muslim Civil Rights Group
content:
The Council on American-Islamic Relations, which has been targeted by Gov. Greg Abbott, called the news “a huge relief.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Attorney General Ken Paxton has dropped a lawsuit that sought to ban the country’s largest Muslim civil rights group from operating in Texas, state court records show.

The lawsuit, filed in February, had asked a Collin County judge to declare the Council on American-Islamic Relations a foreign terrorist and transnational criminal organization. It alleged that CAIR was working with the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Muslim group, to “usurp governmental power and establish dominion through Sharia law.” At the time, CAIR said it was being punished for its opposition to Israel’s war in Gaza.

The petition came after Gov. Greg Abbott slapped the same designation against the two groups and urged Paxton to take legal action against CAIR amid a surge in Republican candidates running anti-Islam campaigns.

Paxton’s office filed a notice of nonsuit Monday, voiding the lawsuit nearly two weeks after a blue wave sunk Paxton’s U.S. Senate bid and swept Abbott out of office. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she will remove the “foreign terrorist organization” label against CAIR.

Shaimaa Zayan, the Austin director of CAIR-Texas, called the lawsuit’s end — which was first reported by Bloomberg Law — a “huge relief.”

“CAIR-Texas faced a huge injustice and continued to operate despite the threats,” Zayan said Tuesday. “We are looking forward to a new chapter in Texas, hopefully where civic life will be flourishing and every voice will be heard in Texas.”

CAIR and its Texas chapter have also cheered Hinojosa’s pledge, which she announced during an interview with The Washington Post.

“Greg Abbott, Ken Paxton, Bo French, and Mayes Middleton staked their political campaigns on shredding the First Amendment to target Texas Muslims, but the people of Texas rejected this un-American bigotry,” the groups added in a statement. “Anti-Muslim hate is no longer an effective political weapon in Texas, and it must no longer have any place in state governance.”

The dropped lawsuit follows a flurry of other lawsuits Paxton’s office has abandoned since the election, including cases against immigrant rights groups as well as the NCAA over transgender athletes.

author: David Venn
title: RCMP conducts ‘largest drug seizure destined for Nunavut’
content:
In what the RCMP calls “the largest drug seizure destined for Nunavut,” police seized five kilograms of cocaine in southern Canada in August, a news release issued Tuesday says.


As a result, an estimated 50,000 doses (measuring one-tenth of a gram) were prevented from entering the territory, the release said.


“This seizure represents far more than the removal of drugs from the supply chain,” Chief Supt. Kent Pike said in the release. “It represents lives protected, families spared from harm and fewer opportunities for organized crime to profit at the expense of Nunavummiut.”


In February 2026, the police force began investigating an alleged money-laundering and drug-trafficking operation.


In August, officers from Nunavut and the federal Arctic unit executed a search warrant in Ottawa, where they seized the drugs.


The federal Arctic unit works under the Federal Policing Northwest Region, which co-ordinates resources to investigate organized crime in Alberta, Manitoba, the Northwest Territories, Saskatchewan and Nunavut.


The release did not say if any charges have been laid. It said the investigation is ongoing and that the RCMP will not provide further comment.

author: Daron Letts
title: Two children killed in sliding tragedy in Kimmirut
content:
Kimmirut is in mourning after two young sisters were killed while sliding Sunday afternoon.


Holly Lyta, 8, and Melanie Pootoogook, 5, were struck by a water truck as it was reversing, said Elisapie Pootoogook, the girls’ great aunt Tuesday in a phone interview.


Their father Charlie Pootoogook witnessed the incident, she said.


“I’m having trouble sleeping,” Elisapie Pootoogook said of how she’s handling the tragedy.

She added that she is very close to her nephew Charlie Pootoogook, who grew up with her in Kinngait.


The girls’ grandparents are planning to head to Kimmirut Friday from Kinngait to support the parents, Elisapie Pootoogook said.


Kimmirut has a population of approximately 400 people.


The community’s school and daycare were closed Monday out of respect for those affected by the girls’ deaths.


South Baffin MLA David Joanasie, whose riding includes Kimmirut and Kinngait, shared his support for the family Monday in a Facebook post.


“My sincere condolences [go] out to the people of Kimmirut during this difficult time of grief after a sudden tragedy,” he said.

“We feel for all those who are most impacted by their loss and hope that love and grace surrounds the families and community as a whole. I thank all the responders who help during this hardship.”


The Education Department, in partnership with the Canadian Red Cross, will provide supports,

 he added.


Elisapie Pootoogook and others in the community are holding various fundraisers for the family.


“Donations to the family are also welcome,” she said. “No family should ever have to experience such heartbreaking loss.”


The RCMP did not respond to an interview request as of noon on Tuesday.

author: Chris Walker
title: Largest Data Centers in US Emit as Much Carbon as Denmark, Study Finds
content:
The largest US data centers use almost 2 percent of US electricity, more than New York City and Los Angeles combined.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A new study published this week suggests that the combined yearly output of carbon dioxide from the largest data centers in the U.S. rivals that of some countries.

The study, which appeared in the journal Nature Sustainability on Monday, finds that the largest data centers in the country release a combined total of 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year. That accounts for about 2 percent of all electricity use in the U.S. — an amount that is greater than the yearly electricity use of Los Angeles and New York City combined.

The study examined 403 facilities in total, finding that their combined carbon emissions were comparable to those of countries the size of Bolivia or Denmark.

Some states’ data centers had larger carbon outputs than others. Virginia, Iowa, and Ohio account for half of emissions alone, while other states, such as Oregon, have much smaller carbon emissions, due to a larger portion of electricity being generated through means other than fossil fuels.

According to reporting from The New York Times, much of the researchers’ work amounted to “detective work” due to the lack of federal requirements on public disclosure by these facilities.

“Communities shouldn’t need a team of Harvard researchers to analyze satellite images to understand their environmental impact,” said Gianluca Guidi, the Harvard scientist who led the research team.

Indeed, safeguards against pollution from data centers are limited, in large part due to workarounds that are being allowed by the Trump administration’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), including the use of “islanded” power plants, which are built solely to power data centers and are not part of the electrical grid.

Data centers are also undoing recent progress in reducing pollution in states with larger carbon emissions. In Texas, for example, years of work to lower those rates could be undone if a plan to build hundreds of new data centers (in addition to those that have already been constructed) goes through in the next few years.

Americans appear aware of the problems posed by data centers, including rising electricity prices and environmental concerns. Earlier this month, in midterm elections across the country, voters overwhelmingly passed referenda to bar or regulate the rapid expansion of data centers in their communities.

“Tuesday’s election was a historically bad night for the Republican Party. It might have been even worse for big tech and their plans to spend trillions of dollars building AI data centers,” read one analysis of the election outcomes.

Public opposition to data center expansion likely played a role in Democrats’ “blue wave.” Exit poll data from NBC News found that 56 percent of voters described data centers and artificial intelligence (AI) as “crucial or major factor[s]” in determining their vote.

author: Sarah van Gelder
title: Democrats Face First Test Post-Midterms: Fund or Oppose Forever Wars?
content:
The Democrats should use their midterm momentum to stop writing a blank check for the Pentagon.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The historic Democratic Party midterm victories were fueled in large part by deep opposition to the war on Iran, according to polling. Every Democrat who won in a competitive congressional race, except for one, opposed the war, including 13 in the Senate and 48 in the House, according to post-election analysis by the Progressive Change Institute.

New members won’t take office until January 3, when control of both houses shifts to Democrats. But the first test of whether Democrats in Congress will heed voters’ mandate for the end of the war on Iran, and respond to widespread opposition to “forever wars” more broadly, could occur much sooner. Although Democrats remain in the minority until January, they still have powerful leverage to block excessive Pentagon funding and stop the war in Iran during the current lame-duck session.

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is key. The bill authorizes $1.15 trillion in military spending — along with dangerous policies to move toward integration of U.S. and Israeli military technology development, to build a destabilizing new generation of nuclear weapons, and to accelerate deployment of AI in weaponry.

The Trump administration is requesting an additional $350 billion just for the Iran War, bringing the total spending to a breathtaking $1.5 trillion dollars.

But Congress could just say no. The message delivered by the midterm elections could finally flip the script on the conventional wisdom that Congress will grant any level of Pentagon funding in the name of national security. Democrats must use their midterm momentum to stop destabilizing policies and sky-high defense spending, and finally take a stand for spending that meets the needs of families and communities.

The 2027 NDAA was passed by the House in July. But in the Senate, 60 votes are required to allow a measure to come to the floor for a vote, and Senate Democrats were able to stop the bill from progressing. They can do that again, with or without Republican support, and the midterm election results make clear that is what voters want them to do.

Opposing the massive increase in military spending and the war in Iran should be an easy call — especially at a time when so many Americans are struggling to get the food, housing, medical care, and education they need. But giant defense corporations invest heavily in lobbying to influence defense policy, with nearly $164 million spent on lobbying in just the first three quarters of 2026, according to OpenSecrets. Defense expenditures are distributed nationwide, so members of Congress are often reluctant to reduce budgets that could impact their districts. Funding the Pentagon is also conflated with support for U.S. service members and considered a signal of patriotism. It is time to put that falsehood to rest.

Neither the NDAA nor the Pentagon appropriations bill is truly a must-pass measure. The two bills serve different purposes: the NDAA authorizes military programs and establishes defense policies, while the appropriations bill actually provides the money to fund them. If an appropriation bill doesn’t pass, Congress can keep the Pentagon operating through a continuing resolution. And the programs and policies included in the NDAA do not have to be bundled into one massive annual bill; Congress can address them through separate legislation.

If either bill stalls, the incoming Congress, with its new Democratic majorities, could write new versions after members take office in January 2027. They could use these bills to end the war in Iran, to halt destructive new nuclear weapons development, to stop military technology integration with Israel, and to force a reduction in Pentagon spending.

Congress could redirect our taxpayer dollars toward unmet needs of families and communities, beginning by reversing cuts to Medicaid funding scheduled to take effect in the new year.

Only Congress has the Constitutional power to determine federal government funding, and it should use that power. Here are seven things it could do instead of rubber-stamping the Pentagon’s requests:

End the deeply unpopular war in Iran. The Iran war was a “crucial” or a “major factor” for 74 percent of voters, according to an NBC exit poll …
